Total: 2 
 
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of those 
recommendations/observations which have been categorized as interim replies by the 
Committee should be furnished at the earliest.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

2 
 
 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
MINISTRY 
 
LACK OF CONNECTIVITY 
 
a) Road 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee, therefore, recommends that roads connecting the sites in the Circuits 
must be improved. The Ministry of Tourism, along with the States concerned and the Ministry of 
Road Transport and Highways, must come together to ensure the completion of pending projects 
and develop new projects to connect these places. Moreover, the existing roads must be made 
into four-lane roads and traffic congestion must be checked and resolved. The Committee also 
recommends that existing roads must be maintained to m eet international standards. Roads must 
also be kept litter -free and must be cleaned regularly. Unnecessary speed breakers must be 
removed and roads must be tarmacked. 
(Para 8) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1. Recommendation of Committee has been noted for compliance. Ministry of Tourism has 
identified Buddhist Circuit as one of the priority areas for development. The Ministry is working 
on improving connectivity and overall travel experience for the visitors in  the circuit and has 
taken up the issue with concerned line Ministries. 
 
1.2. For improvin g the road connectivity in the C ircuit, t he Ministry has taken up the issue 
with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, who has informed that work on four -laning 
of National Highways in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar is in process and is expected to be complete by 
June 2019.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
1.3. The Committee notes the reply. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2.  The Committee recommends that a Committee or Panel should be instituted, which would 
include the State Governments concerned, Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, NHAI, 
Ministry of Tourism and any other stakeholders, to ensure the construction and mainte nance of 
roads connecting the various sites under the Buddhist Circuit. 
(Para 10) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1. Recommendation of Committee has been noted.  However, construction and maintenance 
of National Highway/ State Highway is the responsibility of conc erned Government in whose 
jurisdiction it falls. The Ministry of Tourism, only takes up the issues with the concerned 
Ministry/ Government for action.  
 

3 
 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
2.2. The Committee notes the reply.  The Committee impresses upon the Ministry to 
pursue, from time to time,  the issue of construction and maintenance of roads/highways 
connecting the various sites under the Buddhist Circuit, with the concerned 
Ministry/Government for timely action. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3.  The Committee notes that the Circuit does not suffer from lack of funds. However, 
execution of existing projects leaves much to be desired. The Committee, therefore, recommends 
that a timeline be fixed for each project undertaken for construction and perio dic reports be 
submitted on the same, to ensure their timely completion.  
(Para 11) 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1. Recommendation of Committee has been noted. The projects sanctioned by the Ministry 
under Buddhist Circuit are with specific timelines and Minist ry carries out regular monitoring of 
the projects for its timely implementation.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
3.2. The Committee notes the reply.   
 
b) Rail 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee further recommends that a special tourist ticket, with additional services 
on specific scheduled trains and key routes (for instance, New Delhi- Gaya, with possible stops in 
Varanasi, Sarnath, Nalanda, Rajgir) would be useful. This could be accompanied by facilities 
such as tourist -assigned ticketing up to 24 hours in advance of departures, discounts on select 
accommodation etc. Circuit specific trains like the Shramjevi Express and the Buddhapurnima 
Express are good possibilities for such a scheme. The Committee further recommends that luxury 
trains such as 'Palace on Wheels' or even hop- on- hop-off trains connecting feasible sites may be 
introduced. The feasibility of a fully AC/superfast train connecting important Buddhist sites to 
metros should be explored. The conditions of Gaya and Cantonment Railwa ys station must also 
be improved upon.  
(Para 20) 
Reply of the Ministry 
4.1. Since the matter pertains to Railways Board, Ministry has forwarded the recommendation 
to the Board for their comments. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
4.2. The Committee notes the reply.  However, the Committee desires to be apprised of 
the comments offered by the Railway Board. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
5. In this regard, the Committee observes that the full potential of the Buddhist Circuit is yet  
 
to be exploited by the stakeholders. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of 

4 
 
 
Tourism must pursue the development of  the Buddhist Circuit with a renewed vigor and zeal. 
(Para 28) 
Reply of the Ministry 
5.1. The Ministry has noted the recommendation for compliance. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
5.2. The Committee notes the reply. 
 
INSUFFICIENT OUTREACH AND PUBLICITY OF THE BUDDHIST CIRCUIT 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
6. The Committee feels that the integrated Buddhist Circuit has no formal brand identity and 
is portrayed and packaged in a fragmented and inconsistent manner. Despite the unique status of 
the Circuit and the enormous international market -size of Buddhist travelers, proactive and 
coordinated destination marketing effo rts are limited and the Circuit is primarily promoted by 
individual operators and religious bodies. Also, there is limited online marketing. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that there should be a pan India sub -brand for Buddhist 
tourism, which would b e recognized the world over. Also, the Committee strongly feels the need 
to reclaim the legacy of Buddha which many countries are now claiming for themselves. 
(Para 46) 
Reply of the Ministry 
6.1. Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, undertakes several  promotional activities in 
the domestic and international markets for promotion of the varied tourism products and 
destinations of the country including Buddhist Heritage, Sites and Circuits. The Ministry 
produces publicity material and collaterals in Engl ish and foreign languages for domestic and 
international markets; media campaigns in the print and electronic media are undertaken in the 
domestic and international markets; familiarisation tours for trade, media and opinion makers are 
undertaken from over seas to Buddhist Sites and Circuits in the country under the Hospitality 
Scheme of the Ministry. 
 
6.2. Ministry of Tourism has produced two films on promotion of Buddhist Tourism, (1) India 
– The Land of Buddha by CNN    and (2) Following the path of the Bu ddha by TABI Channel 
Japan. 
 
6.3. Both the films have been promoted on electronic and digital media.   India –The Land of 
Buddha film was launched by the Hon‟ble President on World Tourism Day (27th  September 
2018), the film is based on the legacy of Buddha  and it enforces the very idea of India being land 
of Buddha. 
 
6.4. On social media, this film was well received, reaching millions of views in two weeks‟ 
time. In the Incredible India 2.0 campaign, market specific creatives are being used.  Creatives on 
promotion of Buddhist sites are being used in the Buddhist dominating markets, such as China, 
Japan, Korea, etc. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
6.5. The Committee notes the reply and impresses upon the Ministry to put in more 

5 
 
 
efforts for promotion of Buddhist legacy in both national and international Buddhist 
markets, to give a fillip to Buddhist tourism in the country. 
 
6.6. The Committee feels that the Ministry should take up promotion of Buddhist legacy 
to remote areas of the country where digital m eans are very limited.  The Ministry of 
Tourism in collaboration with Ministry of Culture, should promote activities like 
plays/dramas in remote areas of the country.  Various promotional products like books/T -
Shirts/paintings relating to Buddhism should b e launched by the Ministry in the markets 
near the places of Buddhist Circuit.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
7. The Committee further recommends that there should be a single website for Buddhist 
tourism for all the States, something along the lines of a on e- stop solution for all matters and 
information related to Buddhist Circuit which will cater to the needs of a tourist. This site can be 
linked to other sites for related Government agencies etc. 
(Para 47) 
Reply of the Ministry 
7.1. The Ministry of Tourism has developed a dedicated website “indiathelandofbuddha.in”. 
This website was launched in July, 2018 during the International Buddhist Conclave. This site 
has comprehensive information covering not only the sites visited by Buddha but also Buddhist  
Heritage which were developed by Buddhist Disciples and Buddhist Monasteries which are  
popular among Buddhist travelers/seekers . This website is linked to incredibleindia.org, the 
primary website of Ministry of Tourism. The suggestion of the Hon‟ble Committee with regard to 
linking the site with other Government agencies is well taken for implementation. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
7.2. The Committee notes the reply. 
 
7.3. In this electronic era, the Committee feels that a mobile App should be launched 
which will prove very handy and attractive for tourists.  It should be designed in a way so 
that these places are covered under Swadesh Darshan Scheme, Heritage sites and plac es of 
archaeological importance.  Various offers should be launched for probable tourists while 
booking tours to such places from the App itself.  It will not only promote the tourism 
industry in a big way but will also give a major boost to digitalization.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
8. The Committee believes that there is a need to promote the Circuit in a sect -specific 
manner. This will help to promote other States with Buddhist heritages and the Circuit will not 
find itself confined to Gaya and Bodh Ga ya. This will also go a long way towards solving the 
problem of seasonality that ails the Circuit, since other places do not suffer from extremes of 
temperature especially the summer heat, like in Northern India. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that efforts must be made to promote sites specific to the individual sects. The sites 
may be marketed according to the sects.  
(Para 48) 
Reply of the Ministry 
8.1. The above recommendation has been noted.  

6 
 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
8.2. The Committee notes the reply and seeks to be apprised of the steps taken by the 
Ministry in the said direction. 
Recommendation/Observation 
9.  Moreover, destinations along the Buddhist Circuit need to be transformed into learning -
contact points, which in turn will stim ulate demand, promote longer stays and generate a desire 
to visit other sites and lead to growth in goods and service providers. 
(Para 49) 
Reply of the Ministry 
9.1.  The above recommendation has been noted. 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
9.2. The Committee expects the Ministry to apprise it of the steps taken by the Ministry 
to transform Buddhist sites into Centres of Learning. 
 
 
PROTECTION OF MONUMENTS AND PRESERVATION OF ARTEFACTS 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
10. The Buddhist Circuit would be incomplete without giving the credit where due. The John 
Marshall Museum, apart from preserving the history of the discovery of Buddhist artefacts in 
India, would also serve as a major attraction for tourists, both domestic and international, 
academicians and researchers alike. The Committee, therefore, recommends that though the 
development of the University and the Museum in Kapilavastu is not under its purview, it may 
coordinate with the Ministry of Culture, the respective State Government and its agencies and the 
ASI, to pursue the development of the proposed John Marshall Museum. 
(Para 58) 
Reply of the Ministry 
10.1. The recommendation is noted for compliance. The Ministry regularly interacts with ASI 
for better convergence and smooth execution of projects in and around premises under the 
purview of ASI. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
10.2. The Committee notes the reply.

sites would become more attractive and popular among the visiting tourists.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation

biodiversity, rich culture and heritage, the tourism sector has not grown to the desired level

and have helped to increase the popularity of various tourist spots, the Committee had 
recommended its replication across the country so that t he country‟s huge, but barely 
tapped, potential could be realized.  Since the Ministry of Tourism is responsible for the

REPORT
The Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and
Culture deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Culture on the Recommendations/Observations as
contained in its Two Hundred and Seventy First Report on ‘Fellowships, Scholarships, Grants, Pensions
and Schemes administered by the Ministry of Culture’ which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament
on 21
st December, 2018.
2. The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 15 th October, 2019 in respect of all the
Recommendations/Observations contained in the 271st Report. The replies have been categorized as follows:—
Chapter I: Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Ministry:
Paragraph Nos.:   22, 32, 36, 38, 39, 45, 50, 51.
TOTAL:   8
Chapter II: Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the
replies of the Ministry:
Paragraph Nos.:   8, 18, 30, 42, 48, 49, 56.
TOTAL:   7
Chapter III: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have not been
accepted by the Committee:
Paragraph Nos.:   14, 15, 17, 21, 26, 27, 28, 29, 34, 46, 52, 53.
TOTAL:   12
Chapter IV: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the final replies of the Ministry are still
awaited:
Paragraph Nos.:   9, 16, 54.
T
OTAL:   3
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of those Recommendations/Observations which
have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the earliest.

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY
TRANSPARENCY IN THE ALLOCATION OF FUNDS
Recommendation/Observation
1. The works of the artistes and organizations, wherever possible, should be uploaded on the website of
the Ministry of Culture. This will make the public aware of the cultural activities being performed by the
artistes / organizations and display the richness of our cultures. Also, digitizing the works would preserve
these for the future. (Para 22)
Reply of the Ministry
1.1 Media Cell of Ministry of Culture is entrusted with the task of uploading all such relevant material on
various social media handles like Twitter, Youtube, Instagram and Facebook.  Further, the relevant information
is made available to the public through ‘Sanskriti App’ managed by the Media Cell and the official website of
the Ministry managed by NIC.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
1.2 The Committee notes the reply.
PROPER UTILISATION OF FUNDS
Recommendation/Observation
2. The Committee feels that such a central database would also aid in ensuring proper utilization of
allocated funds and keep a check on frauds. In pursuance of the same, the Committee recommends that the
work on the central database should be expedited and that it should include information on the beneficiaries
of all Schemes along with the records of their work. A system should then be put in place which makes use
of this data and checks for any redundancies to ensure that an artiste/organization does not get benefits
under multiple Schemes. Rules should be framed to restrict the award of Grants to a beneficiary, say, only
under one Scheme at a time, or only a certain number of times in their lifetime. This will ensure that the
reach of the funds is maximized over time. (Para 32)
Reply of the Ministry
2.1 Noted for further action.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
2.2 The Committee may be apprised of the progress being made in this regard.
NEED FOR MORE BENEFICIARIES OF FELLOWSHIPS AND SCHEMES
Recommendation/Observation
3. The Committee strongly feels that these figures are not satisfactory keeping in mind the vast and
varied artistic community in our country. Many deserving artistes are not getting the benefits of these
schemes. Therefore, the Committee recommends that effective measures may be taken by the Ministry of
2

3
Culture to increase the number of artistes and organizations supported by its Schemes. The Ministry should
explore the option of lowering the eligibility criteria for Schemes that are not garnering enough response
from the artistes so that besides seasoned artistes, upcoming artistes also get adequate support from the
Ministry. (Para 36)
Reply of the Ministry
3.1 Noted for further action. Time to time, spaces on Media regarding the benefits to the old artists
through the Scheme of Artistes Pension and Medical Aid to Artistes will be considered, specially in local
media as maximum numbers of artistes applying for the Scheme are from rural and interior areas. The
information regarding artistes pension is spreading through the existing beneficiaries of respective States
also.
3.2 As regards the schemes of Award of Senior / Junior Fellowships to Outstanding Artistes in the Field of
Culture and Award of Scholarships to Young Artistes in Different Cultural Fields, it is informed that the
response in both the schemes is satisfactory and the number of applications received for both the schemes
is almost 8 to 10 times of the total number of Fellowships / Scholarships granted under the scheme.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
3.3 The Committee notes the reply.
ANNUAL REVIEW OF PRESENT SCHEMES
Recommendation/Observation
4. The Committee is of the considered view that annual review of the Schemes can help arrive at conclusions
regarding the possible future course of action for the Schemes. This becomes all the more important given
the fact that the Ministry of Culture is short on funds and therefore, only Schemes having the desired impact
at ground level should be continued.    (Para 38)
Reply of the Ministry
4.1 A Third-Party review of the schemes concerning this Ministry was carried out while considering the
continuation of these schemes till FY 2019-20.  These schemes are due for further review for their continuation
beyond March 2020.  The recommendation of the committee shall be duly kept in mind while conducting
the review exercise.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
4.2 The Committee appreciates the periodic reviews of the Schemes being conducted by the Ministry
of Culture as the same will lead to meaningful insights about the schemes presently in operation.
The Committee may be informed of the outcome of the review of the Schemes carried out / planned
to be carried out.
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should conduct annual review of the performance and
achievements of its Schemes. The feedback received on the existing Schemes should be analyzed to update/
modify the Schemes at regular intervals to maximize their impact and to explore the possibility of the

4
initiation of new Schemes which could help the Ministry to reach out to more deserving artistes and
organizations. The outcome of such review should be made public so as to allow constructive criticism and
collect feedback thereon which can then be reflected in streamlining the Schemes further. (Para 39)
Reply of the Ministry
5.1 Noted for further action. A mechanism for analyzing the on-ground performance of various schemes
is already in existence so as to judge the outcome of these schemes. The same is ensured through random
physical inspection carried out through the officials of the Ministry and its various attached/subordinate/
autonomous offices and organizations.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
5.2 The Committee notes the reply.
COMPLAINT REDRESSAL MECHANISM REGARDING GRANTS AND FELLOWSHIPS
Recommendation/Observation
6. The Committee recommends that the details on the procedure to be followed in order to register a
complaint regarding the Schemes of the Ministry should be available and prominently visible on the Schemes
section of the website of the Ministry. Name, designation and contact details of the officer in charge of
handling such complaints should also be made available. The progress of the action taken to address such
complaints should also be uploaded on the website. Wherever possible, the list of complaints received should
be available publicly in order to ensure transparency.    (Para 45)
Reply of the Ministry
6.1 Noted for further action.  However, there exists a specific portal (CPGRAMS) developed by the
Government for redressal of individual grievances relating to any subject concerning this Ministry including
schemes.
6.2 All complaints are attended on priority basis as and when received. The immediate replies/clarifications
are sent by e-mail, speed post to the complainant.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
6.3 The Committee notes the reply.
SCHEME SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATIONS
Recommendation/Observation
7. The Committee recommends that the eligibility criteria for availing the Scheme for Pension and
Medical Aid to Artistes should be revised periodically, keeping in mind the rising cost of living. Similarly,
the amount paid to the artistes also be revised periodically. (Para 50)
Reply of the Ministry
7.1 Eligibility criteria for availing the pension to artists are reviewed and revised periodically. The latest
guidelines in this regard have been revised in 2017-18. The reply of para 49 is also applicable for this specific
recommendation.

5
Further Recommendation/Observation:
7.2 The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
8. The Committee recommends that the artistes/fellows eligible for the medical aid should be covered
under some medical insurance Scheme with broad coverage like CGHS/ESI.  (Para 51)
Reply of the Ministry
8.1 The matter is related to policy and will be taken into consideration at the time of reviewing the scheme
in future.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
8.2 The Committee notes the reply.

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH THE
COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE
REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY
SAFEGUARDS IN THE SELECTION PROCESS OF BENEFICIARIES OF V ARIOUS SCHEMES
Recommendation/Observation
1. The Committee recommends that in order to ensure that the funds are being utilized for the intended
activities, the progress of activities performed by the beneficiaries should be monitored closely and at
frequent intervals. Digital records of the activities performed by the beneficiaries may be kept wherever
possible, in the form of photographs, video etc. (Para 8)
Reply of the Ministry
1.1 The monitoring mechanism in respect of all the schemes being handled in this Ministry is provided in
the Scheme guidelines.  The individuals/organizations applying under the schemes are, inter-alia, required
to provide proofs of activities being performed by them in their area of expertise which is examined by the
Expert Committee constituted for selecting beneficiaries.  Similarly, these individuals/organizations are required
to provide Utilization certificate, photographs, videos, upload their activities on Youtube etc. for release of
subsequent grants by the Ministry of Culture.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
1.2 The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the required proof of activities performed by
the beneficiaries uploaded on Youtube etc., are being thoroughly verified for their authenticity. The
Committee desires that the Ministry may assess the efficacy of the existing monitoring mechanism
and take corrective action from time to time based on the findings.
SENSITIZING THE STATE GOVERNMENTS TO ENCOURAGE MORE APPLICATIONS FOR THE
SCHEMES
Recommendation/Observation
2. The Committee recommends that the importance of preserving and celebrating our different cultures
should be communicated to the State Governments. The Ministry of Culture may drive home to the State
Governments, the positive impact of the richness of a culture on the tourism prospects of a State. A detailed
plan should be evolved in order to encourage better participation of the State Governments. Incentivizing
the State Governments having good participation by highlighting the work of the artistes from such states
on the Ministry’s website, should be considered and implemented suitably. (Para 18)
Reply of the Ministry
2.1 Noted for further action. However, so as to protect, preserve and promote various forms of art and
cultural heritage in the country, Government has set up 07 Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) with headquarters
at Patiala, Allahabad, Nagpur, Udaipur, Kolkata, Dimapur and Thanjavur. All the States of the country are the
participating States of 01 or more of these ZCCs, which organize various cultural activities and programmes
throughout the country with participation of artistes from all over the country.
6

7
Further Recommendation/Observation:
2.2 The Committee notes the reply.
PROPER UTILISATION OF FUNDS
Recommendation/Observation
3. The Committee is of the view that a practical and effective monitoring mechanism lies at the core of
ensuring the proper utilization of funds for any Scheme. Such a mechanism should be framed with inputs
from the artistes and beneficiaries so as to keep a check on fraudulent claims, while minimizing the trouble
caused to the beneficiaries in complying with the monitoring mechanism. (Para 30)
Reply of the Ministry
3.1 The beneficiary organizations are required to submit Utilization Certificate, Newspaper cuttings, proof
of conduct of function etc. before further release of grant to them.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
3.2 The Committee notes the reply.
EASE OF PROCESS OF APPLICATION
Recommendation/Observation
4. The Committee strongly feels that no eligible artist should be left out of availing financial assistance
because of their lack of understanding of the intricacies involved in the process. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that necessary assistance should be readily available to artistes and organizations. Contact
details of officials to be contacted in case of queries should be provided in the Schemes section of the
website of the Ministry and in the advertisements published for creating awareness about the Schemes. The
Committee desires that the Ministry should ensure that no application is rejected for trivial reasons and that
rejected applications should provide specific reasons for the rejection, so that deserving candidates can re-
apply if they fulfil the criteria, but were left out, because of ignorance of the relevant rule. (Para 42)
Reply of the Ministry
4.1 It has been the constant endeavor of this Ministry to ensure that no deserving candidate is denied an
opportunity for trivial reasons. For this purpose, contact numbers of the concerned officials of this Ministry
are made available on the official website and at the time of issuance of advertisement. All necessary support
and guidance is provided to the applicants, online as well as offline.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
4.2 The Committee notes the reply.
TAKING SUO MOTO COGNIZANCE IN EXTRAORDINARY CASES
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee feels that this is not an isolated case since such news keep appearing in the media from
time-to-time. This points to the poor living conditions faced by a vast section of the artistes community in

8
our country once they reach old age and to the fact that the Ministry’s pension scheme is not reaching the
intended recipients. (Para 48)
Reply of the Ministry
5.1 Time to time, spaces on Media regarding the benefits to the old artists through the Scheme of Artistes
Pension and Medical Aid to Artistes may be considered specially on local media as maximum numbers of
artistes applying for the Scheme are from rural and interior areas. The information regarding artistes pension
are spreading through the existing beneficiaries of respective States also.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
5.2 The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
6. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should be proactive and suo motu extend its Artistes
Pension Scheme whenever a case comes to the light, where an artist with significant contribution to our
cultural heritage is found to be living in penury. The reasons for which such deserving artistes got left out
in the first place should be looked into by the Ministry and the Artistes pension Scheme should be updated
accordingly to ensure a dignified life to all deserving artistes. If need be, the Ministry should allocate
more funds to this Scheme since financial assistance is direly needed by artistes in the later stage of their
life. (Para 49)
Reply of the Ministry
6.1 The guidelines and terms and conditions of the Artistes Pension Scheme are being reviewed time to
time to ensure dignified life to all deserving artistes. The updated Scheme guidelines are already available in
our website along with other relevant information for getting artistes pension. The matter of allocation of
more funds to this scheme will be decided as and when required.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
6.2 The Committee notes the reply.
GENERAL RECOMMENDATION
Recommendation/Observation
7. In this regard, the Committee would like to point out the need to have Zonal Cultural Centres in
Punjab and Haryana and the need to give more attention to the Central Schemes of financial assistance to
artistes. The Committee suggests that theatre culture may be developed in the country so as to provide a
platform for recognition of small artistes and artisans. (Para 56)
Reply of the Ministry
7.1 The Mandate of Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) is to promote and preserve folk & tribal art of the
country. North Zone Cultural Centre (NZCC), established by the Government of India in Patiala is already
catering to the needs of the artistes of the States of Punjab and Haryana. Further, it may also be mentioned
that National School of Drama (NSD), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture is actively working
in the field of development and preservation of culture.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
7.2 The Committee notes the reply.

CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH
REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY HA VE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED
BY THE COMMITTEE
EQUITABLE REPRESENTATION OF CULTURES FROM ALL STATES IN V ARIOUS SCHEMES OF
THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
1. The Committee notes that effective steps must be taken in order to ensure uniform representation of the
whole country. India is an amalgamation of many distinct cultures and the allocation of the majority of the
Grants of the Ministry to artistes and organisations of only a few States goes against the spirit of such
Schemes wherein funds are allocated in the first place. The culture of each State is equally important and
this should reflect in the efforts that must be put in to ensure their conservation. (Para 14)
Reply of the Ministry
1.1 The Ministry has no state specific scheme, however, schemes being implemented in the Ministry are
open to citizens from all the States of the country. It may also be stated that the response to the schemes is
over whelming from all the states.  All efforts are made and will continue to be made in order to accord wide
publicity to the schemes in all the States to ensure equal and further better representation.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
1.2 The Committee reiterates its recommendation that some mechanism should be there in place
to ensure a certain minimum representation of artists and organisations from all States in the
schemes of the Ministry. An upper limit for representation from an individual State may also be set
after analyzing the statistics of representation from an individual in the various schemes, while
factoring in the population and size of the States in deciding upon such limit.
Recommendation/Observation
2. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Culture should ensure equitable allocation of funds
to States for Grants, Fellowships, Pensions and Schemes. In case of lack of adequate representation of
artistes / organizations from a State in a particular year, the reasons behind the lack of representation should
be looked into and necessary remedial action may be taken without delay. (Para 15)
Reply of the Ministry
2.1 The schemes being handled in the Ministry are Central Sector Schemes and no grant is therefore,
directly provided to the States.
Further Recommendation/Observation:
2.2 India has a vast pool of artistes and their organizations. The Committee, in para 15 of its 271
st
Report, sought selection of artistes under the Scheme for Grants, Fellowships and Pensions to
ensure that the interests of artistes from all the States are duly protected and there is no room for
a few States-centric selection of artistes and in that way, vast cultural ethos of the country can be
propagated and preserved effectively. The Committee would like to reiterate its recommendation
made in this regard.
9

10
SENSITIZING THE STATE GOVERNMENTS TO ENCOURAGE MORE APPLICATIONS FOR THE
SCHEMES
Recommendation/Observation
3. The Committee could understand that the biggest reason for the lack of representation of the vast
majority of States in the various Schemes of the Ministry is the inaction and indifference shown by the State
Governments. The Committee strongly feels that deserving artistes and beneficiaries should not suffer for
no fault of theirs. The Committee, therefore, urges the Ministry of Culture to impress upon the State Governments
to show more interest in getting the artistes their due benefits. The Committee is working towards facilitating
greater cooperation between the Ministry of Culture and State Governments. Improvement in Centre-State
and intra-State dialogue will ensure the performance of State Governments through shared learnings and
collaborations for overcoming challenges. (Para 17)
Reply of the Ministry
3.1 The schemes being handled in this Ministry are Central Sector Schemes and no grant is, therefore,
provided directly to the States,
Further Recommendation/Observation:
3.2 The Committee is aware that the Culture Departments of State Governments accord priorities
to other sectors, as a result of which various dimensions of Arts and Culture get totally neglected.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that to help more and more artistes in the fields of Music,
Drama, Dance, etc., the Ministry should devise a robust Centrally Sponsored Scheme which would
give a little flexibility to the States in terms of extending financial assistance to deserving artistes.
The Committee feels that the Scheme may be executed through the State machinery.
TRANSPARENCY IN THE ALLOCATION OF FUNDS
Recommendation/Observation

Ministry of Culture shows that the total funds allocated to various schemes of the Ministry has increased
from

of about 35%. Yet, the amount allocated to the “Scheme for Safeguarding the Intangible Cultural Heritage
and Diverse Cultural Traditions of India” remains stagnant at ` 3.50 crores and has not seen a commensurate
increase. Moreover , even out of the paltry ` 3.50 crores allocated to this Scheme, the Ministry was able to

Intangible Cultural Heritage of India.

scrutinize/ screen the proposals/ applications. However, the tenure of the Expert Committee was constituted

5.3 However, now the Expert Committee has been reconstituted and it is expected that the scheme would
now be implemented more smoothly.
Further Recommendation/Observation:

be allowed to be non-functional for such a long period. The Committee feels that since the tenure of
the EC is known beforehand, the requisite actions to reconstitute the EC should have been set in

reasons for the undue delay in reconstitution of the Expert Committee. The Committee may also

I Brief Background 
 The tourism sector has huge potential as an instrument for economic 
development.  Tourism is also an important source of foreign exchange earnings.  Not 
only does the tourism sector spearhead growth, it also improves the quality of people‟s 
lives with its capacity to create large -scale employment of diverse kind.  It also 
supports environmental protection and champions diverse cultural heritage.  
2.  Ministry of Tourism is the nodal agency to formulate national  policies  and  
programmes for the development an d promotion of tourism. In the process, the 
Ministry consults and collaborates with other stakeholders in the sector including 
various Central Ministries/ Agencies, State Governments/ Union Territory 
Administrations and the representatives of the private sector. 
3. Secretary (Tourism) is the executive chief of the Ministry. The Directorate 
General of Tourism has 20 Domestic field offices and an Indian Institute of Skiing and 
Mountaineering within the country and 08 overseas offices. The overseas offices 
promote Indian tourism in the markets abroad. 
4. The domestic field offices also play a vital role for promotion of tourism sector 
in the country. They are also involved in monitoring the progress of implementation of 
projects sanctioned by the Ministry to the Stat e Governments/Union Territories. India 
Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) is the only public sector undertaking under 
the charge of the Ministry of Tourism.  
5. The Ministry also has the following autonomous institutions: 
(i) Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management (IITTM). 
(ii) National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology 
(NCHMCT); and the Institutes of Hotel Management (IHMs). 
(iii) Indian Culinary Institute (ICI).

22. The NITI Aayog Report titled Strategy for New India @75 in its chapter on Travel 
Tourism & Hospitality lists increase of Foreign Tourist Arrival from 8.8 million to 12 
million as one of the objectives for the tourism sector. The Ministry has taken several 
steps for achieving the above objective details of which are: 
 
i. Launched the Swadesh Darshan Scheme with a vision to develop theme based 
tourist circuits. 
ii. Launched the National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, 
Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) Scheme for holistic development 
of identified pilgrimage destinations. 
iii. Identified 17 Iconic Sites in the country for development by seeking 
convergence with other Central Ministries/Departments/State Governments 
/Urban Local Bodies  

 
 
12 
 
iv. Launched the Adopt a Heritage Project for development and maintenance of 
tourist amenities at heritage sites/monuments and other tourist sites. 
v. Development and promotion of „Niche Tourism‟ products to attract tourist with 
specific interest and to ensure repeat visits for the unique products in which 
India has a comparative advantage. 
vi. Launched 24x7 toll free Multi-Lingual Tourist Helpline. 
vii. Promoting India as a holistic tourism destination including its various tourism 
sites and products through Incredible India 2.0 Campaign. 
viii. Providing facility of e-Visa for 5 sub-categories i.e. e-Tourist visa, e-Business 
visa, e-Medical visa, e-Medical Attendant visa and e-Conference visa for 
nationals of 170 countries. 
ix. E-Visa has been further liberalized and the visa fee has been substantially 
reduced. 
x. Revamp of Incredible India Website having information on tourism 
sites/destinations in different States/Union Territory Administrations. 
xi. Launched Buddhist website – India the land of buddha.in to promote and 
showcase the rich Buddhist Heritage in India. 
xii. Launched Incredible India Tourist Facilitator Programme on an online digital 
platform to provide basic, advanced and refresher courses for tourist 
facilitators. 
xiii. New mountain peaks have been opened for Mountaineering/Trekking to give 
boost to adventure tourism in the country. 
xiv. Lowering of GST on hotels rooms with tariffs of Rs. 1,001 to Rs. 7,500/night 
to 12% and for Rs. 7,501 & above to 18% to increase India‟s competitiveness 
as a tourism destination.

2189.22 crore in BE 2018-19 and BE 2019 -20 respectively which were further 
reduced to Rs. 2113.48 crore and Rs. 1416.00 crore at RE 2018 -19 and RE 2019 -
20 stage respectively.   

 
 
13 
 
25. The Committee observes that tourism being a labour -intensive multi -
sectoral activity characteri sed by multiple services and industries is a key driver 
of socio -economic progress as well as employment generation and economic 
development.  The tourism sector has the potential to stimulate other economic 
sectors through its backward and forward linkage s and cross -sectoral synergies 
with sectors like agriculture, handicrafts, transport, construction, to name a few.  
It is thus evident that any higher investment made in the tourism sector can lead 
to large sale employment generation, alleviate poverty and  propel India to a 
faster growth trajectory.   
26. The Committee is dismayed to note that despite its unique endowments of 
biodiversity and its rich culture and heritage, India‘s total share in global 
international tourist arrivals remains a modest 1.24% a gainst the target of 3% 
while, as per the Report of the Working Group of Tourism of the 12 th Five Year 
Plan, in about 150 countries of the world, tourism is one of the 5 top export 
earners and number one export earner in about 60 countries. When measured by 
the yardstick of its vast tourism resources, India‘s low share of tourism arrivals 
is certainly below its potential.  Similarly, the contribution (direct and indirect) 
of tourism in the GDP and the total jobs in the country is estimated to be 5.06% 
and 12.75% respectively, which, in the considered opinion of the Committee, is 
inadequate and way  below the massive potential that exists. The Committee 
wishes to point out that in many smaller and developing countries , the entire 
economy of the country depends on tourism for its survival and tourism remains 
a major source of foreign exchange earnings . That being the case , the world's 
second largest country in terms of population, seventh largest by area, having 
7500 km of coastline and one of the most endowed regions of the world in terms 
of its tourism attractiveness, India receives less internationa l tourists than its full 
potential.  Taking all these factors into account, the Committee apprehends that 
the shortfall of Rs. 147.42 crore in BE 2020 -21 against the projected demand of 
Rs. 2647.25 crore would seriously jeopardize the targeted tourism outc omes 
during the Financial Year 2020-21.  

 
 
14 
 
27.    The Committee notes the submission of the Ministry that the difference in 
the projection made by it and the allocation given for the financial year 2020 -21 
is not high and that if additional funds are require d, it would move the Ministry 
of Finance for additional allocation at the RE 2020 -21 stage.  The Committee 
observes that availability of adequate resources to the tourism sector is sine qua 
non for achieving the tourism growth as well as inclusive growth.  Since 
development of tourism infrastructure is capital intensive, the Committee 
apprehends that with the budgetary allocation of Rs.2499.83 crore for 2020 -21, 
which, in the opinion of the Committee, is low, it would be difficult for the 
Ministry to take u p significant activities related to on -going infrastructure 
development of the sanctioned tourism circuits/destinations and also 
development of new tourism products of global standards.  If the tourism sector 
has to play a major role in faster and inclusiv e growth, the infrastructure 
bottlenecks need to be unleashed.  The Committee notes that more than half of 
the allocation of the Ministry for 2020 -21 is devoted for the schemes relating to 
infrastructure development.  In most of the States/UTs, the outlay for tourism is 
meagre and the Central Government has dominance in the domain of public 
resource mobilization by w ay of collection of tax revenue.  The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry be provided a higher financial outlay at the RE 
2020-21 stage.  The  Committee would like the Ministry of Tourism to bring the 
above recommendation to the notice of Ministry of Finance and also intimate the 
Committee of their response in this regard.    
28.    Since the consumption demand arising from tourist expenditure h as a 
multiplier effect on the economy, the expansion of the tourist sector can lead to 
large scale employment gene ration and poverty alleviation. Needless to mention, 
tourism has huge potential to stimulate overall economic growth and any 
increase in the o utlay for tourism sector can propel our country to a faster 
growth trajectory and will lead to large scale employment generation and 
alleviation of poverty. If our country can tap its full potential of the tourism 
sector, it can play a major role for faste r and inclusive growth;  but for this to 
happen, the budgetary provisions for the Ministry has to be enhanced 

 
 
15 
 
substantially.  By doing so, tourism infrastructure could be strengthened/ 
upgraded, conservation and development of all heritage sites could be 
undertaken and completed and last mile connectivity to tourist de stinations could 
be improved. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government 
should accord priority status to the tourism sector and enumerate a fiscal 
roadmap for generating and allo cating more financial resource for tourism so 
that the full potential of a vibrant sector could be tapped. 
29. The Committee notes with dismay the huge mismatch between the 
projected demand for funds and actual allocations made for the Ministry of 
Tourism for the years 2018 -19 and 2019 -20 as well.  The pattern of shortfall in 
allocation of funds indicates that budgetary requirements are being projected by 
the Ministry more on the basis of theoretical anticipation rather than on actual 
trend of requirement. The Ministry‘s reply that the Schemes/Projects 
undertaken by them are of continuous nature and that the targets are fixed and 
funds are released as per budgetary allocation by the Ministry of Finance 
suggests the casual and routine manner in which the Budg et Estimates are being 
prepared and the Ministry is not very serious about the activities to be 
undertaken by them.  Tourism is important for both economic growth and 
employment generation and the corpus of funds should not have been arbitrarily 
decided without reference to any ground reality.   
30. The Committee would, therefore, like the Ministry to have the entire 
requirement of funds realistically assessed after collecting timely information on 
requirement of funds from the State Governments and other s takeholders and 
take steps to rectify and improve upon the existing system of assessing 
requirement of funds. The Ministry should formulate Schemes/Programmes 
which can be implemented in a time -bound manner.  The Committee desires to 
be apprised of the specific action taken in this regard. 
31. The Committee takes serious note of the fact that the Ministry has kept the 
unspent provisions of Rs. 43.18 Crore till the close of the financial year 2018 -19 
and surrendered the same on 29.03.2019 totally disregardin g the provisions of 

 
 
16 
 
General Financial Rules which states that unspent provisions in a grant should  
be surrendered as soon as they  are foreseen, without waiting for the last day of 
the year.  The Committee deprecates such a casual approach of the Ministry in 
adhering to the fiscal discipline and desires the Ministry to avoid such lapses in 
future and surrender unspent budgetary provisions timely s o that starved 
projects/schemes are not deprived of the same. 
32. The Committee takes note of the fact that the annual growth rate of the 
Tourism Sector in India is 5.2% and its contribution to GDP is 5.06%. According 
to UN World Tourism Organisation Report (2011), for diversified economies, the 
contribution of tourism to national GDP is over 10% for countries where tourism 
happens to be the main driver of national economy. Quite apparently, despite 
having a strong domestic tourist base which is likely  to grow further on the back 
of a rapidly rising middle class with increased disposable incomes and having 
many World Heritage sites and rich fauna, our country has not been able to 
exploit its tourism potential to the fullest possible extent and the touri st sector 
has not proved to be the proverbial engine of growth for our economy. For a 
country of our size, with wealth of attractions and experiences, this 
underperformance represents significant foregone economic value. Since tourism 
in the country has th e potential to emerge as a key economic driver through 
economic growth and employment generation, the country can make a giant leap 
towards achieving 5 trillion dollar economy by tapping the enormous potential of 
the tourism sector. The Committee, therefor e, recommends that the strategies 
adopted for promotion and development of the tourist sector should be 
recalibrated to harness the full potential of Indian tourism and double the 
current contribution of tourism to GDP in the next 5 years. The Committee 
would like the Ministry to prepare a vision document, chalking out a road map 
for accelerating the expansion of the tourism sector and helping achieve a 5 
trillion dollar economy by 2025 by way of a substantial contribution from the 
tourism sector. The Commi ttee, therefore, desires that policy measures may be 
initiated by the Ministry to accelerate the growth momentum of the tourism 

 
 
17 
 
sector and raise the contribution of tourism from the current 5.06% to 10% of 
GDP. 
33. The Committee notes from the information made available to it , that a 
substantial amount of Rs. 245.308 crore is involved in pending Utilization 
Certificates (UCs) under various Schemes/ Programmes of the Ministry.  Since 
conditionality regarding submission of UCs is an absolute bar for release o f 
funds, the Committee apprehends that the pendency of UCs may impinge on the 
implementation of the flagship Schemes/Projects of the Ministry.  The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should put in place a 
dedicated mechanism to ensure that all pending UCs are liquidated within a 
period of six months from the presentation of this Report.

56. The Committee is constrained  to observe that under the Swadesh Darshan 
Scheme (SDS), out of the 77 projects sanctioned so far for Rs. 6035.70 Crore, 
only 9 Projects have reached their logical conclusion and the remaining projects 
have witnessed physical progress ranging from 50% to 90% and 10 projects have 
not even  taken off due to non -release of funds. The Committee also notes that no 
new projects have been sanctioned during 2019 -20, though the Ministry has not 
adduced any reasons for this.  The Committe e further notes with serious concern 
that against the sanctioned provision of Rs. 6035.70 Crore under the SDS, only 
Rs. 3744.00 crore have so far been released.  It is a matter of anguish for the 
Committee that such substantial variations have occurred bet ween the 
sanctioned provisions and the actual release and expenditure.  Obviously, these 
instances betray absence of a sound budgetary mechanism for assessing the 

 
 
25 
 
actual requirements of funds.  The Committee , therefore, recommends that the 
Ministry should address this issue squarely and devise a foolproof mechanism to 
overcome the deficiencies in the existing system of assessing the requirement of 
funds under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme. 
57. The Committee takes note of the remedial measures formulated by the  
Ministry for effective implementation of the projects sanctioned under the SDS 
and would like the Ministry to carry out an appraisal of their efficacy so that the 
avowed objective of developing world class infrastructure in the circuit 
destinations, promoting cultural and heritage value of the country and providing 
complete tourism experience with varied thematic circuits under the Scheme 
could be achieved. 
58. The Committee is of the view that though the Ministry reviews the 
progress of the projects const antly under the SDS, the absence of a dedicated 
monitoring mechanism at the State level is hampering the performance and goals 
of the projects sanctioned under it.  The Committee , therefore, recommends that 
the Ministry should , without further loss of time , take up the issue with the 
concerned State Governments at the highest level to understand their constraints 
in implementation of tourism projects and put in place a dedicated mechanism 
for implementation of the projects as it has a direct bearing on the timelines set 
for these projects.  Such a focused monitoring would go a long way in speeding 
up long pending SDS projects crucial for enhancing the tourist attractiveness and 
realising the tourism potential of India‘s assets. 
59. The Committee observes that rural tourism is among a few emerging areas 
of tourist interest world -wide.  Rural tourism is important because it helps in 
inclusive development of remote and backward areas by way of enhancing 
earning capacity and better livel ihood for the rural population.  As of now, two 
projects with a sanctioned outlay of Rs. 125.02 crore have been approved under 
Rural Circuit out of which only Rs. 21.24 Crore has been released for a project in 
Bihar while no funds have been released for an other sanctioned Rural Circuit in 
Kerala which is indicative of the snail‘s pace of progress in the matter.  The 

 
 
26 
 
Committee is of the opinion that had the Ministry made co -ordinated efforts with 
the State Government of Kerala , the handicaps in implementing the project 
could have been ironed out and the project could have kick started. 
60. The Committee recommends that for better promotion of rural  tourism, a 
cluster approach may be pursued rather than a stand -alone approach and more 
and more Rural Circuit P rojects may be sanctioned and implemented for 
promotion of niche tourism and more funds may be earmarked for rural circuits 
under the SDS. 
61. The Committee is dismayed to note that all 5 Buddhist Circuit Projects 
costing Rs. 355.26 Crore have witnessed ti me overruns.  The reasons attributed 
by the Ministry  include land availability, delay in statutory clearances, delay in 
tendering work by implementing agencies, etc.  The Committee is of the firm 
view that had the Ministry completed pre -project activities  including clearance 
before sanction of these projects or before award of contract, persistent problem 
of time overrun could have been easily avoided.  Now that the Ministry has 
revised the guidelines of the scheme in 2017, the Committee expects that the 
sanctioned Buddhist Circuit Projects would be implemented expeditiously and 
the issues related to time overrun would be resolved.  The Committee desires to 
be apprised of the outcome in this regard. 
62. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should  pursue with all 
the State Governments the matter of setting up of a State Level Monitoring 
Committee to remove various impediments like delays in land acquisition and 
statutory clearances so that time overrun in Buddhist Circuit Projects is 
minimized.  Th is would also speed up execution of Buddhist Circuit Projects 
within the approved cost.

2015, the accumulated amount rele ased for all the sanctioned projects under the 
PRASHAD is Rs. 505.15 Crore against the sanctioned 28 Projects for Rs. 840.20 
Crore.  Out of these 28 approved projects, only two projects, viz, Development of

75. The Committee notes that the PRASHAD has been launched  with the 
objective of holistic development of identified pilgrimage and heritage 
destinations and aims at infrastructure development.  Since the provision of 
infrastructure is a prerequisite towards improving the country‘s tourism 
productive capacity and attracting more tourists, the delay being witnessed in the 
expeditious operationalization of PRASHAD projects is pathetic and is suggestive 
of laxity in the monitoring system of the Ministry and the State Governments. 
This leaves the Committee wondering as  to how the Ministry would achieve their 

 
 
35 
 
envisaged objective of this Scheme.  The Committee , therefore, recommends that 
the shortcoming noticed in implementation of the projects under the PRASHAD 
should be addressed quickly. The Committee also recommends that the projects 
initiated under the PRASHAD should have a definite date of completion. Unless 
this is done, ambitious budgeting without commensurate capacity to deliver the 
desired outcomes under the PRASHAD would remain a futile exercise. The 
Committee also recommends that the achievements of the targets set under 
PRASHAD be analysed in detail for formulating remedial measures.  
76. The Committee is constrained to note nil progress in respect of four 
PRASHAD Project s, namely, (i) Development of Omkareshwar,  (ii) Cruise 
tourism in river Ganga (Varanasi), (iii) Development of Varanasi II and (iv) 
Development of Trimbakeshwar (Nasik) during the year 2017 -18. The 
Committee is further constrained to note that the reasons behind the lack of 
progress in implementing them were the deficiencies in project formulation and 
delay in obtaining all required clearances.  It is obvious that the efforts of the 
Ministry towards operationalization of the above projects have been undertaken 
in a piecemeal manner.  Though the Ministry has informed the Committee that 
appropriate corrective measures have been taken to eradicate t he deficiencies in 
project formulation and obtain all necessary approvals, the Committee desires 
that the Ministry should regularly monitor the progress of the above projects at 
higher levels, particularly so, as it relates to the creation of tourist infrastructure. 
77. The Committee notes that against the sanctioned outlay of Rs. 840.02 
Crore under the PRASHAD, a total of Rs. 505.15 Crore has been released.  The 
Committee desires to be apprised of the variations, if any, between the 
sanctioned provision and the actual expenditure incurred under the PRASHAD.

including Market Development Assistance was launched with the major objective of 
creating a general awareness amongst the domestic population about the tourist 
destinations and to develop tourist market within the country. The Committee 
observes that it is often seen that the researches pertaining to travel and tourism take 
place mainly on inbound and outbound tourist num bers and Domestic Tourism is 
given lesser importance. But, since domestic tourism generates income redistribution 
effect from tourists to local population and is also a catalyst for various other 
multiplier effects throughout the value chain, boosting loca l economy as well as 
national economy in the process, it should not be regarded as opposed or an 
alternative to Overseas Tourism. Instead these two forms of tourism should 
complement each other. The Committee , therefore, recommends that statistical data 
should be collected for planning and evaluation of various Domestic Tourism 
Programmes and that deficiencies in various types of domestic tourism statistics 
should be addressed.

VIII Cruise Tourism 
 
127. The Ministry of Tourism provides Central Financial Assistance (CFA) to the 
State Governments/UT Administrations/Central Government Agencies for 
development of Tourism including Cruise Tourism and Cruising along rivers. The 
Ministry has also sanctioned various projects for the development of Cruise Terminals 
and related infrastructure in Goa, Maharashtra, Kerala and Tamil Nadu at the major 
ports for Rs.135.72 Crore under the Scheme - „Assistance to Central Agencies for 
Tourism Infrastructure Development‟.  
 
128. The Committee has been informed that to harness the potential of cruise tourism in 
the country, a Task Force had been constituted with the Secretary (Tourism) as the 
Chairman and Secretary (Shipping) as the co -Chairman.  On the recommendations of 
Task Force, the following measures were taken for the development of cruise tourism:- 
 
 Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) have been formulated to be followed by the 
various agencies for handling cruise ships. 
 The facility of e-tourist visa has been extended to passengers arriving at the ports 
of Mumbai, Mormugao, Mangalore, Kochi and Chennai. 
 The Ministry of Home Affairs has waived off biometric requirements for cruise 
passengers arriving on e-via for a period of three year, i.e. upto 31.12.2020. 
 To address manpower, co-ordination and logistical issues for handling cruise 
vessels at ports, “Port Level Facilitation Committees” have been formed under the 
respective Chairman of the Major  Ports to facilitate seamless handling of cruise 
ships and passengers. 
 Foreign flag vessels carrying passengers have been allowed to call at Indian ports 
without obtaining licence from Director General of Shipping. 
On being asked as to why the Ministry has not utilized any other waterways, except 
for National Waterway 1 and Natio nal Waterway 2, for developing cruise circuits 
in the country and what are the difficulties faced by the Ministry in developing 
cruise tourism projects in And aman and Nicobar Islands, the Ministry has stated 
the following: 
The mandate of Inland Waterways A uthority of India (IWAI) is to develop 
and regulate National Waterways for cargo shipping & navigation.  
 
The infrastructure developed for transportation on National Waterways by 
IWAI including fairway, terminals, jetties, navigation aids etc. are used by 
the river cruise tourism operators. IWAI plays the role of a technical 
facilitator for river cruise tourism on National Waterways. 
 

 
 
51 
 
River cruise tourism has been a regular feature on National Waterway 
(NW)-1(Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system) and NW -2 (river 
Brahmaputra) since several years. Various cruise operators viz., M/s 
Heritage River Cruises Pvt. Ltd., M/s Vivada Inland Waterways and M/s 
Assam Bengal Navigation Company operate their cruise vessels on NW -1, 
NW-2 and Sunderbans waterways. 
 
National Waterway (NW) -1 (Ganga - Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system 
from Allahabad to Haldia), NW – 2 (River Brahmaputra from Dhubri to 
Sadiya), NW -3 (West Coast Canal from Kottapuram to Kollam along with 
Udyogmandal and Champakara Canals) have already been develo ped with 
fairway navigational aids, jetties and terminals with mechanized equipment 
handling facilities for loading and unloading of cargo. 
 
In addition to NW -1 & NW -2; NW -3 Kerala is a world renowned tourist 
destination for domestic and foreign tourists w here house boat tourism with 
food and accommodation facilities are available. The area of operation of 
these boats include Vembnad lake of Alapuzha, Kuttanad area and 
Astamudi lake of Kollam area. 
 
129. The Committee notes from the information made availab le to it that in the meeting 
chaired by the Prime Minister on 21 st June, 2014, it was decided that the Ministry of 
Shipping and the Ministry of Tourism would jointly identify the routes for carrying out 
cruise tours on waterways and also take measures to develop necessary infrastructure.  
Accordingly, a Working Group was  constituted to examine the modalities of cruise tours 
connecting religious places and other relate d issues.  The W orking Group has identified , 
inter alia , the following key issues and challenges pertaining to development of these 
circuits:- 
(i) Development of Infrastructure including all weather navigable channels. 
(ii) Provision of tourist amenities at terminals, jetlines, river fronts, etc., and 
(iii) Proper maintenance of tourist places. 
 
130. The Committee has also been informed that the Task Force constituted with 
Secretary (Tourism) as the Chairman and Secretary (Shipping) as the Co -Chairman 
consists of representatives from the ports, Ministry of Health, Home Affairs, External 
Affairs, Custom s, CISF, Coastal States etc. The Task Force meets regularly and has 
formulated Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) to be followed by the various agencies 
for handling of cruise ships. The Task Force has reviewed the SOPs and updated them 
into the SOP versi on 2 which is to be used for the cruise season 2017 -18. On the 

 
 
52 
 
recommendation of the Task Force, Ministry of Shipping and Ministry of Tourism have 
jointly appointed a consultant for preparing Action Plan and detailed road map for the 
development of Cruise Tourism in India. The consultants have submitted their report 
which contains many recommendations for making India a preferred destination both for 
Sea and River Cruise. The Task Force has accepted the report and decided to engage a 
Project Management Cons ultant to monitor its implementation. No projects have been 
sanctioned for development of cruise facilities to States during the year 2017 -18, 2018-19, 
2019-20.  
131. The Committee gathers that during the year 2017 -18 a total of 1,62,660 cruise 
passengers visited India at six major ports, namely, Mumbai Port, Chennai Port, Kochin 
Port, Kolkata Port, New Mangalore Port and Mormugao Port. During the same period a 
total of 139 cruise ships visited India at the six major ports. As per media reports,  the 
total cruise callings were 285 during 2018-19. 
 
132. The Committee observes that Cruise Shipping is one of the fastest growing 
components of the leisure industry world -wide.  The Indian economy is 
developing at a steady pace and became the fifth largest economy in 2019 
surpassing the U.K. and France (as per IMF‘s October 2019 World Economic 
Outlook).  India‘s middle class possessing disposal incomes is also growing in 
number. Despite all these advantages, cruise tourism in India is still in its nascent 
stage and India does not even figure in the top ten in Asia in terms of Cruise line 
port calls.  India has a mere 285 cruise calls in FY 2018 -19 whereas Thailand and 
Malaysia get about 500 cruise calls a year.  The fact remains that India‘s 
enormous cruise potential remains untapped despite being endowed with 7,500 
km of coastline.  To meet India‘s untapped cruise potential, a high level Task 
Force was constituted in the year 2015 with Secretary (Tourism) as Chairma n 
and Secretary (Shipping) as co -Chairman.  Five years have elapsed since then.  
The Task Force has reviewed and updated t he Standard Operating Procedure  
and a consultant has been jointly appointed by Ministry of Tourism and Ministry 
of Shipping for prepar ing an Action Plan and detailed blue print for the 
development of cruise tourism in the country.  It is really intriguing that despite 
acceptance of the report of the Consultant, no projects have been sanctioned for 

 
 
53 
 
development of cruise tourism to the States during 2017-18, 2018-19 and 2019-20. 
This, in the opinion of the Committee, speaks volumes of the Government‘s 
inertia and lethargy in the matter.   
133. Cruise Tourism is a supply -driven market and cruise lines are always in 
search of new markets and destinations.  India‘s enchanting and exotic 
destinations could catapult India as one of the leading cruise destinations.  But 
for that to happen, stable and consistent operating conditions will have to be 
concretized because cruise line companies which ty pically plan two to three years 
ahead, need to know that the basic conditions of operating are stable and 
consistent.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Tourism 
in collaboration with Ministry of Shipping should expedite appropriate policy 
measures for developing India‘s largely untapped and hitherto small cruise 
market and pull cruise vessels to its shores.  The Committee desires to be 
updated on the progress made in this regard. 
134. The Committee also observes that many of India‘s destinations are in its 
interiors and water -based tourism is well -developed in some States like Kerala, 
Goa, West Bengal etc. However, a lot remains to be done to develop river cruise 
that connects interior tourist destinations. The Committee, therefore, d esires to 
be kept apprised of the steps taken and the achievement made towards 
developing river cruise in the country.

X. Safety and Security of Tourists 
 
153. The Committee has been informed that Ministry of Tourism is seized with the issue 
to ensure safety and security of the tourists visiting the Country in general and women in 
particular. In this connection, the following steps have been taken so far: (i) Meetings of 

 
 
61 
 
the Tourism Ministers of State Governments and Lt. Governors / Tourism 
Ministers/Administrators of all Union Territory Administrations were held in 2013 and 
2014 wherein a resolution was adopted that the Departments of Tourism of all States and 
UTs will work for ensuring safety and security of tourists, especially, women. (ii) A code 
of conduct by the Indian travel and tourism industry was adopted for Safe and Honourabl e 
Tourism which contains a set of guidelines to encourage tourism activities to be 
undertaken with respect to basic rights like dignity, safety and freedom from exploitation 
of both tourists and local residents, in particular women and children. (iii) To e nsure 
safety & security of Tourists it is ensured to include CCTV cameras in most of the 
projects under Swadesh Darshan and  PRASHAD schemes. Further, instructions have 
been issued to all State Governments to set up Tourist Police. (iv) To ensure the safet y 
and security of the tourists while clicking selfies, Ministry of Tourism had issued a letter 
on 10.8.2016 to all State Governments/UT Administrations with the advice to take 
following measures that could go a long way in avoiding any such mishaps:-  
(1) Identification of all such tourist spots which are prone to accidents.  
(2) Erection of signage warning visitors of the danger involved in taking selfies at 
such locations.  
(3) Posting of volunteers/tourist police at such identified places, if feasible.  
(4) Sensitization through Public Address system.  
(5) Spreading awareness through social and other media campaigns.  
(6) Barricading areas, wherever possible danger is identified. 
 
154. The Committee has been informed that t he Ministry, on an    ongoing basis 
coordinates with all the State Governments/UT  Administrations on      matters of safety 
and security of tourists.  
 
155. The Ministry has also informed that the following steps have been taken to ensure 
safety and security of tourists at tourists places:- 
 
(i) The Ministry has set up a 24x7 Multi -Lingual Tourist Info-Helpline on the toll free 
number 1800111363 or on a short code 1363 in 12 Languages including 10 
international languages, Hindi & English for domestic and foreign  tourists to 
provide support service in terms of information relating to Travel in India and also 
to offer appropriate guidance to tourists in distress while travelling in India.  
(ii) The Ministry has taken up the matter with all State Governments/ Union Terri tory 
(UT) Administrations for setting up of dedicated Tourism Police. With the efforts 
of Ministry of Tourism, the State Governments /UT Administrations of Andhra 
Pradesh,      Delhi, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, 
Jammu and Kashmir,       Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim and 
Uttar Pradesh have deployed tourist police in one form or the other.  

 
 
62 
 
(iii) The Ministry along with all stakeholders, including the Tourism 
Departments of all States and UTs, have adopted the 'Code of  Conduct for Safe & 
Honourable Tourism' which is a set of guidelines to encourage tourism activities to 
be undertaken with respect for basic right like dignity, safety and freedom from 
exploitation of both tourists and local residents in particular, women and children.  
 
(iv) The Ministry has issued Guidelines on Safety and Security of Tourists for 
State Governments/Union Territories to stress on the importance of safety and risk 
management, assist in identifying best practices and encourage closer cooperation 
for ensuring a pleasant experience to the tourists. 
 
156. The Committee observes that safety and security of tourists is of vital 
importance as any adverse impression in this regard has serious implications on 
tourist arrivals to the country.  In the past, there have been numerous incidents 
of crime reported against foreign tourists in some popular destinations across the 
country.  In order to make India a safe tourist destination where tourists would 
feel safe  and feel free to move around, the State Governments/ UT 
Administrations of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, 
Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Punjab, 
Rajasthan, Sikkim and Uttar Pradesh have set up tourist po lice in one form or 
the other.  The Committee recommends that in the light of the security concerns 
at tourist destinations, a committed and professionally trained tourist police 
should be deployed at all important destinations of tourist importance so tha t 
foreign and domestic tourists visiting tourist destinations are assured of their 
safety and security.  The Committee would , therefore, like the Ministry of 
Tourism to take up the matter up with the remaining States/UTs at the highest 
level so that Touris t Police is set up in all important tourist destinations of each 
State/UT of tourist importance. 
157. The Committee takes note of the other measures initiated by the Ministry 
of Tourism such as a 24 7 Multi-Lingual Tourist Info -Helpline, adoption of the 
Code of Conduct for ‗Safe and Honourable Tourism,‖ and Guidelines on Safety 
and Security of Tourists to ensure that widespread awareness on issues related to 
good behaviour towards tourists, civic responsibilities and security and comfort

of tourists, is generated.  The Committee desires to be apprised of the efficacy of

XI India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) 
 
158. India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) is a Public Sector Undertaking 
under administrative control of the Ministry of Tourism. Incorporated on October 1, 1966, 
ITDC played a key role in the development of tourism infrastructure in the country. The 
Corporation is running hotels, restaurants at various places for t ourists, besides providing 
transport facilities. In addition, the Corporation is engaged in production, distribution and 
sale of tourist publicity literature and providing entertainment and duty -free shopping 
facilities to the tourists. The Corporation als o has its presence in engineering related 
consultancy services. ITDC was set up with a view to undertake development and 
promotion of tourism related activities. ITDC has been mandated to promote tourism in 
the country in form of infrastructure development , hotels & accommodation, travel & 
tourism promotion, printing & publicity, event management, hospitality education, Sound 
and Light Shows and other related activities. It went ahead with a view to promote 
tourism by providing quality infrastructure in pla ces where the tourism potential was 
untapped due to non-availability of accommodation, travel arrangements, etc. 
 
159. The Corporation also takes up work of execution of Engineering Projects and 
preparation of DPRs for tourism related projects. ITDC has pl ayed a committed and 
pivotal role in the development of tourism infrastructure in backward areas, thereby trying 
to promote regional balance. After the disinvestment of 09 hotels and one incomplete 
hotel project, ITDC consolidated its remaining activities and restructured itself to take up 
diversified service -oriented business activities. As per Disinvestment Policy of the 
Government of India, 9 hotel properties including 3 Joint Venture Hotel properties (viz 
Hotel Lake View Ashok, Bhopal; Hotel Brahmaputra  Ashok, Guwahati, Hotel Bharatpur 
Ashok, Bharatpur, incomplete hotel project at Gulmarg, Hotel Janpath, New Delhi, Hotel 
Jaipur Ashok, Jaipur, Lalitha Mahal Palace Hotel, Mysore, Hotel Pataliputra Ashok, Patna 
and Hotel Donyi Polo Ashok, Itanagar) have bee n transferred/ handed over to the 
respective State Governments. Disinvestment/Divestment process of remaining properties 
i.e. Process for joint leasing in respect of Hotel Pondicherry Ashok, Puducherry; Hotel 
Nilachal Ashok, Puri, process for giving Hotel Kalinga Ashok, Bhubaneswar on 
Operation & Maintenance Contract is underway. Hotel operations at Hotel Ranchi Ashok, 
Ranchi and Hotel Nilachal Ashok Puri are closed. Incomplete Project at Anandur Sahib, 
Puri is under way to be transferred to State Government. 
 
160. With the changing economic and business scenario, the Corporation is in the 
process of strengthening all business verticals to increase its turnover and profitability and 
to position itself as one stop solution for travel, tourism and hospitality needs.  

 
 
64 
 
 
161. ITDC is striving to achieve the desired position by leveraging on inherent strength 
of Corporation as a well -known, established and trusted brand and by strengthening and 
enlarging other potential SBUs by adopting SBU specific strategy, incre asing customer 
base from B2G to B2C and  B2B, achieving customer delight and by offering value for 
money, quality services at par with best in industry.

172. The Committee notes that as per the Disinvestment Policy of the Government 
of India, 9 hotel properties including 3 joint venture properties have been

observes that in modern times , the success of hospitality business hinges on 
distribution and digital strategy. Distribution means having a wide portfolio of hotels 
- budget, mid-market, upscale, luxury, et c. - at key destinations. By transferring the 
management of these 9 hotels to State Governments who will run them as individual 
units, these hotels will lack the distribution strength that all the branded hotel chains 
- foreign or domestic - have been buil ding. The Committee  recommends that ITDC
