renovation and upgradation of hotel propert ies is a continuous activity. However, as 
a consequence of Disinvestment, no real attention has been given for upgradation and 
renovation of ITDC's hotel properties. The Committee is, therefore, of the considered 
opinion that in order to remain competitive  and match the standards of the private 
players, ITDC would require more funding support from the Government of India. 
Since share capital of ITDC is small and not adequate to carry out major capital 
expenditures and capital ventures, the Committee recomme nds that the Government 
of India should provide more funding support to ITDC by way of equity infusion. 
The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the action taken in its regard. 
174. The Committee also recommends that ITDC should undertake detailed 
manpower study in all its units/ divisions so that deployment of human resources 
could be rationalized. 
XII Miscellaneous 
175. The Committee notes that the Working Group on Tourism of the 12 th Five 
Year Plan , in its Report , had suggested a number of strategies  regarding 
development of the tourism sector like infrastructure, connectivity, human resource 
development and capacity augmentation, convergence among various agencies at 
Centre and State level for development of tourism, taxation, incentives and 
facilitation of tourism sector etc.  The Committee desires to be apprised of the extent 
to which those recommendations have been taken into consideration by the Ministry 
while formulating its Policies and Programmes.  
176. The Committee feels that each State Government has a responsibility to 
identify and reserve suitable Government land for development of potential tourist 
locations and the land so reserved should not be used for any other purposes other 

 
 
68 
 
than for constructi ng hotels, shopping complexes, etc.  The Central Government 
should also play a pivotal role in this regard. Central Ministries may also be advised 
to explore the possibility of identifying and reserving idle land for development of 
tourist locations. 
177. In order to promote tourism, the Committee would like the Ministry to act as a 
catalyst for building more amusement/theme parks on the lines of the Essel World, 
Mumbai and Disneyland, California.  In the coming years, such parks may be built in 
big metropolitan cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and funds should be earmarked 
for the purpose. 
178. The progress of implementation of projects sanctioned by the Ministry should 
be monitored on a monthly basis by a High Powered Project Monitoring Committee  
and it should be ensured that the funds released for the sanctioned projects do not 
remain idly parked , but are utilised produc tively for the intended purpose  and a 
monthly Progress Report  be submitted to the Minister for suitable direction, 
whenever the Projects are lagging behind. 
179. The Committee notes from the information furnished , that our country has 
targeted to increase its share in global tourist arrivals from the current 1.24% to 3% 
and double the number of domestic tourist visits from the current 18 54.9 million to 
3200 million visits.  If these ambitious targets are to be met, the country has to create 
appropriate employable skill in the population and also reduce the skill -gap.  The 
State Governments are major stakeholders in human resource and skill development.  
The Committee would, therefore, recommend that the Ministry in co -ordination with 
the State Governments, should formulate a multipronged approach to bridge the skill 
gap in the tourism sector and should also launch a programme to upgrade th e skills 
of the existing tourist service providers. 
180. The Committee notes that the Scheme of Swadesh Darshan was launched with 
the objective of developing tourist circuits on specific themes and as of now, 15 such 
Circuits have been identified for Integ rated Infrastructure Development. Since the 
creation of tourist infrastructure leads to overall economic growth, the Committee 

 
 
69 
 
would like the Ministry to identify more tourism circuits and develop them in an 
integrated manner. 
181. The Committee notes that  there is lack of reasonably priced accommodation 
near the tourist destinations in the country. Expensive accommodation is a big 
deterrent not only for international tourists , but also for domestic tourists. The 
Committee would, therefore, like the Ministr y to take up with the State 
Governments, the issue of promotion of Home Stays and earmark funds for the same 
so that the widening gap between supply and demand of the accommodation sector 
could be easily bridged.  
182. The Committee notes that most of the international and domestic tourists visit 
enchantingly beautiful Kerala which is famous for its beautiful backwaters, unique 
culture and traditions and rich vegetation. The State is one of the most popular 
tourist destinations of the world. From the inform ation made available, it seems that 
no major tourism project has been sanctioned for the State of Kerala in the recent 
past.  The Committee, therefore, desires to know whether any tourist project 
forwarded by the State Government of Kerala for funding supp ort from the Ministry 
of Tourism is pending approval. The Committee also recommends that the approval 
to any such pending projects should be expedited.  
183. The Committee observes that cruise tourism in India is a niche product to 
promote and attract tour ists with specific interest. The Committee would, therefore, 
like the Ministry of Tourism to work in coordination with Ministry of Shipping 
towards establishing dedicat ed cruise terminals at all the Major P orts and also  
private ports in the country.  
184. The Roads and Highway networks play an important role in tourism and also 
in the growth of Indian economy. The Committee is aware that the Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways had taken up detailed review of National Highways 
network with a view to impr ove the road connectivity to tourist places. The 
Committee desires to be apprised of the progress made so far in this regard. 

 
 
70 
 
185. The Committee recommends that under the PRASHAD, the Ministry should 
develop a dedicated thoroughfare for use by pedestrians visiting Srisailam. The 
Araku Valley and Lambasingi in Visakhapatnam have great tourism 
significance and should be developed as tourist spots. 
186. The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministries of Civil Aviation, 
Shipping, Road Transport & Highways, Culture, Tourism and Railways  are not 
only inter -related and interconnected but also have a common objective to 
improve conne ctivity and better amenities for the benefit of tourists, travellers 
and faster movement of freight within the country. The Committee, therefore, 
feels that there is a pressing need for having an effective co -ordination 
mechanism among these Ministries so that the policies and guidelines being 
formulated by them are executed seamlessly and can supplement each other in 
achieving these objectives. This will not only increase effectiveness and efficiency, 
but will also help in utilization of funds and skilled manpower to the maximum 
possible extent. Therefore, the Committee recommends that an easy -to-use 
interface should be made available which allows hassle -free communication and 
co-ordination amongst them. A hotline number which is common to all these 
Ministries, may be established so that whenever emergency arises, there can be 
effective and prompt coordination among these Ministries and issues in hand can 
be resolved at the earliest. 
187. Belum Caves in Kurnool District, Andhra Pradesh which are the second 
largest caves on the Indian subcontinent, have immense tourism value and are, 
therefore, of national importance.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the 
above Caves and stone age Kethavaram Rock Paintings should be developed under 
the  Swadesh Darshan Scheme (SDS).   
188. Since religious tourism is an important segment of domestic tourism, the 
Committee recommends that Kolanu Bharati Saraswati Temple, Mahanandi, 
Ahobilam, Yaganti Uma Maheshwar Temple, Veera Brahman Gaari Matham, 
Kadapa District, Andhr a Pradesh should be developed under Spiritual Circuit of

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS — AT A GLANCE 
 
ANALYSIS OF BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS FOR 2020-21 
 The Committee notes that due to broad budgetary cuts imposed by the 
Ministry of Finance, the Ministry has witnessed a reduction in allocation of funds 
for the financial year 2020 -21 and has been allocated only Rs. 2499.83 crore as 
against its projected demand of Rs. 2647.25 crore.                           (Para:23) 
 The Committee also notes that less allocation as compared to the projected 
demand is not unique to the financial year 2020-21.  Against the projected 
demands of Rs. 4320.42 Crore and Rs. 4612.18 Crore for Financial Year 2018-19 
and 2019-20 respectively, Ministry of Finance provided Rs. 2150.00 crore and Rs. 
2189.22 crore in BE 2018-19 and BE 2019-20 respectrively which were further 
reduced to Rs. 2113.48 crore and Rs. 1416.00 crore at RE 2018-19 and RE 2019-
20 stage respectively.                                                                                                  
(Para:24) 
 The Committee observes that tourism being a labour -intensive multi -
sectoral activity characterised by multiple services and industries is a key driver 
of socio -economic progress as well as employment generation and economic 
development.  The tourism sector  has the potential to stimulate other economic 
sectors through its backward and forward linkages and cross -sectoral synergies 
with sectors like agriculture, handicrafts, transport, construction, to name a few.  
It is thus evident that any higher investment  made in the tourism sector can lead 
to large sale employment generation, alleviate poverty and propel India to a 
faster growth trajectory.                            (Para:25) 
The Committee is dismayed to note that despite its unique endowments of 
biodiversity and its rich culture and heritage, India‘s total share in global 
international tourist arrivals remains a modest 1.24% against the target of 3% 
while, as per the Report of the Working Group of Tourism of the 12 th Five Year 
Plan, in about 150 countrie s of the world, tourism is one of the 5 top export 
earners and number one export earner in about 60 countries. When measured by 
the yardstick of its vast tourism resources, India‘s low share of tourism arrivals 

 
 
74 
 
is certainly below its potential.  Similarly,  the contribution (direct and indirect) 
of tourism in the GDP and the total jobs in the country is estimated to be 5.06% 
and 12.75% respectively, which, in the considered opinion of the Committee, is 
inadequate and way below the massive potential that exis ts. The Committee 
wishes to point out that in many smaller and developing countries , the entire 
economy of the country depends on tourism for its survival and tourism remains 
a major source of foreign exchange earnings. That being the case , the world's 
second largest country in terms of population, seventh largest by area, having 
7500 km of coastline and one of the most endowed regions of the world in terms 
of its tourism attractiveness, India receives less international tourists than its full 
potential.  T aking all these factors into account, the Committee apprehends that 
the shortfall of Rs. 147.42 crore in BE 2020 -21 against the projected demand of 
Rs. 2647.25 crore would seriously jeopardize the targeted tourism outcomes 
during the Financial Year 2020-21.                                                         (Para:26) 
        The Committee notes the submission of the Ministry that the difference in 
the projection made by it and the allocation given for the financial year 2020 -21 
is not high and that if additional funds are required, it would move the Ministry 
of Finance for additional allocation at the RE 2020 -21 stage.  The Committee 
observes that availability of adequate resources to the tourism sector is sine qua 
non for achieving the tourism growt h as well as inclusive growth.  Since 
development of tourism infrastructure is capital intensive, the Committee 
apprehends that with the budgetary allocation of Rs.2499.83 crore for 2020 -21, 
which, in the opinion of the Committee, is low, it would be diffi cult for the 
Ministry to take up significant activities related to on -going infrastructure 
development of the sanctioned tourism circuits/destinations and also 
development of new tourism products of global standards.  If the tourism sector 
has to play a ma jor role in faster and inclusive growth, the infrastructure 
bottlenecks need to be unleashed.  The Committee notes that more than half of 
the allocation of the Ministry for 2020 -21 is devoted for the schemes relating to 
infrastructure development.  In most  of the States/UTs, the outlay for tourism is 
meagre and the Central Government has a dominance in the domain of public 

 
 
75 
 
resource mobilization by way of collection of tax revenue. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry be provided a higher financial out lay at the RE 
2020-21 stage.  The Committee would like the Ministry of Tourism to bring the 
above recommendation to the notice of Ministry of Finance and also intimate the 
Committee of their response in this regard.         (Para:27)  
    Since the consump tion demand arising from tourist expenditure has a 
multiplier effect on the economy, the expansion of the tourist sector can lead to 
large scale employment generation and  poverty alleviation. Needless to mention, 
tourism has huge potential to stimulate ove rall economic growth and any 
increase in the outlay for tourism sector can propel our country to a faster 
growth trajectory and will lead to large scale employment generation and 
alleviation of poverty. If our country can tap its full potential of the tour ism 
sector, it can play a major role for faster and inclusive growth, but for this to 
happen, the budgetary provisions for the Ministry has to be enhanced 
substantially.  By doing so, tourism infrastructure could be strengthened/ 
upgraded, conservation and  development of all heritage sites could be 
undertaken and completed and last mile connectivity to tourist de stinations could 
be improved. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government 
should accord priority status to the tourism sector and enumerate a fiscal 
roadmap for generating and allocating more financial resource for tourism so 
that the full potential of a vibrant sector could be tapped.      (Para:28)  
 The Committee notes with dismay the huge mismatch between the 
projected demand for  funds and actual allocations made for the Ministry of 
Tourism for the years 2018 -19 and 2019 -20 as well.  The pattern of shortfall in 
allocation of funds indicates that budgetary requirements are being projected by 
the Ministry more on the basis of theore tical anticipation rather than on actual 
trend of requirement. The Ministry‘s reply that the Schemes/Projects 
undertaken by them are of continuous nature and that the targets are fixed and 
funds are released as per budgetary allocation by the Ministry of F inance 
suggests the casual and routine manner in which the Budget Estimates are being 
prepared and the Ministry is not very serious about the activities to be 

 
 
76 
 
undertaken by them.  Tourism is important for both economic growth and 
employment generation and the corpus of funds should not have been arbitrarily 
decided without reference to any ground reality.                                                 
(Para:29)  
 The Committee would, therefore, like the Ministry to have the entire 
requirement of funds real istically assessed after collecting timely information on 
requirement of funds from the State Governments and other stakeholders and 
take steps to rectify and improve upon the existing system of assessing 
requirement of funds. The Ministry should formulate  Schemes/Programmes 
which can be implemented in a time -bound manner.  The Committee desires to 
be apprised of the specific action taken in this regard.    (Para:30)  
 The Committee takes serious note of the fact that the Ministry has kept the 
unspent provisions of Rs. 43.18 Crore till the close of the financial year 2018 -19 
and surrendered the same on 29.03.2019 totally disregarding the provisions of 
General Financial Rules which states that unspent provisions in a grant should 
be surrendered as soon as the y are foreseen, without waiting for the last day of 
the year.  The Committee deprecates such a casual approach of the Ministry in 
adhering to the fiscal discipline and desires the Ministry to avoid such lapses in 
future and surrender unspent budgetary prov isions timely so that starved 
projects/schemes are not deprived of the same.       (Para:31)  
The Committee takes note of the fact that the annual growth rate of the 
Tourism Sector in India is 5.2% and its contribution to GDP is 5.06%. According 
to UN World Tourism Organisation Report (2011), for diversified economies, the 
contribution of tourism t o national GDP, is over 10% for countries where 
tourism happens to be the main driver of national economy. Quite apparently, 
despite having a strong domestic tourist base which is likely to grow further on 
the back of a rapidly rising middle class with inc reased disposable incomes and 
having many World Heritage sites and rich fauna, our country has not been able 
to exploit its tourism potential to the fullest possible extent and the tourist sector 
has not proved to be the proverbial engine of growth for our  economy. For a 

 
 
77 
 
country of our size, with wealth of attractions and experiences, this 
underperformance represents significant foregone economic value. Since tourism 
in the country has the potential to emerge as a key economic driver through 
economic growth and employment generation, the country can make a giant leap 
towards achieving 5 trillion dollar economy by tapping the enormous potential of 
the tourism sector. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the strategies 
adopted for promotion and developmen t of the tourist sector should be 
recalibrated to harness the full potential of Indian tourism and double the 
current contribution of tourism to GDP in the next 5 years. The Committee 
would like the Ministry to prepare a vision document, chalking out a roa d map 
for accelerating the expansion of the tourism sector and helping achieve a 5 
trillion dollar economy by 2025 by way of a substantial contribution from the 
tourism sector. The Committee , therefore, desires that policy measures may be 
initiated by the Ministry to accelerate the growth momentum of the tourism 
sector and raise the contribution of tourism from the current 5.06% to 10% of 
GDP.                                        (Para:32) 
 The Committee notes from the information made available to it , that a 
substantial amount of Rs. 245.308 crore is involved in pending Utilization 
Certificates (UCs) under various Schemes/ Programmes of the Ministry.  Since 
conditionality regarding submission of UCs is an absolute bar for release of 
funds, the Committee a pprehends that the pendency of UCs may impinge on the 
implementation of the flagship Schemes/Projects of the Ministry.  The

and that the funds earmarked for them be utilized fully. The Committee would 
like to be informed of the achievements made vis-a-vis the targets fixed in this 
regard. The Committee also recommends that hospitality and tourism training 
institutes may also be set up in rural a reas to conduct training for the local 
community so that the opportunities for the poor can be expanded.         
(Para:125) 
 The Committee is aware that there is shortage of trainers specific to 
hospitality and tourism education and that the requirement of teachers would 
continue to be large and growing.  The Committee, therefore, desires to know as 
to how many dedicated teacher training institutes have been set up under the 
Scheme Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITM/NIWS and whether they are man dated 
to conduct customized training courses to cover the requirement of niche tourism 
products and new emerging areas specific to tourism. The Committee also 
desires to be apprised of the current production of trainers/teachers vis-a-vis 
their requirement annually.                    (Para:126) 

 
 
87 
 
CRUISE TOURISM 
 
 The Committee observes that Cruise Shipping is one of the fastest growing 
components of the leisure industry world -wide.  The Indian economy is 
developing at a steady pace and became the fifth largest economy in 2019 
surpassing the U.K. and France (as per IMF‘s October 2019 World Economic 
Outlook).  India‘s middle class possessing disposal incomes is also growing in 
number. Despite all these advantages, cruise tourism in India is still in its na scent 
stage and India does not even figure in the top ten in Asia in terms of Cruise line 
port calls.  India has a mere 285 cruise calls in FY 2018 -19 whereas Thailand and 
Malaysia get about 50 0 cruise calls a year.  T he fact remains that India‘s 
enormous cruise potential remains untapped despite being endowed with 7,500 
km of coastline.  To meet India‘s untapped cruise potential, a high level Task 
Force was constituted in the year 2015 with Secretary (Tourism) as Chairman 
and Secretary (Shipping) as co -Chairman.  Five years have elapsed since then.  
The Task Force has reviewed and updated the Standard Operating Procedure 
and a consultant has been jointly appointed by Ministry of Tourism and Ministry 
of Shipping for preparing an Action Plan and detailed blue  print for the 
development of cruise tourism in the country.  It is really intriguing that despite 
acceptance of the report of the Consultant, no projects have been sanctioned for 
development of cruise tourism to the States during 2017 -18, 2018-19 and 2019-20. 
This, in the opinion of the Committee, speaks volumes of the Government‘s 
inertia and lethargy in the matter.                             (Para:132) 
 Cruise Tourism is a supply -driven market and cruise lines are always in 
search of new markets and des tinations.  India‘s enchanting and exotic 
destinations could catapult India as one of the leading cruise destinations.  But 
for that to happen, stable and consistent operating conditions will have to be 
concretized because cruise line companies which typic ally plan two to three years 
ahead, need to know that the basic conditions of operating are stable and 
consistent.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Tourism 
in collaboration with Ministry of Shipping should expedite appropriate pol icy 
measures for developing India‘s largely untapped and hitherto small cruise 

 
 
88 
 
market and pull cruise vessels to its shores.  The Committee desires to be 
updated on the progress made in this regard.               (Para:133) 
 The Committee also observes tha t many of India‘s destinations are in its 
interiors and water -based tourism is well -developed in some States like Kerala, 
Goa, West Bengal etc. However, a lot remains to be done to develop river cruise 
that connects interior tourist destinations. The Commi ttee, therefore, desires to 
be kept apprised of the steps taken and the achievement made towards 
developing river cruise in the country.                (Para:134) 
CONNECTIVITY 
 
 The Committee is of the view that air connectivity is the key to unlocking 
India‘s inbound tourism potential.  Some States including those in North Eastern 
Region and other hilly regions have great tourism potential , but lack air 
connectivity.  Though 36 tourism sectors/ routes have been accepted by the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation  for incorporation under Region Connectivity Scheme 
– UDAN-3 which aims to promote short haul routes and gives flexibility to 
airlines in designing their network, the Committee apprehends that 
operationalisation of these 36 routes/sectors would face challe nge because UDAN 
is already facing serious issues with previous two rounds. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Tourism , in coordination with the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation , and through the Inter -Ministerial Coordination 
Committee for Tourism Sector should focus on prioritizing operationalisation of 
these 36 tourist routes/sectors.  The Committee would like to be apprised of the 
progress made in this regard.                                                                    (Para:146) 
 The Committee takes note of the fact that in -principle approval has been 
accorded to transfer land and working permission has been accorded to Airport s 
Authority of India for completion of terminal building at Leh Airport and the 
targeted date of completi on of the project is 30 th September, 2021.  The 
Committee would exhort the Ministry to ensure that this project is completed 
within the designated timeline and the approved cost, which will enable the 

 
 
89 
 
tourists to reach Leh without any hassle, thereby , contributing to improving the 
living conditions of people of Leh.                          (Para:147) 
 The Committee notes the submission of the Ministry that a total amount of 
Rs. 225 Crore has been earmarked for a period of three years for ―Extending 
Incentives for Improving Air Connectivity‖ under the Champion Services Sector 
Scheme.  But a perusal of Demand No. 98 for 2020 -21 pertaining to the Ministry 
of Tourism reveals that an amount of Rs. 123.00 Crore has been allocated in BE 
2020-21 for the Scheme of C hampion Services Sector Scheme.  Obviously, there 
is lack of clarity in this regard.  The Committee would, therefore, like the 
Ministry to explain in unambiguous term, the dichotomy in the matter. (Para:148) 
 The Committee notes that Rail is the most preferred mode of transport for 
domestic tourists.  As per the Budget (2011 -12), 26 railway stations had been 
identified for joint development of tourist amenities by the Ministry of Tourism 
and the Ministry of Railways.  The Committee notes with concern t hat out of the 
26 railway stations, only one has been completed and the remaining projects are 
still under implementation even after the lapse of ten years. This Scheme being 
conceived with the aim of improving railway stations for better tourist 
experience, the Committee expects the Ministry to go into the factors attributable 
to the delay in implementation in detail and urgently address , in collaboration 
with the Ministry of Railways , the pending issues pertaining to implementation 
of the scheme of upgradation of the 26 railway stations. Considering the fact that 
this Project has been languishing since long, the Committee desires to be 
furnished with a factual note detailing the current status of the Project and the 
Ministry‘s plan of action for expediting its implementation.  (Para:149) 
 The Committee notes that a  number of priority items aimed at ensuring 
cleanliness facilities at the railway stations have been identified.  Though 
cleanliness at railway stations ha s improved, it is not uniform across rail way 
stations.  The Committee , would, therefore, like the Ministry of Railways to 
conduct a third party audit and cleanliness ranking of the identified railway 

 
 
90 
 
stations so that an assessment could be made as to the efficacy of measures taken 
for providing world class facilities at the identified railway stations.  (Para:150) 
 The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has signed an MoU 
with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for development of roadside 
amenities on NationalHhighways and observes that some of the important tourist 
destinations in the country are still not connected properly.  The Committee, 
therefore, desires to be updated on the State road segments leading to important 
tourist destinations/circuits which have  been identified for development by the 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.  The Committee would also like to 
know the progress made towards developing wayside amenities on National 
Highways and the extent of private participation therein.    (Para:151) 
 The Committee also recommends setting up a core group comprising 
officers at the level of Joint Secretary of the Ministries of Civil Aviation, Culture, 
Road Transport & Highways, Shipping, Tourism and Railways to regularly 
coordinate on monthly basis , to suggest ways for connecting aspects of potential 
tourist spots and attracting  tourist flow in the country.   (Para:152) 
SAFETY AND SECURITY OF TOURISTS  
 The Committee observes that safety and security of tourists is of vital 
importance as any adverse impression in this regard has serious implications for 
tourist arrivals to the country.  In the past, there have been numerous incidents 
of crime reported against foreign tourists in some popular destinations across the 
country.  In order to make India a s afe tourist destination where tourists would 
feel safe and feel free to move around, the State Governments/ UT 
Administrations of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, 
Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Punjab, 
Rajasthan, Sikkim and Uttar Pradesh have set up tourist police in one form or 
the other.  The Committee recommends that in the light of the security concerns 
at tourist destinations, a committed and professionally trained tourist police 
should be deployed at a ll important destinations of tourist importance so that 
foreign and domestic tourists visiting tourist destinations are assured of their 

 
 
91 
 
safety and security.  The Committee would , therefore, like the Ministry of 
Tourism to take up the matter up with the remaining States/UTs at the highest 
level so that Tourist Police is set up in all important tourist destinations of each 
State/UT of tourist importance.                                                                    (Para:156) 
 The Committee takes note  of the other measures initiated by the Ministry 
of Tourism such as a 24 7 Multi-Lingual Tourist Info -Helpline, adoption of the 
Code of Conduct for ‗Safe and Honourable Tourism,‖ and Guidelines on Safety 
and Security of Tourists to ensure that widespread a wareness on issues related to 
good behaviour towards tourists, civic responsibilities and security and comfort 
of tourists is generated.  The Committee desires to be apprised of the efficacy of 
these measures in bringing about an attitudinal change towards tourists.                 
           (Para:157) 
INDIA TOURISM DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (ITDC) 
 The Committee notes that ITDC has registered a total turnover of Rs. 
371.72 crore in the financial year 2018 -19. It reported a profit before tax (PBT) 
of Rs. 57.91 crore during this period as compared to Rs. 21.25 crore in the 
corresponding period last year, clocking an increase of 63.30 %. It registered 
profit after tax (PAT) of Rs. 42.15 crore compared to 17.71 crore in the previous 
financial year. Since one simple way to determine if a company has a good return 
on equity is to compare it to the average of its industry, the Committee desires to 
be apprised of ITDC's Return on Equity (ROE) and how the same compares with 
the average ROE in the hospitality sector.     (Para:171)  
 The Committee notes that as per the Disinvestment Policy of the 
Government of India, 9 hotel properties including 3 joint venture properties have 
been transferred/handed over to the respective State Governments. The 
Committee observes th at in modern times , the success of hospitality business 
hinges on distribution and digital strategy. Distribution means having a wide 
portfolio of hotels - budget, mid -market, upscale, luxury, etc. - at key 
destinations. By transferring the management of these 9 hotels to St ate 
Governments who will run them as individual units, these hotels will lack the 


 
 
92 
 
distribution strength that all the branded hotel chains - foreign or domestic - 
have been building. The Committee recommends that ITDC should reorient its 
strategy towards ma ximising the revenue by leveraging resources of its existing 
hotels through Public Private Partnership and consolidation of existing 
businesses.               (Para:172) 
 The Committee notes that for the financial year 2019 -20 the revised 
budget estimates for capital outlay was Rs. 17.75 crore which includes renovation 
of Hotel properties and catering units for Rs. 15.80 crore. The Committee 
observes that renovation and upgradation of hotel prope rties is a continuous 
activity. However, as a consequence of D isinvestment, no real attention has been 
given for upgradation and renovation of ITDC's hotel properties. The Committee 
is, therefore, of the considered opinion that in order to remain competitive and 
match the standards of the private players, ITDC would require more funding 
support from the Government of India. Since share capital of ITDC is small and 
not adequate to carry out major capital expenditures and capital ventures, the 
Committee recommends that the Government of India should provide more 
funding support to ITDC by way of equity infusion. The Committee desires to be 
kept apprised of the action taken in its regard.                  (Para:173)     
 The Committee also recommends that ITDC should undertake detailed 
manpower study in all its units/ divisions so that deployment of human resources 
could be rationalized.                            (Para:174)  
MISCELLANEOUS 
 The Committee notes that the Working Group on Tourism of the 12 th Five 
Year Plan , in its Report , had suggested a number of strategies regarding 
development of the tourism sector like infrastructure, connectivity, human 
resource development and capacity augmentation, convergence among various 
agencies at Centre and State level for development of touri sm, taxation, 
incentives and facilitation of tourism sector etc.  The Committee desires to be 
apprised of the extent to which those recommendations have been taken into 

 
 
93 
 
consideration by the Ministry while formulating its Policies and Programmes. 
                                                                                 (Para:175) 
 The Committee feels that each State Government has a responsibility to 
identify and reserve suitable Government land for development of potential 
tourist locations and the l and so reserved should not be used for any other 
purposes other than for constructing hotels, shopping complexes, etc.  The 
Central Government should also play a pivotal role in this regard. Central 
Ministries may also be advised to explore the possibility  of identifying and 
reserving idle land for development of tourist locations.                          (Para:176)  
 In order to promote tourism, the Committee would like the Ministry to act 
as a catalyst for building more amusement/theme parks on the lines  of the Essel 
World, Mumbai and Disneyland, California.  In the coming years, such parks 
may be built in big metropolitan cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and funds 
should be earmarked for the purpose.               (Para:177)
  The progress of implementa tion of projects sanctioned by the 
Ministry should be monitored on a monthly basis by a High Powered Project 
Monitoring Committee  and it should be ensured that the funds released for the 
sanctioned projects do not remain idly parked , but are utilised prod uctively for 
the intended purpose  and a monthly Progress Report  be submitted to the 
Minister for suitable direction, whenever the Projects are lagging behind.  
(Para:178)  
 The Committee notes from the information furnished , that our country 
has targeted to increase its share in global tourist arrivals from the current 
1.24% to 3% and double the number of domestic tourist visits from the current 
1854.9 million to 3200 million visits.  If these ambitious targets are to be met,  the 
country has to create appropriate employable skill in the population and also 
reduce the skill -gap.  The State Governments are major stakeholders in human 
resource and skill development.  The Committee would, therefore, recommend 
that the Ministry in co-ordination with the State Governments , should formulate 
a multipronged approach to bridge the skill gap in the tourism sector and should 

 
 
94 
 
also launch a programme to upgrade the skills of the existing tourist service 
providers.                                                                 (Para:179)  
 The Committee notes that the Scheme of Swadesh Darshan was launched 
with the objective of developing tourist circuits on specific themes and as of now, 
15 such Circuits have been identified for Integrated I nfrastructure Development. 
Since the creation of tourist infrastructure leads to overall economic growth, the 
Committee would like the Ministry to identify more tourism circuits and develop 
them in an integrated manner.                           (Para:180)  
 The Committee notes that there is lack of reasonably priced 
accommodation near the tourist destinations in the country. Expensive 
accommodation is a big deterrent not only for international tourists , but also for 
domestic tourists. The Committee would, therefore, like the Ministry to take up 
with the State Governments , the issue of promotion of Home Stays and earmark 
funds for the same so that the widening gap between supply and demand of the 
accommodation sector could be easily bridged.             (Para:181)
                     
 The Committee notes that most of the international and domestic tourists 
visit enchantingly beautiful Kerala which is famous for its beautiful backwaters, 
unique culture and traditions and rich vegetation. The State is one o f the most 
popular tourist destinations of the world. From the information made available, 
it seems that no major tourism project has been sanctioned for the State of 
Kerala in the recent past.  The Committee, therefore, desires to know whether 
any tourist  project forwarded by the State Government of Kerala for funding 
support from the Ministry of Tourism is pending approval. The Committee also 
recommends that the approval to any such pending projects should be expedited. 
                          (Para:182) 
 The Committee observes that cruise tourism in India is a niche product to 
promote and attract tourists with specific interest. The Committee would, 
therefore, like the Ministry of Tourism to work in coordination with Ministry of 

 
 
95 
 
Shipping towards establi shing dedicated cruise terminals at all the major ports 
and also private ports in the country.                (Para:183)  
 The Roads and Highway networks play an important role in tourism and 
also in the growth of Indian economy. The Committee is aware that the Ministry 
of Road Transport and Highways had taken up detailed review of National 
Highways network with a view to improve the road connectivity to tourist places. 
The Committee desires to be apprised of the progress made so far in this regard.  
                     (Para:184)  
 The Committee recommends that under the PRASHAD, the Ministry 
should develop a dedicated thoroughfare for use by pedestrians visiting 
Srisailam. The Araku Valley and Lambasing in Visakhapatnam has great 
tourism significance and should be developed as tourist spots.  (Para:185)  
 The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministries of Civil Aviation, 
Shipping, Road Transport & Highways, Culture, Tourism and  Railways  are not 
only inter -related and interconnected but also have a common objective to 
improve connectivity and better amenities for the benefit of tourists, travellers 
and faster movement of freight within the country. The Committee, therefore, 
feels that there is a pressing need for having an effective co -ordination 
mechanism among these Ministries so that the policies and guidelines being 
formulated by them are executed seamlessly and can supplement each other in 
achieving these objectives. This will not only increase effectiveness and efficiency, 
but will also help in utilization of funds and skilled manpower to the maximum 
possible extent. Therefore, the Committee recommends that an easy -to-use 
interface should be made available which allows hassl e-free communication and 
co-ordination amongst them. A hotline number which is common to all these 
Ministries, may be established so that whenever emergency arises, there can be 
effective and prompt coordination among these Ministries and issues in hand ca n 
be resolved at the earliest.                                                                   (Para:186) 
 Belum Caves in Kurnool District which are the second largest caves on the 
Indian subcontinent, have immense tourism value and are, therefore, of na tional 

 
 
96 
 
importance.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the above Caves should 
be developed under the  Swadesh Darshan Scheme (SDS).    (Para:187)  
 Since religious tourism is an important segment of domestic tourism, the 
Committee recommends that Kolanu Bharati Saraswati Temple, Mahanandi, 
Ahobilam, Yaganti Uma Maheshwar Temple, Veera Brahman Gaari Matham, 
should be developed under Spiritual Circuit o f Swadesh Darshan Scheme.  The 
Committee also recommends that Mantralayam Raghavendra Swamy Varri 
Temple, Tumblam Jain and Ram Temple and Urukunda Eeranna Temple (Sri 
Narasimha Eranna Swamy Temple) in Kurnool District should be developed 
under PRASHAD Scheme.                   (Para:188) 
 The Committee has come to know that th e State Government of Telangana 
has sent a proposal for development of Alampur - Jagulambha Temple, which is 
one of the Shakti Peethams, located in Telangana. For this, the Committee 
recommends that Telangana's proposal should be considered promptly and that 
the above scheme should be included for its development under PRASHAD 
Scheme.                                                                                                  (Para:189) 
 The Committee notes that an allocation of Rs. 450 Crore has been made in 
BE 2020 -21 under the Scheme of Overseas Promotion and - Publicity for 
promotion of Indian tourism in overseas source markets.  The Committee 
recommends that an audit may be carried out to assess the efficacy of expenditure 
in promoting tourism in overseas source market and it should be ensured that 
value from money is derived from the money spent under the above head. 
                           (Para:190) 
 The Committee recom mends that an audit of the expenditure incurred 
under the various tourism schemes should be conducted to make the 
implementation of these programmes effective so that actual benefits reach the 
intended target groups and delivery systems are improved. Invol vement of Local 
Member of Parliament could add value to the features of various programmes of 
the Ministry.                       (Para:191) 

 
 
97 
 
 The Committee has been informed that the State Government of Arunachal 
Pradesh has forwarded proposals for develop ment of Vismak Nagar, Dibang 
Valley District and Malani Tan, Lower Siang District in Arunachal Pradesh for 
inclusion under the PRASHAD Scheme.  The Committee lends its support for the 
same and recommends their inclusion and development under the PRASHAD 
Scheme.                                                    (Para:192) 
 The Committee also recommends inclusion of Srirangapatna, Melukote, 
Mandya District (Karnataka) for inclusion and development under the 
PRASHAD Scheme.                             (Para:193) 
 The Committee takes note of the submission of the Ministry that no project 
under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme is pending for scrutiny by the Central 
Sanctioning & Monitoring Committee and observes that the above submission is 
factually incorrect.  The Committee has been informed that several proposals sent 
by the State Governments for inclusion under the SDS are pending approval by 
the Ministry of Tourism.  The Committee desires to be furnished with a list of 
such proposals indicating the date of their receipt in the Ministry, action taken 
thereon and shortcomings, if any, noticed.  The Committee also desires to know 
whether the concerned Governments have been informed about the shortcomings 
noticed in this regard.                   (Para:194)  
 The Comm ittee observes that to overcome the aspect of seasonality and 
promote India as a 365 -days tourism destination, it is necessary that the potential 
of adventure tourism is harnessed fully.  To give a fillip to the growth of 
adventure tourism, it is important  that adventure tourism activities like 
paragliding, parasailing, aero -sports including skydive etc. are encouraged.  The 
Committee is, however, constrained to note that no dedicated budgetary provision 
has been made in BE 2020 -21 of the Ministry for promo tion of the above said 
activities.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that sufficient outlay be 
earmarked for the adventure tourism activities including paragliding, parasailing, 
aero sports etc.                                                                                                 (Para:195) 

 
 
98 
 
The Prime Minister has taken keen interest to promote the tourism sector 
of our country globally.  In view of this, the Committee urges that the 
Ambassadors should take the initiative to propagate the idea of the Prime 
Minister of making India a major tourism hub.  The Ministry of External Affairs 
should also post an exclus ive tourism officer in all the E mbassies for doing the 
same.  The Ambassador should also conduct regular meeting s with the 
stakeholders on the measures taken by the Government to promote tourism and 
also direct the officials posted in the E mbassies to make the local public aware of 
the immense pot ential of the country‘s tourism. Committee desires that the 
feedback so received may be sent to  the Secretary, Ministry of Tourism via 
Secretary, Ministry of External Affairs to enable the Tourism Ministry to act on 
the feedback.                    (Para:196)

1 
 
REPORT 
The Ministry of Civil Aviation is responsible for the formulation of national policies 
and programmes for the development and regulation of the Civil Aviation sector in the 
country. It is responsible for the administration of the Aircraft Act, 1934, Aircraft Rules, 
1937 and various other legislations pertaining to the aviation sector in the country. 
2. In addition to primary functions of framing of policies, the Ministry provides 
guidance to the organizations in the implementation of policy guidelines, monitors and 
evaluates their activities and also provides their interface with Parliament. It also supervises 
implementation by the organizations of special programmes of the Government, particularly 
those intended for the weaker sections of society. 
 3. The Ministry of Civil Aviation  has the following organizations under its 
administrative control:- 
(i) Attached Offices /Organizations 
 Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) 
 Bureau of Civil Aviation Authority (BCAS) 
 Commission of Railway Safety (CRS) 
 Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) 
(ii) Autonomous Bodies 
 Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Uran Akademi (IGRUA) 
 Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) 
 Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University (RGNAU) 
(iii) Public Sector Undertakings 
 Airports Authority of India (AAI) 
 Air India Limited (AIL) 
 Pawan Hans Limited (PHL) 
4. The Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism 
and Culture considered Demand No.8 containing the details of budget allocations of the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation for the financial year 2020 -21 at it s meeting held on the 20 th 
February, 2020. During the meeting, the Committee heard the views of the Secretary and 
other senior officers of the Ministry as well as the Heads of the organizations under its 
purview, mainly on budgetary aspects  and incidental aspects relating thereto. 
5. The Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation, while making a presentation before the 
Committee, on Demands for Grants (2020 -21) of the Ministry, mentioned that actual 
investment for this sector comes from airports and airlines. H e added that about 1441.71 lakh 
passengers were carried by domestic airlines during January to December, 2019 as against 
1389.76 lakh during the corresponding period in 2018, indicating an annual growth of 3.74%.

13.2. In its written reply, the Ministry has informed that the Ministry of Finance has not 
provided any reason for less allocation of budget against the projections given by the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation. Due to cut in projected budget for the year 2020 -21, some of the 
activities under Revenue Section  of the Ministry will be affected. In order to meet the 
requirement for the on -going projects of the Ministry, proposals will be taken up in th e first 
Supplementary and RE 2020 -21. In response to a query as to how the Ministry proposes to 
utilize the proposed budgetary allocation, the Secretary, while deposing before the 
Committee, stated that out of Rs. 3480.42 crores (Schemes), Rs. 810.23 crore s will be spent 
for purchase of two VVIP aircrafts, Rs. 2205 crores has been given to Air India for service of 
debts and the rest will be utilized for other activities. 
13.3. The Committee notes that compared to BE 2019 -20 of Rs. 4500 crores and Rs. 
3700 crores at RE 2019-20, Rs. 3797.71 crores has been allocated to the Ministry of Civil 
Aviation for 2020-21.  Elaborating the reasons for the reduction of Rs. 800 crores at RE 
stage, the Secretary clarified that the delivery of two Special Extra Section Fligh t 
(SESF) VVIP aircrafts which were bought through Air India have been rescheduled 
from January, 2020 to June, 2020 and  hence this reduction. The Committee notes that 
the Capital side allocation had remained the same, whereas, on the revenue side , more 
than 50% of allocation is meant for servicing the debt of Air India and Purchase of 2 
VVIP Planes and  the remaining allocation is available for other activities of the 
Ministry.  Keeping in view the security threat prevailing in the aviation sector all over 
the world, the Committee is of the considered view that the inadequacy of budgetary 
allocation would hamper vital activities, such a s installation of body scanners and  
provision of Capital for Rohini Heliport . The Committee feels that it is high time for 
installation of body scanners at all the airports in the country and therefore, fund 
allocation to the Ministry be substantially increased at the R.E. stage for the purpose.

14.1. The savings of Rs.1056.86 crore in Revenue section includes the surrendered amount

received in Capital section through technical supplementary  and therefore, in true sense , the

(Revenue section Rs.1051.52 crore and Capital Section Rs.23.91 crore)  was surrendered on 
29/03/2019. As regards savings for 2019-20, it is stated that the amount provided by Ministry 
of Finance in  RE 2019 -20 is Rs.3700.00 crore against BE 2019 -20  of Rs.4500.00 crore. As 
such, Rs.800.00 crore will be surrendered in the month of February/March-2020. 
14.2. Considering the vital role played by the aviation sector in the growth and 
development of the nation and the growth registered by the aviation industry in the 
recent years, the Committee f ails to understand why the Ministry requires more funds 
when even the allocated fund is not being spent fully both at the B.E. and R.E. stage of 
2019-20, and there is a saving of Rs. 76.80 Crores in the Revenue Section.  The 
Committee desires to know the r easons for such a saving whereas crucial schemes like 
RCS are not being reimbursed fully to AAI.  The Committee, therefore, opines that 
efforts should be made to fully utilize the funds allocated before seeking funds. 
Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) 
15. The Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation, while deposing before the Committee, 
stated thus: 
".....I would like to say that there is a small challenge before us which I would 
like to bring to the notice of the Committee.  This Carbon Offsetting and 
Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) has said that airlines 
pollute.  They burn fuel, so they pollute.  So, this is said that whatever we 
pollute in the year 2020 will become our benchmark, and beyond that, if we 
pollute, we will have to buy carbon credits.  Now, this has serious implications 
for our aviation industry in the sense that we are still a growing industry.  The 
European and American airlines have reached their peak, but we are still 
expanding.  So, we will be capped at a very low level.  In future, when we 
expand, we will have to buy carbon credits.  We have to take this up 
diplomatically.  We are trying to change the entire thing.  At different fora, it 
is being discussed internationally.  I t is our attempt that this has to be 
postponed, but it is a serious concern for the aviation industry in India....".

Shortage of pilots 
26. The following steps have been taken by DGCA to enhance the availability of pilots:- 
(i)  There is the shortage of type r ated commanders in the country due to growth in 
aviation industry and induction of new type of aircraft in the fleet by the airline. Though 
sufficient numbers of Indian Co -pilot are available and employed by the airlines, they do not 
possess the level of s kill and experience the commander s require on the latest fleet of 
aircrafts. To cover the shortage of type rated pilots, validation of foreign pilots is done as per 
Rule 45 of Aircraft Rules, 1937. As per their policy , the expat pilots are phased out by th e 
airlines once the Co-pilots inducted by them become eligible for commander after undergoing 
requisite training for the same . The present policy of hiring foreign pilots by Airlines has 
been extended up to 31.12.2020 by the Central Government. 
(ii)  The c ondition of having flying experience in preceding Five years for issue of 
Commercial Pilot Licence has been done away with by amending Section J of Schedule II of 
The Aircraft Rules, 1937 (containing the requirements for the issue of Commercial Pilot 
Licence) so that more number of aspiring pilots after completing the requisite number of 
flying hrs and undergoing recency and skill test, may now apply for the issue of CPL. 
(iii)   In order to have more number of experienced instructors and examiners with the  
Flying Training Organization (FTO) an amendment in Section Q & R of Schedule II of 
Aircraft Rule 1937 {containing the requirements for the issue of Assistant Flight Instructor 
(AFIR) and Flight Instructor Rating (FIR) respectively} has been carried out. B y easing out 
amendment in Section Q&R, more CPL holder can apply for AFIR & FIR and the shortage of 
Instructors / examiners in FTO will be addressed. Subsequently, after acquiring more 
experience, these Instructors / examiners can apply for FTO. 
(iv)  DGCA has also made provision for conversion of AFIR/FIR Ratings obtained on the 
foreign licence to ensure the availability of more Instructors. 
(v)  DGCA has also amended the flying experience requirements for issue of Airlines 
Transport Pilots Licence (Aeroplane/Helicopter) by amending the Section N &M of Schedule 

18 
 
II of Aircraft Rules, 1937 containing the requirements for the issue of ATPL. By amendments 
in Section M & N more Co -pilots may get ATPL and may become eligible for Pilot -in 
command and more number of defence pilot will become eligible to get ATPL. 
26.1. The Committee notes that  it is a matter of grave concern that the country needs 
about 1000 pilots a year and that around 200 to 300 pilots only are trained, which leads 
to  shortage of type rated commanders in the country. The Committee strongly feels 
that with the huge manpower potential and skilled workforce available in the country, it 
is just a matter of time and effort that these resources are tapped into.

31. As regards the Air Cargo sector, the Ministry has furnished the following details:-

from January, 2020 to June, 2020 and  hence this reduction. The Committee notes that

than 50% of allocation is meant for servicing the debt of Air India and Purchase of 2 
VVIP Planes and  the remaining allocation is available for other activities of the 
Ministry.  Keeping in view the security threat prevailing in the aviation sector all over 
the world, the Committee is of the considered view that the inadequacy of budgetary 
allocation would hamper vital activities, such a s installation of body scanners and  
provision of Capital for Rohini Heliport . The Committee feels that it is high time for

 Considering the vital role played by the aviation sector in the growth and
