CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
MINISTRY 
 
Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1. The Committee notes that RCS has given the Indian aviation industry a huge fillip. This 
Scheme has made air travel more affordable and also the connectivity to remote and hilly 
regions of the country has improved. The Comm ittee notes that availability of funds and high 
cost of operations are the major constraints under the Scheme. The Committee finds that out of 
688 valid routes awarded, only 256 routes have commenced operations, which constitute only 
37% of the awarded rou tes. Despite the fact that the Ministry frequently conducts bidding for 
RCS routes and awards routes, desired progress has not taken place. Given the tremendous 
enthusiastic response from the stakeholders including the passengers and significant change 
noticed in the economic activity of the connected routes with current level of 37% routes, there  
is a huge potential in terms of connectivity and the resultant economic prosperity under the 
Scheme. The Committee, therefore , desires that concerted efforts sho uld be made to 
operationalize all the awarded routes at the earliest. The Committee also desires that periodic 
evaluation of the Scheme be conducted to address the constraints of the issues in 
implementation. 
 
Reply of the Government 
(Recommendation at Para 16.5 of 276th Report) 
1.1. Out of the 688 valid routes awarded, 268 RCS routes have been commenced so far. The 
Selected Airline Operators (SAOs) are obligated to commence RCS flight operations on a RCS - 
route, as part of individual route -proposal or a network proposal within a period of six months 
from the issuance of Letter of Award or within two months from the readiness of airport, 
whichever is later, unless any extension is granted by the Implementing Agency. 
1.2. There is also a mechanism to revi ew the performance of Selected A irline Operators 
(SAO) for RCS routes. RCS -UDAN is regularly monitored for successful implementation. In 
case of wilful default by a Selected Airline Operator (SAO), cancellatio n of routes are done by 
forfeiting the Performance Guarantee/Proposal Security and the routes are offered for rebidding 
in subsequent rounds of bidding. 
1.3. MoCA has therefore been making all possible efforts to operationalize awarded routes 
at the earliest. 
Development of Airport Infrastructure 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2. The Committee exhorts the Ministry to develop a comprehensive, strategic and futuristic 
master plan for the airports in the country, in order to cater to the ever increasing demand for 
new and better airports. 
(Para 17.2)

3  
Reply of the Government 
 2.1. Noted please. 
2.2. The expansion and development of infrastructure facilities at the airports is a continuous 
process and is undertaken on the operational requirements fo r safety of aircraft operation and 
demand from airlines, depending upon availability of land and viability, as well as other facilities 
with reference to intended aircraft operations. 
2.3. AAI has embarked upon a CAPEX plan of Rs. 25000 Crore in next five years for 
development/ upgradation/modernization of various airports in the country to meet the 
requirement of Air Traffic / passengers growth which includes expansions / modification of 
existing terminal, new terminals, expansions / strengthening of exist ing runways, aprons, ANS 
works like control tower, technical block etc. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
3. The Committee is of the view that sufficient parking spots and slots should be made 
available at the airports, in order to increase the efficiency of th e airlines. The Committee urges 
the Ministry to devise viable measures and a robust monitoring policy for attracting more and 
more investment for airport projects. 
(Para 17.3) 
Reply of the Government 
3.1. Development of Apron Parking Bays at Indian Airport s is  a continuous process  based  
on the requirement of the Airlines, slots and procurement of Aircraft. AAI is continuously 
developing Apron Bays considering 5 years horizon. At present there are approximately 705 
aircraft registered with Indian Schedule d carriers. As of now , there are approximately 1335 
aircraft parking bays at Indian Airports including AAI Airports,  JV  airports,  DIAL  and  
MIAL. 
3.2. Further, approximately 550 additionally aircraft Bays are being planned / under 
construction keeping in view the requirement of bays for the next 5 years. After  the  
construction of bays, Indian Airports will have approximately 1885 Aircraft parking bays. 
3.3. Slots at airports to various airlines are allocated  based  on  the  Airport  capacity.  
Airport capacity consists of Runway capacity, Terminal capacity & parking stand capacity. 
Airport capacity can be enhanced by adding new  /improving  existing  infrastructure  along  
with latest technological advancement associated with Runways, parking stands,  Taxiways, 
rapid exit taxiways terminal building etc.  Through  Airport  capacity  enhancement,  no.  of slots 
at airports can be increased, which will benefit both airlines and airports as well. Development of 
Apron Parking Bays at Indian Airports is a continuous process based on the requirement of the 
Airlines, slots and procurement of  Aircraft.  AAI  is  conti nuously developing Apron Bays 
considering 5 years horizon. At present there are approximately 705 aircraft registered with 
Indian Scheduled carriers. 
3.4. As far as attracting investment in the airport sector, Ministry of  Civil  Aviation  has  
been taking  various policy decisions in this direction.  The  Airports  Infrastructure  Policy,  
1997 and the National Civil Aviation Policy, 2016 encourage development of airports by the 

4  
State Governments or the private sector or in PPP mode. Recently, Govt. of India has  
undertaken PPP exercise of six airports of AAI namely, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Mangaluru, 
Jaipur, Guwahati and Thiruvananthapuram. The bidding process  has  been  completed,  and 
three projects i.e., Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Mangaluru have been awarded to the successful 
bidder. Award of remaining three airports is in progress. 
3.5. Further, Greenfield Airports at Durgapur and Kannur have been operationalized with 
private partici pation. Further, Govt. of India  has  granted  'in  principle'  approval  for  
Greenfield Airports at Jewar, Navi Mumbai and Mopa which are being executed under PPP 
mode. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
4. The Committee recommends that while granting approval for new airports, the Ministry 
should ensure that sufficient space is earmarked for commercial shops in the airport. Further, 5 
Star/3 Star hotels and multiplexes should be constructed near the new airports. The Committee 
also desires that extra land, if a ny, should not be sold and should be kept for future 
developmental activities. 
(Para 17.4) 
Reply of the Government 
4.1. The Airports Infrastructure Policy, 1997 put major thrust towards increasing the share 
of commercial revenue emerging from non-aeronautical sources to help in optimal exploitation 
of the full commercial potential of airports and make the airports not only viable but capable of 
generating surpluses for further expansion and development. In the allocation of space 
commercial facilities, airports are required to prepare a Master Plan and follow a strict adherence 
to stipulated procedures, while maintaining sufficient flexibility in order to ensure quality 
products and services and attract the holders of reputed brand -names. Further, the National Civil 
Aviation Policy 2016 prescribes for ‗Hybrid Till‘  framework for economic regulation of airports 
under which 30% of non -aeronautical revenue will be used to cross -subsidise aeronautical 
charges. This framework encourages the airport op erators to maximize the land use potential of 
airport for commercial activities. 
4.2. Thus, the airport developers of new airports have not only freedom but also they get 
incentive for utilizing the airport land for commercial facilities and generate non -aeronautical 
revenue. 
4.3. Further, Airports Authority of India earns revenues from Aeronautical and Non - 
Aeronautical resources. Non -Aeronautical resources include earmarking 10 -15% area of a 
Terminal building for Offices, Retail and F&B. Also city side la nd is leased for non - 
Aeronautical activities as identified in the AAI Act which include hotels, restaurants, warehouses 
etc.

Recommendation/ Observation

Kushinagar Airport have been completed, the ATC Tower and runway lighting are yet to be 
completed. The Committee observes that the claim of the Ministry about the completion of the

Kushinagar - Gaya - Kushinagar - Lucknow.

Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) facilities in India 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
11. The Committee is aware of the huge potential that India has, in offering MRO facilities 
in its soil. It is a sad fact that India could not fully exploit the opportunities available in this 
sector. MRO, being a sunrise industry, and with our huge technical  and skill base, by creating a 
congenial environment, India can easily meet the requirements of the sector. By giving boost to 
this sector, new employment opportunities can be created for our fresh engineering students.  
The Committee, therefore, strongly feels that the Ministry should give adequate and immediate 
focus on the issues faced in the MRO sector and chalk out strategic measures to make positive 
interventions in order to ensure that India becomes a key player in offering MRO facilities. This 
will also help in achieving the Prime Minister’s vision of attaining 5 trillion dollar economy. 
(Para 30.1) 
Reply of the Government 

8  
11.1. The Government has taken up further improvements in policy, taxation and regulatory 
regime. The roadmap h as been developed in consultation with MRO industry for realizing self -
sufficiency in this vital and strategic aviation segment, which includes upgrading the 
demonstrated airframe capacity and setting up component and engine MROs in India. Reciprocal 
acceptance of air safety certificates between Indian and overseas regulators has also been taken 
up. Convergence between Defence sector and the civil MROs would be established to create 
economies of scale and maintenance costs for airlines would be brought down  including through 
rationalisation of royalty charged for MROs at airports. 
11.2. The implementation of the roadmap would act as a catalyst for future growth towards a 
well-developed Indian MRO ecosystem which will help in leveraging India‗s engineering 
advantage, a step towards achieving higher self -reliance in airline operations and Make-in- India. 
It will also help nurture R&D besides creating MRO training infrastructure, skills development, 
and churning out more jobs for the youth of India.  Commensurate with the airlines‘  fleet growth 
over time, the size of India aviation MRO is estimated by industry to grow annually from an 
estimated Rs. 13,500 crore in 2019 -20 to Rs. 21,600 crore in the  next five years, with domestic 
MRO contributing a higher proportion of about Rs. 5,000 crore. 
11.3. In pursuance of the roadmap, the tax regime for MROs has been substantially 
rationalized as below: 
(a) Import Duty has been exempted on Special Tools and Equipment for MRO. 
(b) Customs duty waived that applied to spares only for Airlines extended to MRO. 
(c) Aircraft brought into country for MRO allowed to stay from 1 month to 6 months 
without penalties. 
(d) Spares purchased for MRO can be consumed upto 36 months (up from 12 months) 
from time of landing in India. 
(e) GST on Domestic MRO reduced from 18% to 5% w.e.f. 1st April, 2020. 
(f) Sub-contracted transactions to domestic MRO by foreign MRO now treated  as 
exports with zero-rated GST w.e.f. 1st April, 2020. 
Air Cargo sector 
Recommendation/ Observation 
12. The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry unveiled its National Air Cargo Policy 
in January, 2019 which includes some good initiatives like the first -in-world dedicated Air  
Flight corridors between India -Afghanistan which is proposed to be extended to all and land - 
locked countries in a phased manner. The Committee would like the Ministry to initiate concrete 
actions in that direction, for it will encourage code sharing/interline agreements between  
foreign and Indian carriers. 
(Para 31.1) 

9  
12.1. The Committee is of the view that India has  a huge untapped market potential in the 
sector and it is high time to bring about policy and structural changes aimed towards 
transparency and paperless trade environment in this sector. 
(Para 31.2) 
Reply of the Government 
12.2. (a) Growth of air cargo is  critical for industries such as e -commerce, pharmaceuticals, 
electronics, agriculture, horticulture, floriculture, animal husbandry and marine exports, 
and high -value goods, including gems and jewellery and fashion garments, where 
shipments are highly time-sensitive. 
(b) High air cargo growth of 9.3% (CAGR) has been achieved during last five years 
compared to hardly any growth the preceding years. India‗s air cargo growth exceeded 
global growth during this period. During FY 2018-19, total air cargo handled reached to 
3.57 million MT comprising domestic air cargo of 1.36 million and international air 
cargo of 2.20 million MT. Domestic and international cargo grew annually by 12.1% 
and 2.6%, respectively. Indian air express and courier industry is one of the fast est 
growing markets globally. Growth is estimated at 17% CAGR during the last five years. 
Entry of e-commerce giants in air cargo business is expected to give further impetus to 
its growth. 
(c) Government has taken several initiatives to sustain the growth impetus in air cargo by 
way of cost reduction, efficiency improvement and better inter -ministerial coordination, 
and to bring the country‗s logistics on a par with global standards. These include, inter 
alia, the following: 
 
A. Infrastructure Creation/ Upgradation: 
(i) 23 Common User Domestic Cargo Terminals (CUDCTs) and 20 International Cargo 
Terminals (CUTs) made operational by Airport Authority of India (AAI) through its 
wholly-owned subsidiary, the AAI Cargo Logistics and Allied Services Ltd. (AAICLAS). 
Both d omestic and international cargo terminals are also developed and operated at JV 
airports (Bengaluru, Cochin, Delhi, Hyderabad and Mumbai). 
(ii) AAICLAS has taken up a time -bound programme for developing air cargo facilities 
(including X -Ray machines) at unserve d airports and upgrading existing facilities at 
underserved airports as per commercial and other considerations.

16.1. (a) In a landmark initiative to create new business and top jobs for India's banking, non -

Affairs, Financial Services, Corporate Affairs, Commerce), and Regulators (IRDAI, RBI, 
DGCA). It also carried out a detailed study and 360 -degree review of current regulatory 
framework affecting aircraft financing, identified challenges/barriers and recommended their 
potential solutions. It thus recommended a detailed roadmap along with an implementation action 
plan for developing aircraft financing and leasing as an asset class from institutional investors in

13  
based airlines along with other key stakeho lders during the Aviation Conclave 2019 on 27

Delhi organised by the Ministry i n association with foreign lessors/asset managers on 20 August

emphasized on the significant business of aircraft financing and leasing activities : “As the 
world’s thi rd largest domestic aviation market, the time is ripe for India to enter into aircraft 
financing and leasing activities from Indian shores. This is critical to the development of a self -

elements of the regulatory roadmap for making India a hub for such activities”. 
(e)  Implementation of this mandate has been taken up through the Task Force on IFSC 
chaired by HMOS (Finance) and Group of Secretaries chaired jointly by DEA and MOCA. 
(f)  A detailed proposal for amending the Gujarat SEZ  Act to provide specific exemption 
from payment of Stamp Duty on instruments executed in connection with aircraft financing/ 
leasing transactions from India‘ s IFSC has also been taken up with the State Government. In 
principle decision already taken to exempt stamp duties by Government of Gujarat. 
(g) Some tax concessions have already been provided to create an enabling ecosystem for such 
financing and leasing activities an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC), notably, to

profit which has been accumulated by the unit after 1 st April, 2017 from operations in

additional tax on distribution of any amount, on or after 1 September 2019, by  a

computing tax liability in respect of income of the nature of interest, dividend etc.

Faulty Engines 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
17. The Committee is satisfied with the action taken by the Ministry. At the same time, the 
Committee recommends that the Ministry should ensure that the airlines may purchase engines 
which have been in the  market for a stipulated, reasonable period of time with credentials of 
international safety standards. The Committee also desires that AAIB should assess the reasons 
for such engine failure and recommend suitable remedial measures. The Committee desires t he 
Ministry to frame safety standards/ protocols in aircraft operations. 
(Para 37.1) 
Reply of the Government 
17.1. Airbus A320 Neo aircraft fitted with two PW1100 series engines are operated by M/s 
Indigo Airlines and M/s Go Air. M/s Indigo Airlines induct ed their first A320 Neo aircraft in 
March 2016 and at present have a total of 106 aircraft in their fleet. M/s Go Air inducted their 
first A320Neo aircraft in May 2016 and presently have 43 aircraft in their fleet. More than 574 
such aircraft are operating globally. 
1. PW 1100 engines are manufactured by M/s Pratt and Whitney (P&W), USA. The engine 
has been type certified by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) of USA, the 
regulatory authority of the State of Design and subsequently by European Aviation Safety 
Agency (EASA). 

15  
2. Post induction of the aircraft into service, technical issues were experienced on these 
engines worldwide. Most of these issues have been suitably addressed by the 
manufacturer except high N2 Vibration and 3rd Stage Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) 
failures, which is being addressed by making suitable modifications during shop visits of 
the engines. 
3. As a final mitigation, modified engines with new 3rd stage LPT blades are being installed 
on the aircraft. 
4. DGCA has directed both the airlines to take following proactive measures in the interest 
of safety: 
(i) Record, monitor and inspect engines if Vibration is reported to be more th an 3CU (as 
against manufacturer‘s guideline of 5CU). 
(ii) Restricting operation of A320 Neo aircraft with P& W engines to Port Blair. 
(iii) Extended Diversion Time Operation (EDTO) for Airbus Neo aircraft has not 
been allowed by DGCA. 
(iv) All new inductions of A320/321 neo aircraft after August 2019 must be installed with 
engines having modified 3rd stage LPT. 
(v) No un-modified engine from MROs shall be accepted after September 2019. 
5. Subsequent to four Air Turn Back (ATB)/ Inflight Shut Down (IFSD) events witnessed in 
a week in October 2019, following additional measures have been taken: 
(i) DGCA reviewed the failure pattern which indicated that the failures were experienced on 
engines which had accumulated more than 2900 Flight hours. To enhance safety of 
operations, DGCA directed both the airlines to operate only those aircraft which had at 
least one modified engine, if the o ther engine had accumulated more than 2900 Flight 
Hours. The directive stands compiled by both the airlines. 
(ii) Further, in view of the fact that more number of events related to LPT failures were 
reported on engines of Indigo fleet (22 in case of Indigo & 4 in case of Go Air, as on 
date), DGCA directed M/s IndiGo for replacement of unmodified engines with modified 
engines on its entire fleet by 31st January 2020. In compliance, the operator and the 
manufacturer have taken steps to expedite replacement of unmodified engines. 
(iii) DGCA‗s stand has been acknowledged by Federal Aviation Administration of US and 
European Aviation Safety Agency, who have also committed to the replacement of 
unmodified engines. It involved procurement of about 200 engines. 
(iv) Considering the logistical challenges involved in replacing this unexpected demand of 
large number of engines and after ensuring that at least one modified engine has  been 
placed on all the aircraft, irrespective of the flight hours accumulated, DGCA has 
extended  the t imeline for complete removal of unmodified engine to 31 st May, 2020 
from earlier mandated 31st January, 2020. 
6. The schedule of replacement of engines has been adversely affected due to global 
lockdown. At present a total of 57 unmodified engines are install ed on aircraft of M/S 
Indigo fleet and 22 unmodified engines are installed on aircraft of M/s Go Air fleet. 

16  
7. M/s P & W is in the process of setting up an MRO in India in collaboration with M/S Air 
India for replacement of 3rd stage LPT at their Mumbai facility. This will significantly 
reduce the time taken for the upgrade. The facility was expected to be operational by the 
end of February 2020, however due to COVID 19 Pandemic, the process of restoration is 
likely to be completed upon normalcy post global lock down. 
8. DGCA is consistently monitoring the performance of these engines operated by Indian 
operators and taking mitigation actions to ensure safe operation of aircraft. Many of the 
issues have been addressed by taking suitable mitigatio n actions, by DGCA and the 
manufacturer.

Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) 
Recommendation/ Observation 
3. The Committee notes that a serious challe nge is awaiting the nation, in the ever 
expanding aviation industry, after 2020 i.e., with regard to buying of carbon credits. As more 
and more areas are connected and expansion takes place, Ministry will have to buy a lot of 
carbon credit, which will invo lve huge financial implications. Under these circumstances, the 
Committee desires the Ministry to have a study of the financial implications involved for future 
expansion of our aviation sector which is presently at a nascent stage, but has a huge potentia l 
for further expansion. The Committee also calls upon the Ministry to take up, this issue 
diplomatically as well as politically, at the highest possible level, to sort it out as early as 
possible so as to secure the future of our civil aviation industry. 
(Para 15.1) 
Reply of the Government 
3.1.   1. It   is   true   that   a   scheme   called   ‗Carbon   Offsetting   and   Reduction   Scheme   
for International Aviation (CORSIA)‘  has been established by the International Civil Aviation 
Organisation (ICAO). The Scheme will commence operation from 2021 in a voluntary form 
which will last till 2026. From 2027 till 2035, it will run in mandatory form for all countries and 
collectively cover around 89% of total international aviation emissions. It will be further 
extended after a review. It provides for a global carbon offsetting mechanism under which the 
international  aeroplane  operators  will  be  required  to  purchase  and  cancel  ‗emissions  units‘ 
(carbon credits) to offset the increase in CO2 emissions covered by the scheme using the average 
annual emissions of 2019 and 2020 as reference. The Scheme lays down a formula for 
calculating the offsetting requirement of individual aeroplane operators. 
2. The Indian carriers will not be required to undertake any offsetting obligations until end of 
2026 since India has chosen not to join the Scheme in the voluntary phase (Pilot Phase 2021 - 
2023 and First Phase 2024 -2026). But from the b eginning of 2027, when the mandatory phase 
begins, India will have to join the Scheme as a member State of ICAO, and its carriers will be 
bound by the offsetting requirements and will have to buy carbon credits from approved sources 
to meet their obligations. 
3. A study has been commissioned by TERI (The Energy and Resources Institute) to assess the 
challenges posed by CORSIA for the air transport sector of India and the impact of CORSIA on 
the Indian airline industry. The first report is expected by the end of October, 2020. 
4. Even though India is committed to addressing the issues of climate change and environmental 
protection, India holds the view that CORSIA is unfair to developing countries like India and is 
also in some respects not in sync with the  UNFCCC. Accordingly, at the 40th ICAO Assembly 
session held in September/October 2019, India raised its concerns through a working paper but 
the updated Resolution on CORSIA was still adopted without any change since there was 

27  
inadequate support for India‗s stand. Still, India has filed its reservations to the Resolution in 
writing. 
5. ICAO has kept a provision for conducting review of the implementation of CORSIA every 3 
years, starting from 2022. In order to present the views of India s trongly and in a concerted 
manner to the ICAO Council during the proposed review in 2022, a Group of Secretaries 
consisting of Secretary, Civil Aviation as Convenor and Secretaries of M/o Environment, Forest 
& Climate Change, External Affairs and Petroleum  and Natural Gases as members, has been 
formed to develop a strategy to take forward the campaign for getting suitable changes in the 
design elements of CORSIA approved by ICAO. The Group has held one meeting in March, 
2020 at which the following points were deliberated: 
a) The proposal to shift the baseline year closer to 2027 needs to be firmly put forth for 
consideration under review of CORSIA scheme. To make the stand stronger, India is 
seeking the support of all states joining CORSIA scheme from 2027 on t he proposal of 
shifting the baseline year. In the recently held 11th BRICS Summit, the issue of CORSIA 
was discussed with the BRICS countries and consensus was built amongst them to work 
together on the review process of the CORSIA framework. 
b) The principle of attributing responsibility of emission reduction to Member  States instead 
of airline operators should be put forth as this will provide a more balanced and fair 
regime for States having large traffic volume of their own but relatively smaller airlines  
vis-à-vis States having low traffic volumes of their own but large airlines. Efforts should 
be made to  relate the emissions of a country to the total international flights from that 
country irrespective of the nationality of airlines operating such flights. 
c) Fast tracking the project for production of indigenous bio -fuels at commercially viable 
cost and to ensure that it meets the ICAO standards for sustainable alternative fuel so that 
the Indian airlines get the benefit of using such fuel under CORSIA scheme. 
d) Exploring diplomatic ways to elicit support of other countries for the above initiatives. 
6. However, due to the onset of the COVID -19 pandemic, the entire focus of the Government 
shifted to the contingency measures required to control the spread of epidemic in the country, and 
therefore, it has not been feasible to hold further meetings of the Group of Secretaries. But efforts 
will be made to organize the next meeting as early as possible. At this meeting, the  impact of 
COVID-19 on the CORSIA scheme  will also be discussed. As international air travel has been 
suspended or drastically reduced by most of the countries, there will be a massive reduction of 
carbon emissions for the year 2020. Hence, CO2 emissions from international civil aviation if 
calculated using the average annual emissions between 2019 and 2020, would result in an 
abnormally lower baseline and lead to higher offsetting requirements for aeroplane operators than 
previously anticipated. It is learnt that this development is being considered by ICAO presently. 
7. The Ministry of Civil Aviation is continuously monitoring the developments at ICAO 
through the Representative of India posted at ICAO in Montreal and efforts are being made to 
project our views at the Council meetings with the su pport of like -minded members of the 
Council. 
 
Further Recommendation/ Observation 

28  
3.2. The Ministry, in its reply, has accepted that there will be deleterious effect on the 
financial health of the Indian carriers operating to foreign dest inations due to the present 
structure of CORSIA, wherein Indian carriers are hardly in any position to ramp up their

The Ministry has indicated that TERI will be assessing the challenges posed by CORSIA

Annexure-I 
 
 
The Terms of Reference (ToR) of the Committee are as under: 
1. Strengthening of the Commission of Railway Safety in order to make its functioning more 
effective and autonomous and with respect to various functions as laid down in Railway 
Act‗1989. 
2. To examine the feasibility of combining the investigating functions and to develop mechanism 
for sharing the best practices and knowledge pool pertaining to accidents concerning the Civil 
Aviation, Railways, Shipping and Oil Sector. 
3. To define a well laid down Inspection Protocol to be followed by IR in case of preventive 
inspections and Accident Investigation as these are well defined duties specified in the Railway 
Act. 
4. Skill upgradation and regular training for the officials involved in technical functions of the 
Commission. 
5. To examine the Recommendations and its implementation related to functioning of Commission 
of Railway Safety as proposed by various Committees and Commissions to examine safety on 
Indian Railways (IR) formed over the years by the Govt. of India. 
6. To suggest suitable Legislation to eliminate duality of Command as CRS is under administrative 
control of MoCA and doing the work of IR. 
7. To examine the stage of implementation of various recommendations given by the 
Commissioners in their Accident Inquiry Report with view to make it more transparent and 
visible so that the accepted recommendations are rolled out in a time bound manner. 
8. To suggest measures to minimize instances of unilateral changes in various Rules, Codes and 
Manuals etc by IR without any consultation with the Commission.

CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
ANNUAL PLAN 2019-20 
Sharp reduction at RE 2019-20 stage  
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee observes that the Ministry has been allocated Rs. 2547.00 crore at RE 
2019-20 stage as against Rs. 3042.35 crore at B.E. 2019 -20 which is a huge reduction of 
over 16%. The Committee observes that many of the projects/activities carried out by the 
Ministry of Culture, if postponed to a future date, will cause irreparable damage to the 
cultural herit age of our country. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry 
may ensure that the available funds are  utilized in an efficient manner, without rushing 
expenditure at the end of a Financial Year.  
      (Para 13) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 Ministry ensured the utilization of available funds in efficient manner without 
expenditure rushing at year end. Ministry re -prioritized its programmes/ activities and 
accommodated them within the reduced allocation. 
 
ANNUAL PLAN (2020-21) 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee observes that while the Ministry had projected a demand of Rs. 
4323.61 crore for 2019-20, a demand of only Rs. 3857.50 crore has been projected for BE 
2020-21. The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for the substantial reduction in the 
projected requirement of the Ministry, even when there had been a reduction of almost Rs. 
500 crores at RE stage in 2019 -20. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may plead 
the cases of such schemes/projects for higher allocations at RE stage in 2020 -21 so that the 
projects are not stalled due to paucity of funds. 
  (Para 26) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1 The projection for 2019-20 was keeping in view the various commemorations such as 
Celebration of 150 th Birth Anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, releasing various payments 
which remained due for the previous year’s commemorations such as payment to NBCC for 
construction of Pt. Deendayal Institute of Archaeology at Greater NOIDA, etc. The Ministry 
will certainly make efforts for higher allocation depending on the expenditure status at RE 
2020-21 so that the projects may not be stalled due to paucity of funds during the year. 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 

3 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee is happy to note that ASI has received a 20% higher allocation at BE 
2020-21 stage compared to the Rs. 1036.41 crore allocation made at BE 2019 -20 and hopes 
that the increased allocation will enable the organization to fulfill its mandate mor e 
efficiently. However, taking into account that 3691 monuments come under the protection of 
ASI, even the increased allocation for protection and conservation appears very meagre. The 
Committee hopes that this pattern of a noticeable increase in the alloc ation made to ASI will 
continue in the coming years so that tangible cultural heritage of our country stays in good 
condition for generations to come. 
  (Para 31) 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1 The Ministry has to work out the modalities to distribute the budgetary allocation 
among its organizations which include attached /subordinate offices and autonomous bodies. 
ASI being a large organization and an attached office of the Ministry is generally allocated 
around one-third of the budget of the Ministry. For  2020-21, the allocation has been kept at 
1246.75 crore for ASI. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee nevertheless appreciates the progress made by ASI in utilization of 
funds to the extent of 89.8% of Rs. 1001.77 crore allotted at RE stage in 2019-20.  
  (Para 32) 
Reply of the Ministry 
4.1 The ASI utilized the funds amounting to Rs. 1002.46 crore during 2019-20, which is 
100.07% of the provisions made in the RE 2019-20. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
5. The Committee notes that the BE 2020 -21 allocation under the Capital Head for ASI 
is five times the allocation made at RE stage in 2019 -20. The Committee hopes that ASI 
would be able to make full use of the enhanced allocation so that the planned 
construction/acquisition activities are completed on time. 
  (Para 35) 
Reply of the Ministry 
5.1 The enhanced allocation under Capital Head may be utilized by the ASI as per the 
MOF monthly / quarterly expenditure Ceilings during the FY 2020-21. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
6. The Committee appreciates the e -ticketing initiative of the ASI and desires that this 
initiative should be extended to all monuments at the earliest. 

4 
 
  (Para 41) 
Reply of the Ministry 
6.1 The E-ticketing has been implemented at all the ticketed monuments. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
7. The Committee desires that top priority should be given to excavation and 
conservation of ancient remains of the Stone Age. 
  (Para 45) 
Reply of the Ministry 
7.1 The recommendation of Committee has been noted. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
8. The Committee also urges that the field offices of ASI should pursue such cases of 
encroachment persistently with the District Authorities on urgent basis and chalk a way out 
in such cases. The Committee also underlines the need for adequate follow up of the cases 
filed in Court of law against the encroachers. 
  (Para 47) 
Reply of the Ministry 
8.1 For removal of encroachments, the Superintending Archaeologist in charge of the 
Circles has been vested with the powers of an Estate Officer to issue eviction notices/orders 
to the encroachers under Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act,  1971. 
They are also delegated with the powers to issue notices under the provisions of Ancients 
Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 and Rules 1959   followed by 
an order to the District Collector/Magistrate by Central Government to re move such 
encroachment under Section 19 of the Act. Assistance in containing and removing 
encroachments is also sought from the   respective State Government/police force. 
8.2 In most of the cases, defaulter seeks shelter in Court of Law against Notice or 
Demolition Order issued. Such cases are regularly monitored by Superintending 
Archaeologist of Circle Office with the help of Central Government Standing Counsels. 
 
NATIONAL MISSION ON LIBRARIES 
Recommendation/Observation 
9. The Ministry’s decision not to approve the Mission beyond March, 2020 appears 
questionable when proposals have still not been received from 11 State Governments/UTs. 
The Committee recommends that NML may be extended for another year and the Ministry 
may write to State Governments which have not submitted proposals for the National Mission 
on Libraries, to submit the same so that the objective of the Missions gets complete. 
Additional funds under the head may be requested at Revised Estimates stage in 2020-21. 

5 
 
  (Para 59) 
Reply of the Ministry 
9.1 Ministry has requested state libraries to send proposals and accordingly fund will be 
provided in the RE 2020-21, to meet up the demand. Third Party Evaluation of the scheme is 
being done and the Scheme will be modified and extended accordingl y. The  interim 
extension has already been granted to all the Centre Sector / Centrally Sponsored schemes, 
including NML till the report of 15th FC come into effect. 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF MUSEUMS 
Recommendation/Observation 
10. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may consider holding quarterly 
meeting for selection of new beneficiaries under the ‘Museums Grant Scheme’. The 
Committee feels that this would allow the Ministry to spread its expenditure over the year, 
while reducing the waiting time for the applicants applying for the scheme. 
  (Para 69) 
Reply of the Ministry 
10.1 The suggestion of the Committee is noted by the Ministry. 
 
ANTHROPOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
Recommendation/Observation 
11. The Committee observes that Anthropological Survey of India is doing a 
commendable job of its kind. The functions performed by it assume great significance, 
especially to tribal communities. The Committee feels that the AnSI should coordinate with 
the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and provide inputs in policy making for the welfare of tribal 
communities based on its findings from studies and surveys. 
  (Para 75) 
Reply of the Ministry 
11.1 The AnSI  has begun working in collaboration with Ministry of Tribal Affairs 
(MoTA). In this regards, two meetings were held with the Secretary, MoTA in the year 2019 -
20 and it has been agreed that AnSI would conduct study of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal 
Groups ( PVTGs) of India as desired by MoTA. The Project would be funded by MoTA. 
Further, MoTA has recognised AnSI has centre of excellence in the areas of Tribal study. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
12. The Committee is happy to note that the AnSI  has been able to utilize 88.3% of the 
funds allocated to it under the Revenue Head up to January, 2020. The Committee is, 
however, distressed to note that even after facing a 63.6% reduction at the RE 2019 -20 stage 
under the Capital Head, AnSI has only be en able to spend 72.7% of the reduced RE 2019 -20 

6 
 
allocation of Rs. 4.00 crores. This constraint in utilization of funds requires AnSI to strive 
hard to utilize the higher Capital allocation for completion of the construction work of its 
Head Office and Sub-Regional Centres. 
  (Para 76) 
Reply of the Ministry 
12.1 AnSI was in constant touch with CPWD authority for utilization of funds allocated by 
the Ministry to its highest extent and as a result AnSI  has been able to utilise 99.12% of the 
RE during the financial year 2019 -20. The construction work of new office building of Head 
Office at Salt Lake campus, Kolkata is almost complete except some minor works, 
landscaping and payment of pending bills. AnS i will try to ensure that construction of Head 
Office Building is completed in all respect during the year 2020-21. 
 
CENTENARIES AND ANNIVERSARIES, CELEBRATIONS AND SCHEMES 
Recommendation/Observation 
13. The Committee welcomes steps taken to commemorate the above mentioned eminent 
personalities of our country. However, the Ministry may have to request the Ministry of 
Finance for higher allocation under this head at RE 2020 -21 stage to meet the liabilities for 
the year 2020-21. 
  (Para 88) 
Reply of the Ministry 
13.1 For the year 2020 -21, the Ministry has kept a fund provision of Rs. 160.35 crore for 
the pending liabilities and future activities to be undertaken during the year. The allocation 
under this head is 45.36% higher than the previous FY 2019 -20 BE allocation which was Rs. 
110.00 crore. 
 
GLOBAL ENGAGEMENT AND INTERNATIONAL CO-OPERATION 
Recommendation/Observation 
14. Appreciating the proposed Festivals of India, to be held in 8-10 countries in FY 2020-
21, the Committee recommends the Ministry to seek higher allocation under this head at RE 
2020-21 stage. 
  (Para 92) 
Reply of the Ministry 
14.1 As per the recommendation of the Committee, Ministry will strive for additional 
funds at RE 2020 -21 depending upon the number of proposals for organizing the  Festival of 
India. 
 
SUPPORT TO AKADEMIES 
Recommendation/Observation 

7 
 
15. The Committee is happy to note the new initiatives planned by the Ministry for the FY 
2020-21. The Committee hopes that the enhanced budget allocation of Rs. 434.58 crore at BE 
2020-21 stage will be optimally utilized by the three Akademies. The Committee would like to 
be updated on these initiatives and request the Ministry to furnish the status of fund 
utilization on quarterly basis. 
  (Para 96) 
Reply of the Ministry 
15.1 The academies are utilizing the grants optimally. The fund release is being made as 
per the MOF monthly / quarterly expenditure ceilings a nd accordingly the akademies have

RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE HIGH POWERED COMMITTEE 
Recommendation/Observation 
16. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may review the fund requirements of 
the Akademies, which has not been increased in several years. The Committee is of the view

accordingly, projected requirements should be arrived at. 
  (Para 101)

16.1 While providing the grant to Ministry, MoF makes certain restrictions to allocate

will try to do so. 
 
SUPPORT TO LIBRARIES 
Recommendation/Observation 
17. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Culture should make efforts to work 
seriously for modernization and networking of libraries, resource sharing, training of 
professional staff and strengthening of libraries at local level. 
  (Para 105) 
Reply of the Ministry 
17.1 This Ministry provides grants to four (4) Autonomous Body Libraries, viz. RRRLF, 
DPL, KBOPL and RRL under “Support to Libraries”.  
17.2 Besides, Under “Development of Libraries”, National Mission on Libraries (NML) 
scheme is being implemented, with its four (4) components, namely: 
a. National Virtual Library of India (NVLI),(now Indian Culture Portal) 

8 
 
b. Setting up of Model Libraries, 
c. Capacity Building and  
d. Quantitative & Qualitative Survey of Public Libraries in India 
17.3 RRRLF is the implementing agency for  the component (b), (c) and (d). The “Setting 
up of Model Libraries” component of NML envisages providing Financial Assistance to one 
State Central Library and one District Library in each State / UT as recommended by the 
State/ UT Authority & 6 Libraries under MOC. Under this component, provisions are there 
for modernization and networking of libraries.  
17.4 The “Capacity Building” component of NML envisages providing training to Library 
professionals to upgrade their professional skills as well as to apprise them with the latest 
technology. 
17.5 Apart from the above, the development of public libraries is a State subject as per the 
Seventh Schedule under Article 246 of Constitution of India. However, RRRLF provides 
some financial assistance only to var ious public libraries under various matching and non -
matching schemes and also provides professional skills as well to apprise them with the latest 
technology.

ARTISTS PENSION SCHEME AND WELFARE FUND 
Recommendation/Observation 
22. The Committee appreciates the initiatives taken by the Ministry to ensure timely 
disbursal of the Artistes Pension. 
  (Para 146) 
Reply of the Ministry 
22.1 Ministry of Culture through the Artist Pension Section is ensuring timely disbursal of 
Artistes Pension, on the basis of receipt of requisite document from the pensioner.  
22.2  For guiding the artists for getting artists pension as well as to know details  of other 
schemes administered by Ministry of Culture including the procedure, nodal agency, 
helpdesks have been created in all seven Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCC) and Performing Arts 
Bureau.  

10 
 
22.3 As per the guidelines of Artists Pension Scheme minimum of Rs. 500 from State/UT 
contribution is mandatory, thereby State s are also advised to guide the Artistes for getting 
Pension from the Central Government. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
23. The Committee desires to know the reasons for not holding even a single meeting to 
process the applications in 2015 -16 and 2016 -17. The Committee feels that the Ministry 
cannot afford to keep artistes’ applications for pension, pending for years. The Ministry 
should ensure that regular meetings are held to update the list of b eneficiaries entitled for 
pension under the scheme of the Ministry. 
  (Para 148) 
Reply of the Ministry 
23.1 It has been decided then to carry out the physical verification of the existing pensioner 
to assess their authenticity as an Artist before holding the Expert Committee meeting in 
2015-16. The physical verification of pensioner was a lengthy exercise and he nce meeting 
could not be held in 2015 -16. However, all the proposals of the year 2015 -2016 and 2016-17 
were added to the meeting in the year 2017 -18 and recommended artistes were included in 
the list of beneficiaries. This Ministry is taking care of holdin g of Expert Committee Meeting

Recommendation/Observation 
12. The Committee is concerned to note that out of Rs. 42.78 crore allocated for Cultural

Mission, to produce a database of tangible as well as intangible cultural assets in the

Reply of the Ministry

standard format. Bulk data upload facility is provided. 
(ii) Letters have been sent to Chief Sec retaries of all States/UTs with request to 
supply artists’ data base to the Mission online.

monuments. The Committee strongly recommends that the NMA may come up with an 
effective plan of action to draft and finalize the HBLs for all monuments across the country. 
  (Para 161) 
Reply of the Ministry 
26.1 Section 20E of AMASRA Act prescribes the procedure for drafting Heritage Bye -
Laws for the CPMs/Sites. The Act envisages that 5 Regional Directors of ASI, declared as 
Competent Authority, shall prepare Heritage Bye -Laws (HBLs) in respect of each protected 
Monument and protected area in consultation with expert heritage bodies. 
26.2 Secondly, ASI is required to prepare the detailed site plan of each CPM/Site as 
prescribed in Section 20E (3). The site plan forms part of Schedule 1 of the Bye -Laws. The 
AMASRA Rules, 2011 prescribed time limit of 5 years for prepara tion of site plan of all the 
3691 monuments/sites. The time limit has now been extended by another 5 years. However, 
the site plans have still not been finalised for majority of the monuments. Regional Directors 
of ASI are regularly working on preparation of Heritage Bye -laws and sending it to NMA. 
NMA has to complete the formalities at their ends and then place it in the Parliament. 
26.3  The draft Heritage Bye -Laws are also required to be published through website 
inviting comments of public, which are re quired to be resolved before finalizing the Bye -
Laws, which is also time-consuming process. 
26.4  In view of the above NMA finds it very difficult to finalize the Heritage Bye -Laws at 
the required pace. 

38 
 
26.5 In addition to 5 HBLs already approved 44 draft  HBL covering 57 CPMs are under 
consideration. 
26.6 33 Draft Heritage Bye -Laws covering 38 CPMs have been sent back for clarification 
to Regional Directors 
Further recommendation/observation: 
26.7  The Committee understands that preparing the detailed site  plan and Heritage 
Bye-Laws for all the 3691 monuments/sites is an enormous task . The Committee 
recommends that the NMA may convey its staffing/budgetary requirements to allow 
this process to be carried out parallelly for monuments across the country, to M inistry 
of Culture and take effective measures to complete this important task at the earliest.

Indian Institute of Heritage and Conservation

Heritage and Conservation on priority, to meet the shortage of skilled manpower in several

27.1 Proposal for setting up an Indian Institute of Heritage &  Conservation is being taken

Institute of Archaeology, National Arch ives, IGNCA, National Research Laboratory for 
Conservation of Cultural Property (NRLC) etc. 
27.2  Concept is under preparation.  
Further recommendation/observation: 
27.3  The Committee recommends that the Ministry should expedite 
concretization and implementation of the proposal for setting up the Indian Institute of 
Heritage and Conservation. The Committee desires to be updated in this regard.

ANNUAL PLAN 2019-20 
Quarter-wise Expenditure Details of 2019-20 
The Committee notes that the reasons for the slow pace of expenditure during the first 
two quarters of 2019 -20 as submitted by the Ministry include previous year’s unspent 
balances with the Autonomous Bodies, procedural formalities and delay in capital 
works due to tendering issues. The Committee is not convinced by the reasons adduced 
by the Ministry for occurrence of shortfall in utilization of funds during the first two 
quarters of 2019 -20. The Committee is of the view that the Ministry should have an 
effective monitoring mechanism during the budget preparation stage itself so that the 
funds are fully utilized for the intended purpose within the monthly / qu arterly 
expenditure limits. The Committee also desires to be furnished with a factual note 
detailing the specific steps taken to resolve the issues concerning the unspent balances 
with the Autonomous Bodies, delay in appraisal of proposals by the Expert Co mmittee 
and the measures taken / proposed to be taken for sorting out tendering issues. 
(Para 1.3) 
Budget trends over the past years 
The Committee observes that cultural activities promote various economic activities, 
thereby giving employment to a large section of society and contributing to the GDP of 
the nation. Therefore, Culture should not be treated as a marginal sector . A large 
number of our monuments require urgent attention as they suffer due to lack of 
personnel and funds. The Committee recommend s that the Ministry should cite the 
trend of negligible growth in allocation to the Ministry during the last five years and 
justify the importance of more funds to the Ministry at the RE stage in order to carry 
out its mandate in an efficient manner.  
(Para 2.2) 
ANNUAL PLAN (2020-21) 
The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in Para 2.2  of Chapter III of this 
Report. The Committee also expects the Ministry to pay focussed attention for more 
efficient deployment of the available resources.  
(Para 3.2) 
 

43 
 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
The Committee appreciates that a provision has been made for booking tickets for 
multiple monuments in a single transaction . The Committee, however, reiterates its 
recommendation that the ASI should give tourists, the optio n to buy combined tickets 
or a city/region pass that is valid for a certain duration. The same would allow visitors 
to enter the different monuments present in close vicinity of each other without going 
through the hassle of the ticket purchasing process repeatedly.  
(Para 4.2) 
 
The Committee is of the view that boundary walls are a necessity for the preservation as 
well as clear demarcation of our ancient monuments . Therefore, the Committee 
reiterates its recommendation that a survey of all the monuments s hould be conducted 
to assess the urgency of the construction of boundary wall, along with the budgetary 
requirements for the same.  
(Para 5.3) 
 
NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF INDIA, NATIONAL LIBRARY AND CENTRAL 
REFERENCE LIBRARY 
The Committee is dismayed to note that the Grants Committee of NAI met only once 
during the last Financial Year and even then, the proceedings of the meeting could not 
be initiated. The Committee desires to know the reasons for which the revalidation of 
the schemes being run by the NAI has been pending and why the process for the same 
was not initiated sooner.  
(Para 6.4) 
 
NATIONAL MISSION ON LIBRARIES 
The Committee notes that the BE  in 2019-20 for National Mission on Libraries (under 
Development of Libraries) was Rs. 118.51 crore which was reduced drastically to Rs. 
0.73 crore; but nothing was spent. The reasons for the shortfall in utilization include 
non-submission of proposals by eleven State Governments, non -release of State share 
and non -receipt of claims from the State / UT Library authorities. It appears to the 
Committee that the budget allocations were made under this head without ascertaining 
the status/tenability of the acti vities under this project. The Committee is thus inclined 
to conclude that there is an urgent need to exercise greater due diligence in carrying out 
the budgetary exercise so that such irrational projections of funds are not repeated in 
the future and the practice of overestimation and under -utilization is curbed 
comprehensively.  
(Para 7.2) 

44 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF MUSEUMS 
The Committee feels that the reasons mentioned for slow pace of expenditure are 
routine in nature and could have been sorted out if the Ministry had effectively taken 
up the matter with the concerned State / UT authorities for timely clearances. The 
Committee desires to know the steps taken by the Ministry to ensure that these reasons 
do not cause slow pace of expenditure in the future.  
(Para 8.4) 
 
The Committee observes that merely stating that all museums have been requested to 
ensure the availability of free Wi-Fi facility is not sufficient. The Committee needs to be 
updated on the tangible progress made in this direction.  
(Para 9.2) 
 
The Committee had laid stress on the need on the part of the Ministry in ensuring the 
early completion of the project – “Museum on PMs of India” . But the Committee notes 
from the information furnished that due to the COVID -19 pandemic, this project is 
certain to witness time overrun. The Committee desires that a dedicated mechanism be 
put in place for coordination and completion of the project within shortest possible 
timeframe. Procedural or operational hurdles, if any, should be resolved expeditiously 
at the highest level of the Ministry. The Committee also urges the Ministry to expedite 
action with respect to item no. (ii) and (v) of Para 10.1. Special effort may be made 
especially for item (v) which is the core for the museum.  
(Para 10.3) 
 
CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES/PROJECTS 
The Committee is not at all convinced by the reasons given by the Ministry for slow 
pace of expenditure under this head . The Committee may be informed about what 
caused delays in convening of the Committee meeting under Museum Grant Scheme. As 
admitted by the Ministry, the slow pace of expenditure is the main reason for the severe 
cuts faced by the Ministry at RE stage. India is a resource -constrained country and in 
order to obtain the best possible outcomes, it is imperative that the budge ted funds are 
optimally utilized. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Ministry may take 
all possible corrective measures to ascertain that similar things are not repeated during 
the current FY.  
(Para 11.2)

witnessing inordinate delay . Rs. 150.01 crore allocated in BE 2019 -20 was reduced to 
Rs. 69.75 crore at RE 2019-20 stage; but the actual expenditure was even lesser than the 
reduced RE 2019-20 allocation, mainly on account of slow pace of construction activities 
by the executing agency. What is worrisome is that this trend is likely to continue in FY 
2020-21. Such persistent shortfall in the utilization of budgeted funds indicates fiscal 
indiscipline and laxity o n the part of the Ministry. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should take concrete steps for proper utilization of the 
funds budgeted for “Museum on PMs of India” and set up a Coordination Committee 
to oversee the implementation of this project as early as possible.

CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
 
DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2020-21) OF THE MINISTRY 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Ministry of Shipping which has drawn ambitious program for Port infrastructure 
development and capacity augmentation will become handicapped because of the budgetary 
cuts which will jeopardize the targeted outcomes. The Committee takes note of the fisc al 
constraints faced by Ministry of Finance due to moderation in economic growth and the 
impact of global slowdown. Still, while seeking a balance between public good and need for 
containing fiscal deficit, the Committee would advocate higher budgetary pro visions in 
favour of Sagarmala Scheme and Kolkata Port Trust at the RE 2020 -21 stage. The 
Committee recommends that when the growth momentum is revived and the additional 
resources become available as a result of revenue buoyancy, the allocation for the Mi nistry 
should be increased further.              (Para 7) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1. The recommendation of the C ommittee has been noted. Based on the expenditure 
trend, targets and absorptive capacity of the implementing agencies, additional fund 
requirement will be assessed from time to time and will be projected to the Ministry of 
Finance at appropriate stage. 
Recommendation/Observation  
2. The Committee observes that there is a huge gap between the projected demand and 
the sanctioned budget for the Ministry for the FY 2020 -21. As against the projected demand 
of Rs. 3328.70 crores, the Ministry has been provided with Rs. 1800.00 crores only. 
Obviously, such huge variation is suggestive of the shortcomings in the budgetary planning. 
The Committee would urge upon the Ministry to exercise due diligence in the budget 
formulation with proper planning and assessment, taking into account its needs an d the 
capacity to deliver the functions assigned to it.          (Para 8) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. As per the availability of 
funds, projects priorities will be re -defined and funds will be released accordingly after due 
assessment of all deliverables. 
PORT CAPACITY- ADDITION WORK 
Recommendation/Observation  

3 
 
3. The Committee observes that in Major Ports productivity in terms of ship turn-around 
time, waiting time and average output per ship berthday  continues to be modest when 
compared with global standards and performance of Ports in developed maritime countries. 
Since globalization, rapid adoption of technology and competitiveness are critical objectives 
to the exporters and importers in India, mod ernization of Major Ports is critical to the 
success of their supply chain objectives. It is in this context that, the capacity addition at five 
Ports, namely, Deendayal Port Trust, Mormugao Port Trust, V.O. Chidambaranar Port 
Trust, Cochin Port Trust and Visakhapatnam Port Trust assumes added significance. The 
Committee desires that the progress of implementation of these projects should be monitored 
regularly and that proper guidelines should be issued for their timely completion. The 
Committee also desir es to know whether traffic flows at the above Ports have shown any 
correlation with the GDP subsequent to the capacity addition during 2019-20.    (Para 20) 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1. The Ministry is regularly monitoring the progress o f Port modernization projects. In 
case of any deviations from the target date, suitable instructions/guide lines used to be issued 
to the P orts from time to time to streamline the same. Due to the various initiatives taken 
towards modernization of Major Por ts, the average Turn-round time, which was 87.36 hours 
during 2015-16, has come down to 61.75 hours  during 2019-20.  Like -wise, average output 
per ship berthday, which was 13156 tonnes during 2015-16, has increased to 16433 tonnes 
during 2019-20. 
3.2. Capacity available as on 31.03. 2019 and traffic handled at five Ports, namely  viz., 
Deendayal Port Trust, Mormugao Port Trust, V.O. Chidambaranar Port Trust, Cochin Port 
Trust and Visakhapatnam Port Trust, during 2018-19 and 2019-20,  are given as under:- 
 
Port

3.3. As may be seen from the above, there is no shortage of capacity in these 5 Ports.  If

to handle traffic for the next 7 -8 years in these ports.  As such, the traffic of P ort could not 
correlate with GDP. 
 
CARGO HANDLING CAPACITY 
Recommendation/Observation  

4 
 
4. The Committee also recommends that uneconomic practices coming in the way of 
efficient operations should be identified and reviewed to bring down the cost of cargo 
handling at the Major Ports.           (Para 28) 
Reply of the Ministry 
4.1. Due to various initiatives taken up under the aegis of ease of doing business and doing 
away with the cum bersome documentation process, P orts have already  moved towards 
paperless regime. Efforts have been made to increase DPE and DPD along with doing away 
with the manual formats. With the above efforts, the World Bank ranking on Ease of Doing 
Business has improved tremendously over the last few years. 
 
AVERAGE OUTPUT SHIP BERTHDAY 
Recommendation/Observation  
5. On comparison of the above figures of 2019 -20 with data of 2018 -19, it has been 
noticed that t here was improvement only in 6 P orts viz., Haldia , Visakhapatnam, Cochin, 
Mormugao, Mumbai and JNPT.  However, in Ports of Kolkata, Paradip, Kamarajar, 
Chennai, V.O. Chidambaranar, New Mangalore and Deendayal, the average Output Per 
Ship Berthday is even less than that of 2018 -19. The Committee desires t hat the Ministry 
should look into the reasons for the decrease in average Output Per Ship Berthday of 7 Ports 
mentioned above and take remedial measures.                   (Para 30) 
Reply of the Ministry 
5.1. The reasons for the decrease in average Output Per Ship Berthday and reme dial 
measures suggested by the Ports are given as under: 
Kolkata: 
(i) Decrease was primarily due to increase in percentage of Non -Working Time, 
which was owing to non-Port account reasons. 
(ii) Poor performance of the handling contractor i n terms of poor equipment 
availability with regard to MHC, RST and TT  led to decrease in average ship -day 
output of container vessels  which in turn affected the overall average Ship -day 
Output. 
(iii) Also, due to Covid -19 impact, both Container import and export generation were 
adversely affected leading to lower output. 
Remedial measures by Port: 
(a) Mechanization of 3 NSD Berth - Converting the berth from non -MHC berth 
(where geared vessels used to be handled) to MHC berth (where gearless vessels 
may be handled). 

5 
 
(b) Introduction of Fixed Window Berthing (FWB):  Two FWBs per week introduced 
w.e.f. 23.09.2019 and the third window became operational from 29.11.2019. 
Paradip: 
OSBD of Liquid Bulk Vessels has been reduced from 52119 MT to 50544 in 2019 -20, which 
has affected the Gross productivity of the Port.  The reduction in average parcel size of the 
vessels resulted in slow discharge rate of the Cargo and thus OSBD of POL is affected. 
Kamarajar: 
(i) At Coal Berth 1, the conveyor system connecting Coal berth and NCTPS stack  
yard is frequently got breakdown due to old age structures and also Belt damages. 
Due to this, the berth stay of the vessels has been increased considerably which in 
turn affects the berth productivity. 
(ii) At Coal Berth 2, the pipe conveyor system of NTECL r uns 4.4 Km along the 
coastline which is getting frequent breakdown. Due to the corrosion effects, the 
pipe conveyor gantries in the conveyor system need to be replaced and the same is 
carried out by NTECL. NTECL informed that it is expected to complete by 
September 2020. Due to this, the berth productivity of Coal Berth 2 has been 
reduced considerably. 
Remedial measures by Port: 
(a) KPL is continuously pursuing with TANGEDCO for the replacement of conveyor 
belts at NCTPS plant in order to improve the performance of Coal Berth 1. 
(b) KPL is continuously pursuing with NTECL for the completion of all the pipe 
conveyor gantry replacement works in order to improve the performance of Coal 
Berth 2 
Chennai: 
(i) Increased number of less productive Project Cargo vessels  & 
other General Cargo vessels; and 
(ii) Decreased number of high productive dry bulk cargoes like Limestone/Dolomite 
vessels and Container vessels  for the year 2019 -20 when compared to 2018 -19. 
The shortfall was only in dry bulk wherein, the output per ship berthday decreased 
due to less number  of limestone / dolomite vessels ( viz., 47 vessels during 2018 -
19 as against  13 vessels during 2019 -20) which are normally handled by mobile 
harbour cranes with higher productivity. 
Remedial measures by Port: 
(a) The increase in draft level to 14 metres at JD2 berth at  Chennai port has attracted 
a Limestone Vessel of all -time high of 76342MT and a Gypsum vessel of 61600 

6 
 
MT during the month of March 2020 and  more such vessels are anticipated 
regularly, which will increase the volume and hence the productivity. 
V.O. Chidambaranar: 
     Increase in less productive cargoes like Machinery, Wind Mill Blade and Project 
Cargoes by 44.64% from 57,412 tonnes in 20l8 -19 to 83.042 tonnes in 2019 -20. 
Also, there was increase in shifting of deep draft vessels from the only 
multipurpose deep draft mechanized berth (IX Berth) which affects the 
productivity. 
Remedial measures by Port: 
(i) Port has constructed NCBIII berth with a proposal to add one more deep draft 
berth to handle multipurpose cargo vessels. However, dredging proposal is 
pending for approval from the Ministry. On addition of one more deep draft berth, 
increase in shifting of deep draft vessels can be avoided which would avoid pre-
Berthing Detention, reduced TRT and improve o verall average output per ship 
berthday. 
(ii) Incentive/ Penalty based on berthing norms reviewed to improve the productivity 
of the vessels at Berth. 
New Mangalore: 
(i) Less Crude Oil Handling at the SBM facility.  Crude oil imports declined due to 
shut down of some units by MRPL during April, May, Augu st and September, 
2019 due to up gradation to Bharat  VI standards, water scarcity, l andslides and 
also three weeks of non -working days on account of cyclonic weather in the 
month of September, 2019. 
(ii) Lower Output of Semi-Mechanized Dry bulk cargo due to Weather Constraint.  In 
the year 2019 -20, the Monsoon extended till October, causing constraints on the 
handling of Dry Bulk cargo such as iron ore fines, coal, urea, limestone etc. which 
resulted in a lower average output per ship berthday.  
Remedial measures by Port: 
(i) The operationalization of the m echanized coal handling facility at berth n o. 16 
will ensure higher output for all types of coal cargo during 2020-21. 
(ii) The port is teaming up with the captive Clients such as MRPL to e nsure smooth 
operations in the year 2020 -21.  The port is in close coordination with the captive 
users to not only handle higher cargo but also to increase the performance of its 
operations.  
Deendayal: 

7 
 
(i) Owing to implementation of the barrier in height for cargo dumping & storage, the 
feeding of cargo from hook point to the storage point & vice-versa, has slowed 
down significantly and this has in turn affected (reduced) the unloading / loading 
rates and the per berthday output for dry cargoes, especially bulk cargoes like coal 
etc. 
(ii) Cyclone warning: The Non weather working day was issued for  4 days (from 11 th 
to 14th June, 2019) at Kandla and for 3 days at Vadinar. At Kandla, this affected 
the normal cargo handling operations for nearly 5 days. 
(iii) Impact of COVID 19 pandemic :  The gradual spread of pandemic and the impact 
on cargo handling operations on account of th e subsequent lockdown from 22 nd 
March, 2020. Also due to problems in adequate supply of labour  for cargo 
handling and for carrying out loading / unloading operations caused significant 
impact in decreasing the output of bulk cargoes handled at the port. 
 
MODERNIZATION OF PORTS 
Recommendation/Observation  
6. The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken for modernization of Minor Ports 
and recommends that specialized Minor Ports should also be developed as an integral part of 
the overall Port system.           (Para 42) 
Reply of the Ministry 
6.1. Recommendation from Committee has been noted. There ar e 71 projects worth Rs. 
15125 crores under Sagarmala Programme which are focused on modernizing Minor Ports of 
our country. The list broadl y includes special projects of u pgrading the existing 
infrastructure; development of new infrastructur e; and Ro-Ro jetties projects for Minor Ports 
in coastal States. 
 
CONNECTIVITY TO PORTS 
Recommendation/Observation  
7. The Committee desires to be updated on the progress made towards route 
rationalization for Visakhapatnam and Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) connectivity to 
Deendayal Port.            (Para 46) 
Reply of the Ministry 
7.1. Ministry of Shipping addressed Ministry of Railways for route rationalization of VPT. 
However, Ministry of Railways replied that they will not be able to provide route 
rationalization till completion of two rail lines i.e., Raipur Titlagarh railway line & doubling 
of Titlagarh – Sambhalpur line. 

8 
 
7.2. Regarding DFC connectivity to Deendayal Port, DPT has equipped themselves with 
DFC compliant yard and other necessary infrastructure whereas from Western Railways side, 
work is due starting with electrification of existing rail lines, etc. 
 
SAGARMALA  
Recommendation/Observation  
8. The Committee desires the Ministry to review the requirement of funds based on the 
progress under the ongoing project and newly sanctioned projects, and explore the 
possibility of getting budgetary assistance from the Ministry of Finance or Viability Gap 
Funding (VGP).           (Para 57) 
Reply of the Ministry

PERFORMANCE OF PORTS 
Recommendation/Observation  
7. The Committee observes that the parameters of Average Turn -around time and 
Average Output Per Ship Berthday  are not much in vogue in international Ports in terms of 
international best practices. One such parameter widely used internationally is “average 
moves per crane hour”. With the advent of full scale containerization of general cargo, Ports 
have witnessed paradigm shift in terms of commissioning of container terminals. The 
Committee would, therefore, like the Ministry to apply the yardstick of “Average moves per 
crane per hour” to measure the performance of the Major Ports. The Committee desires to be 
kept apprised in this regard.          (Para 36) 
Reply of the Ministry 
7.1. The Port p erformance cannot be assessed based on a single measure. A meaningful 
evaluation of a Port’s performance will require sets of measures relating to the duration of the 
ship’s s tay in port (t otal Turnaround Time in Port), the quality of the cargo handling 
mechanism and the quality of service to inland transport vehicles during their passage 
through the port. 
7.2. The average moves per crane hour are one of the yardsticks for meas uring crane’s 
ability to move the number of containers in an hour.  It is more suitable for Container 
handling ports. Whereas, the majority of Indian Major Ports are multi -commodity Ports 
handling around 75 -80% cargo comprising Liquid Bulk, Dry Bulk, Break -Bulk, etc.  The 
level of containerization in India is increasing but still below the level of leading international 
container handling Ports.   Some of the Major Ports like Kolkata, Haldia, Paradip, New 
Mangalore, Mormugao, Mumbai, etc. do not have a dedicated state -of-art container terminal 
at present.

Recommendation/Observation 
 16. The Committee takes note of the fact that the East Coast Canal in the Balasore 
district of Odisha has been declared as the NW-5 and the vast agricultural land on both sides 
of the canal depends on the drainage of water during heavy rain in the rainy season. During 
summer season, rabi crops used to be irrigated from this canal. Further, it notes that d ue to 
negligence of authorities, growth of wild shrubs and grass makes the little water available, 
poisonous and it dysfunctions the lift irrigation pumps during summers. They also act as a 
blockade for drainage of water during rainy season, making the are a marshy, waterlogged 
and breeding ground for snakes. Therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry should 
clean the canal from wild shrubs and let the water flow to and fro so that sufficient water is 
available for irrigation during the summer season . The Committee further recommends that 
water gates at Bhograi lock should be maintained and regular dredging of the canal should

Reply of the Ministry 

30 
 
16.1. IWAI undertakes development of National Waterways for shipping and navigation

and this was further evaluated for development of NW 5 on PPP mode by M/s Feedback Infra 
in March, 2016. The findings of this report on development of East Coast Canal (ECC) under 
NW-5 are as under:- 
(i) The canal portion of NW-5 runs from Charbatia lock to Geonkhali lock covering a

bridges, RCC bridges, Railway bridges, Foot bridges run across ECC with 
insufficient vertical clearance.
