Role of Tariff Regulations at India’s Major Ports 
Recommendation/Observation  
28. The Committee feels that the Port sector in India is facing certain tariff - related 
uncertainties due to multiplicity of regimes. The non -Major Ports do not come under any tariff 
jurisdiction and price their services based on market and competition. But the major ones 
(including private terminals therein) fall under the jurisdiction of a regulator viz, Tariff 
Authority for Major Ports (TAMP). This anomaly and the lack of a level playin g field have long 
been debated issue.                  (Para 227) 
Reply of the Ministry 
28.1 The Major Port Trusts and the BOT Terminals operating there were initially covered by 
the Tariff Guidelines of 2005. The Tariff Guidelines of 2005 did not provide flexibility to the 
Port Trusts and the BOT Terminals in pricing of their services. The Port Trusts and the BOT 
Terminals operating there have been taken out of the Tariff Guidelines of 2005 and now are 
covered under the Tariff Policy, 2018 (Major Port Trus ts) and the Tariff Guidelines, 2019 (BOT 
Terminals), which give them flexibility to price their services within their Annual Revenue 
Requirement. 
Further recommendation/observation: 
28.2 The Committee notes the reply. The Committee, however, desires to kno w whether 
tariff has been left entirely to the market forces or a norm based tariff is fixed by the 
regulator. 
Recommendation/Observation

provision of certain ta riff related uncertainties as ascertained by TAMP, the Committee 
recommends that the anomalies in the TAMP rules must be made reasonable in order to make it 
lucrative for ships to call on Major Ports against private ports. The Committee further 

59 
 
recommends that the role of the TAMP must be redefined and that a strategic and market 
oriented system of tariff must be set in place.                       (Para 229) 
Reply of the Ministry 
29.1 The Major Port Trusts and the BOT operating there were initially covered  by the Tariff 
Guidelines of 2005. The Tariff Guidelines of 2005 did not provide flexibility to the Port Trusts 
and the BOT Terminals in pricing of their services. The Port Trusts and the BOT Terminals 
operating threat have been taken out of the Tariff Gui delines of 2005 and now are covered under 
the Tariff Policy, 2018 (Major Port Trusts) and the Tariff Guidelines, 2019 (BOT Terminals), 
which give them flexibility to price their services within their Annual Revenue Requirement. 
29.2 Regarding redefining ro le of TAMP it is stated that steps have already been initiated by 
the Government in this direction. A Major Port Authorities Bill, 2016 was introduced in the Lok 
Sabha in December, 2016, inter -alia, envisaging setting up an Adjudicatory Board, which will 
carry out other than tariff setting functions of TAMP and will adjudicate and look into any

29.3 The Committee has also recommended that a strategic and market oriented  system of 
tariff must be set in place. In this regard, it is stated that the Traffic Policy, 2018 of Major Port 
Trusts and Tariff Guidelines of 2019 for BOT Terminals which were earlier governed by 2005

lucrative for more ships to call on Major Ports.

Lok Sabha in December 2016 but no further progress has been reported since then, which

provisions which are no longer required, are eliminated. The Committee desires to be kept

country, Ministry of Home Affairs has, at the request of Ministry of Shipping, exempted 
cruise tourists arriving with e -visa from the requirement of bio -metric enrolment for a 
period of three years i.e., till 31.12.2020 vide order dated 20th December, 2017.  This will 
facilitate expeditious immigration clearance of cruise passengers with e -visa   enabling 
them to spend more time on shore. 
v.  The port charges have been reduced and all Major Ports are to charge a uniform single 
rate of $0.35 per GRT for first 12 hrs of stay.   Ports will not charge any other rate like 
berth hire, port dues, pilotage, passenger fee etc from cruise liners.   The above rate has 
been made effective from 3 rd November, 2017 and will remain in force for a pe riod of 
three years. 
vi. Composite concession of 40% is given for domestic cruise vessels for calls between 75 -
100 in a year and composite concession of 50% is given for domestic cruise vessels for 
calls exceeding 100  in a year for a period of three years i.e., up to 3-11-2019. 
vii. The Ports do not levy any priority/ousting/shifting charges for berthing the cruise vessel. 
viii. Walk-in berthing/preferential berthing offered to Home Port cruise vessels without any 
extra charge. 
  x. To address manpower, coordination and logistic issues for handling cruise vessels at 
Ports, Port Level Committees with Chairman of the respective Major Port Trusts as 
Chairman, Secretary of Tourism of the concerned state as Vice -Chairman and Regional Director 
of the respective region of Ministry of Tourism as Convener have been constituted.

REPORT 
INTRODUCTION 
    Road Transport plays a critical role in the economic growth of any country. The 
necessity for the continued need for strengthening the road network in the country is 
underscored by the fact that the transport sector contributed abo ut 4.6 percent in the Gross 
Value Added (GVA) for F inancial Year 2018-19, of which the share of road transport was 
about 67 percent (Economic Survey 2020 -21, Volume -2). A robust, safe, well -maintained 
road network would be key for our country to overcome t he damaging impact of the 
Coronavirus pandemic on the national economy. 
2. The tasks and responsibilities of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
encompass, inter alia , construction and maintenance of National Highways (NHs); 
administration of the Nati onal Highways Act,  1956; National Highways Authority of India 
Act, 1988; National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008; 
Motor Vehicles Act 1988; and Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989, as also formulation of 
broad policies relating to road transport and automotive norms, besides making arrangements 
for movement of vehicular traffic with neighbouring countries. 
3. India has the second largest road network in the world of about 62.16 lakh km. This 
comprises National Highways, Expresswa ys, State Highways, Major District Roads, Other 
District Roads and Village Roads as under: 
National Highways 1,36,440 km 
State Highways 1,76,818 km 
Other Roads 59,02,539 km 
Total 62,15,797 km 
 
4. The associated offices under the Ministry of Road Transport  and Highways are as 
follows:  

2 
 
i. National Highways Authority of India (NHAI):   
Set up through an Act of Parliament in 1988, NHAI is responsible for the 
development, maintenance and management of the National Highways entrusted to it 
and for matters related or incidental there to. The NHAI became operational in 
February, 1995. 
ii. National Highways & Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd. (NHIDCL) : 
NHIDCL is a corporate entity under the Ministry, responsible for the construction/ up-
grading/widening of Natio nal Highways in parts of the country which share 
international boundaries with neighbouring countries in order to promote regional 
connectivity on a sustainable basis. 
iii. Indian Academy of Highway Engineers (IAHE):  
The Indian Academy of Highway Engineers (IA HE) is a registered Society under the 
administrative control of the Ministry. It is a collaborative body which was set up in 
the year 1983 with the objective of fulfilling the long felt need for training of 
Highway Engineers in the country, both at the ent ry level and during their service 
period. 
iv. Indian Road Congress (IRC):  
The IRC was formally registered as a Society on 24 th September 1937 under the 
Societies Registration Act of 1860 for periodical holding of road conferences to 
discuss issues related to road construction, maintenance & development.

ROAD DEVELOPMENT 
25. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been entrusted with the responsibility 
of development of Road Transport and Highways in general and construction & 
maintenance of National Highways (NHs) in particular. All roads other than National 
Highways in the states fall within the jurisdiction of respective State Governments. In 
order to assist the State Governments in the development of state roads, Central 
Government also provides financial assistance out of the Central Ro ad Fund (CRF) and 
Inter State Connectivity and Economic Importance (ISC & EI) scheme. Besides National 
Highways development Project (NHDP) & National Highway Inter -connectivity 
Improvement programme (NHIIP), Ministry is implementing SARDP -NE & LWE 
schemes which includes National Highways and State roads. The Ministry is also 
responsible for evolving standards and specifications for roads and bridges in the country 
besides acting as a repository of technical information on roads and bridges.

35. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the implementation of an

Quality Inspection 
60. Quality of the construction activities are being checked at site timely as per specifications 
of MoRTH by the Authority Engineer and by concerned Officers posted at Site and at the 
Regional Offices. Poor quality  work found (if any) is immediately rectified by the EPC 
contractor. NHAI has implemented a system for Quality inspection of NHAI projects 
during construction by engaging Retired Officials from State PWD, MoRTH, BRO etc. 
Suitable actions are also initiated  against defaulting Contractors/Consultants.In addition 
to that, a panel of Independent Special Project Monitors (SPMs) have been set up by 
NHIDCL and the SPMs have been engaged from time to time to check the quality of 
work at Site. 
61. A Quality Control Zone has also been created in the Ministry in September, 2020 headed 
by Chief Engineer with an objective that Quality Control Zone will work towards the 

24 
 
preparation of policy guidelines as well as examine and issue directions/suggestions for 
system improvement on Quality Assurance/Control for National Highway works as well 
as Centrally Sponsored Schemes among executive agencies of this Ministry. 
62.  Accordingly, Quality zone has issued detailed guidelines and Standard Operating 
Procedure for Quality Control/Assurance in construction of National Highways and other 
centrally sponsored projects vide circular dated 01.10.2020 in which it is delegated that 
Quality Control Zone may select any project of the Ministry/NHAI/NHIDCL/BRO on 
random basis to inspect the records/documents related to quality control/assurance & may 
also carry out certain tests in the presence of stakeholders to check the quality of the 
National Highways. Based on such inspection of Quality Control Zone, 
instructions/suggestions will be issued to th e PIUs/ PWD Divisions/ RO Offices for 
necessary compliance. 
63. In compliance to the above, Quality Control Zone has inspected 17 nos. of NHAI/PWD 
Projects in the States of Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and 
Jharkhand and have issued instructions/ suggestion to stakeholders. 
64. The Committee takes note of  the various initiatives taken by the Ministry/NHAI to 
ensure good quality in the road infrastructure projects. The Committee, however, 
feels that the existing quality of roads leave a lot to be desired and need more 
stringent quality check mechanisms to ensure high quality construction of roads 
across the country , with specific reference to levelings and smoothness, and also to 
ensure use of standardized and world -class equipment, technology and know-how to 
ensure relevant friction, sloping and gradient to allow rain water to flow out and 
side margin for road safety. In order to prevent road accidents due to drowsiness of 
drivers on long routes, rumble strips should be installed at appropria te places/road 
intersections.  
65. The Committee recommends that random checks for construction & material 
quality and the compliance of mandatory guidelines, may be made by NHAI for all 
its road projects, in addition to the checks made by the approving offici als. Any 
discrepancies/ deficiencies found in the same, should result in disciplinary action 
against the person/ agencies involved in preparing DPR, the concessionaire as well 
as the approving official. The Committee feels that connivance of the approving 

25 
 
authorities with the concessionaire might be the major cause of below par quality of 
construction in National Highways projects across the country. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Ministry may introduce necessary checks and 
balances in order to ensure that the approving authorities as well as the 
concessionaire are accountable for their work, till a stipulated period of time, even 
after the completion of the project.

117. The Ministry, in its written reply, informed the Committee that road accidents are 
occurring due to multiple ca uses such as over speeding, drunken driving/consumption of 
alcohol, driving on wrong side/lane indiscipline, fault of the driver of motor vehicle, use 
of mobile phones during driving, mechanical defect/fault of the vehicle defect in road 
condition, weather condition and lack of knowledge on road signage etc. These various 
factors can broadly be categorized into human error, road condition/environment and 
vehicular condition that lead to accidents on roads  
118. The Ministry has formulated a multi -pronged strateg y to address the issue of Road 
Safety based on Education, Engineering (both of roads and vehicles), Enforcement and 
Emergency Care. Accordingly, various initiatives have been taken by the Ministry as 
detailed below:-  
(i) Education:  
A.  The Ministry implemen ts a scheme for undertaking publicity measures and 
awareness campaigns on road safety to create awareness among road users 
through the electronic media, print media, NGOs etc.  
B. Observance of National Road Safety Week/Road Safety Month every year for 
spreading awareness and strengthening road safety.  
C. A Certification Course for Road Safety Auditors has been commenced in 
Indian Academy of Highway Engineers (IAHE).  
(ii) Engineering (both of Roads and vehicles)  
A.  Road engineering  
a) High priority to identificati on and rectification of black spots (accident 

42 
 
prone spots) on national highways.  
b) Road safety has been made an integral part of road design at planning 
stage.  
c) The threshold for four laning of National Highways has been reduced 
from 15,000 Passenger Car Units (PCUs) to 10,000 PCUs.  
d) Ministry has delegated powers to Regional Officers of MORTH for 
technical approval to the detailed estimates for rectification of identified 
Road Accident black spots.  
e) Guidelines for pedestrian facilities on National Highways f or persons 
with disabilities have also been issued to all States / UTs.  
B. Vehicle engineering:  
a) Safety standards for automobiles have been improved.  
b) Ministry has notified fitment of Speed Limiting devices on all transport 
vehicles  
c) Scheme for setting up on e model Inspection & Certification Centre in 
each State/UT with Central assistance for testing the fitness of vehicles 
through an automated system  
(iii) Enforcement

enforcement through use of technology and further provides for strict penalties 
for ensuring strict compliance and enhancing deterrence for violation of traffic 
rules.  
B. Rules for protection of Good Samaritans as per MV (Amendment) Act, 2019 
have been published.  
(iv) Emergency care:

snapshot regarding road accidents in the country to suggest  that although there is a 
consistent increase in the number of persons getting killed in road accidents, the 
number of road accidents taking place is witnessing a decrease. The Committee is 
apprehensive whether the trend  indicates a decrease in the reporting of road 
accidents across the country or the severity of the road accidents occurring in the 
country has increased over time. The Committee finds that a significant percentage 
of these deaths belongs to  working age individuals  which might be pushing the 
livelihood of many families at stake, causing serious financial trouble/ poverty . The 
Committee recommends the Ministry to target zero accidents on account of faults in 
road design and construction. The Ministry should take up identification and 
rectification of black spots on a war footing, across the country. The Committee 


44 
 
further recommends the Ministry to  conduct research and analyze into why these 
black spots existed in the road projects in the first place and how the same can be 
avoided from the DPR preparation stage itself in the upcoming projects of the 
Ministry. 
122. The Committee takes note of the 2021 World Bank Report titled “Traffic Crash 
Injuries and Disabilities: The Burden on Indian Society”  which st ates that India 
tops the world in road crash deaths, contributing to 11% of all road accident deaths 
worldwide, despite accounting for only 1% of the world’s vehicles. The 2019 World 
Bank Report “Guide for Road Safety Opportunities and Challenges: Low - and 
Middle-Income Countries Country Profiles” estimates the road crash and serious 
injury cost estimate at 7.5% of India’s GDP. The Committee is of the considered 
view that the observations made in World Bank Report should serve as a stark 
reminder of the gra vity of the situation and a sense of urgency with which the 
Ministry should flag Road Safety as top priority, right from  the DPR stage of a NH 
project. 
123. World Bank Report further highlights that  as high as 44% of the households in 
rural areas reported at least one death after a road crash, compared to 11.6% of the 
households in urban areas. Similarly, Low Income Households reported twice the 
number of deaths post-crash vis-à-vis High Income Households. The Committee feels 
that this striking difference might be because of the difference in the quality of 
medical care available to the victims of road accidents. The Committee recommends 
that the Ministry should work in close coordination with the Ministry of Health and 
Family Welfare, to ensure that free quality medical help is provided to road accident 
victims belonging to Low-Income Households. The Committee recommends that this 
may be partially funded by the penalties collected for the violation of traffic Rules. 
124. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may develop a Road Safety score 
to quantify the safety of the National Highways across the country. The ongoing 
projects of the Ministry may be granted approval only if they score excellent in 
terms of Road Safety. The Committee further recommends that the Min istry may 
prescribe a standard format of data to be collected by the concerned local 
authorities. The data thus obtained, may be tapped into in order to gain actionable 
insights into the factors causing road accidents. 

45 
 
125. The Committee recommends that the Min istry should promote the tollfree 
accident helpline number 1033 at toll booths and other suitable sites on the NHs, so 
as to spread awareness among road users as to how they can get help within the 
golden hour and potentially save the life of the accident victim.  
126. The Committee desires the Ministry to formulate  an Action Plan with 
quantifiable goals regarding the number of black spots to be identified and rectified; 
reduction of response time in case of accidents; reduction in the number of 
accidents; and deaths caused thereby, etc. 
127. The Committee takes note of reduction of 54% in deaths occurring due to road 
accidents in the State of Tamil Nadu in the last four years. Even if the data for the 
year 2020 is excluded from consideration on account of low vehicul ar traffic due to 
the COVID -19 pandemic, the Committee feels that the consistent decrease in the 
deaths caused due to road accidents, is commendable. The Committee lauds the 
efforts of the Government of Tamil Nadu and the concerned authorities in this 
regard. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may conduct extensive 
research into the methodologies adopted in Tamil Nadu regarding Road Safety and 
replicate the same across the country on an urgent basis.  
128. The Committee desires the Ministry  has to come u p with solutions to minimize 
the large number of accidents that take place due to merging of traffic from service 
lanes to the highway. Proper signage  in three languages viz., English, Hindi and 
regional language, may be ensured to alert the drivers at the  points where the road 
traffic gets merged with highways. The Ministry may look into the best international 
practices in terms of ensuring safety with regard to merging of traffic on the 
highways and incorporate the same in its road projects at the design stage itself. 
129. The Committee enquired from the Ministry about the present status of compliance of 
the directions of the Supreme Court of India dated 30 th November, 2017 and additional 
directions by the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety dated 26 th September, 2018, 
for improvement of Road Safety in the States/UTs. The Ministry, in its written reply, 
informed the Committee that all States/UTs have complied with some of the directions of 
the Hon’ble Supreme Court dated 30.11.2017 and the additional directio ns of the 
Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety dated 26.09.2018, whereas some State/UTs 
are in the process of complying with some of these directions. Compliance with the 

46 
 
remaining directions is a continuous process and requires regular monitoring. Statu s 
reports were submitted to the Hon’ble Supreme Court from time to time. In this regard, 
the Hon’ble Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety has continued holding regular 
meetings with State/UTs for ensuring better and complete compliance. The Committee is 
continuously following this up with rest of States/UTs for early compliance. The Ministry 
of Road Transport and Highways has notified “Member of Parliament’s Road Safety 
Committee” in each district of the country to promote awareness amongst road users, 
under the chairmanship of Hon’ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from the district. 
130. Some Members of the Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture, in its 
meeting held on 15 th February, 2021, noted that they had not been invited to any Road 
Safety meeting in their respective district. One Member further noted that he did not 
receive any response, despite bringing this fact to the notice of the Collector and the 
concerned authorities. 
131. The Committee notes that the  meetings of District Road Safety Co mmittees are 
barely held. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may keep track of the 
frequency of the meetings held by the District Road Safety Committees  and as part 
of the monitoring mechanism. Further, the Committee recommends that it should be 
strictly ensured that the Member of Parliament from the area is duly invited for the 
said meetings. The Committee further recommends that a Road Safety Committee 
should be constituted at the State level, comprising , inter alia , of representatives 
from the Mi nistry of Road Transport and Highways  and State Road Departments , 
Chief Secretary of the State and Members of Parliament belonging to the State , 
which may meet at least twice a year, to discuss the road safety issues in the State. 
132. The Committee sought to k now from the Ministry as to how the funds generated 
through payment of penalties for traffic offences are utilized at present. The Ministry, in 
its written reply, informed the Committee that implementation of the provisions of Motor 
Vehicles Act, 1988 and Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989 comes under the purview of 
State Government/ UTs and that the funds generated through payment of penalties are 
utilized by respective State Government/UTs. 
133. The Committee is of the view that the funds generated through paym ent of 
penalties for traffic offences should be utilized for the purpose of enhancing Road 
Safety across the country. The Committee finds that the largest number of deaths 

47 
 
due to road accidents, is on roads other than National Highways and State 
Highways. The Committee, would like the Ministry to urge the State Governments 
to follow certain Guidelines and Rules in the construction of roads and in the 
maintenance of roads, to ensure safety of road users, on roads other than National 
Highways and State Highwa ys also. The State/UT Governments may be encouraged 
to utilize the funds collected from the general public as penalty f or committing 
traffic offences towards a Road Safety Corpus to fund projects/activities that 
improve Road Safety in the respective State.   
134. The Committee takes note of the frequent road accidents that occur in 
mountainous areas and recommends that crash barriers , made of steel or bricks,  
should be made mandatory on all Highways in hilly areas. The Committee further 
recommends that the Minis try should ensure the installation of adequate signages 
and reflectors on roads in such areas.

138.  Taking cognizance of  the glacier burst at Utta rakhand that occurred on 7 th

urgent need for providing for helicopter landing facilities at ecologically sensitive

Committee stresses upon the need for close monitoring of ecological changes using 
the latest technology available, in order to prevent such natural disasters . In brief,

the Committee accentuates the necessity for a very close and effective coordination

4.3% of Annual Capital Outlay under Tribal Sub Plan (TSP) component, wherein specific 
NH/ road projects are being developed which are fully confined within one or more tribal 
districts. In such cases, development of NH corridors covering specific regions (i.e., tribal 
districts) are being taken up and these projects are not spilling over to other non -tribal 
districts. However, it is not feasible to adopt this approach for dedicated earmarking of 
funds under Scheduled Cast es Sub Plan (SCSP) component, as neither development of 
NHs nor earmarking of funds for NH projects is feasible to specifically benefit any 
specific category/ community. It is not feasible to develop NH projects in tune with 
specific beneficiary oriented s chemes. Accordingly, on number of occasions, through 
various correspondences, it was requested to NITI Aayog, Department of Economic 
Affairs and Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (M/o SJ&E) that the Ministry 
may be fully exempted from mandatory earmarking of funds under SCSP components.      
172.  The Department related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture also endorsed MoRT&H’s views for exemption from earmarking 

60 
 
funds under SCSP [Reference para 212 of 278 th Report on Demands for Grants (2020-21) 
of MoRT&H]. 
173.  NITI Aayog, in consultation with Ministry of Finance, had requested the M/o 
SJ&E to take the final decision on exception to any Ministry/ Department.  
174.  Hon’ble Minister (SJ&E) has approved a policy direction on 13.01.2021 that:- 
175.  “Any Department which has been allocated funds under Allocation for Welfare of the 
SCs under budget seeks exemption from the obligation of spending for SC welfare, they 
may be permitted only on condition that they surrender the allocated funds under 
Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC) from their budget to the 
Ministry of Finance”. 
176.  Above views of MoSJ&E with regard to surrender of funds under DAPSC 
from the budget of MoRT&H to Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) is not feasible . 
Ministry may be fully exempted from mandatory earmarking of funds under SCSP as it is 
not feasible for linear NHs projects. Further, Ministry is not in a position to surrender 
8.3% of outlay (i.e., about ₹ 8,000 crore) from its overall BE 2021-22 outlay of ₹1,18,101 
crore as these would constrain targets for construction of 12,000 km length of National 
Highways in 2021 -22 and compromise target market borrowing of ₹ 65,000 crore by 
NHAI under IEBR leading to delay in implementation of Major Flagship schemes such as 
Bharatmala Pariyojana (Phase-I) & other NH programmes. 
177.  Accordingly, Ministry may again reiterate the earlier stand requesting for full 
exemption of earmarking of mandatory funds under SCSP to MoSJ&E, DEA and NITI 
Aayog again. 
178. The Committee endor ses the views of the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways in this regard and recommends that the Ministry of Finance and Ministry 
of Social Justice and Empowerment may grant special exemption to MoRTH from 
earmarking a part of the allocated funds for SC  welfare. The Committee may be 
apprised about the response received in this regard from MoSJ&E, DEA and NITI 
Aayog.

stakeholders on issues related to Road, Travel & Hospitality sectors; and the officials of 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, NHAI, UT Government of Jammu & Kashmir 
on ‘Role of Highways in Nation Building’ with reference to the status of National 
Highways/ State Highways in Jammu and Kashmir.

focus on the maintenance of roads in the Jammu and Kashmir region, since the 
region needs good connectivity throughout t he year, from both economic as well as 
strategic viewpoint. A well -connected, well maintained road network would spur 
economic activities and further the tourism prospects of the region. The Commit tee,

Impact of vehicle overloading on National Highways 
181. During a meeting o f the Committee held on 7 th January, 2021 with various 
stakeholders on the subject ‘Role of Highways in Nation Building’, some of the Members 
of the Committee raised the issue of overloading trucks causing damage on roads which 
are not built to withstand such heavy loads. 
182. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may look into the significant 
impact of vehicle overloading on the condition of National Highways across the 
country. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may employ weigh -in-
motion system a t its toll booths across the country, to identify the extent of 
overloading by heavy vehicles, compared to the permitted load which may be 
obtained through FASTag data of the vehicle and impose suitable penalty 
automatically, so as to have a strong detrime ntal effect on truck owners. The 
Committee feels that this will tackle the possible connivance of RTO officials with 
the truck owners for allowing such overloading, and will help in better maintenance 
of National Highways. There should be a special check o n overloaded trucks, 
especially with reference to those transporting goods – stone chips and other 
minerals, causing damage to the roads. 
Setting up Dedicated Underground Utility Corridors 
183. In the meeting of the Committee held on 15 th February, 2021 on Exam ination of 

62 
 
Demands for Grants (2021 -22) of the Ministry, one of the Members raised the issue of 
frequent trenching of roads across the country for the purpose of Namami Gange project, 
laying of gas pipelines, optical fibers, telephone lines etc. He suggest ed the creation of 
utility corridors which can be utilized for such services to prevent frequent trenching of 
roads. He further suggested the monetization of the utility corridors through the creation 
of a company under the Ministry. 
184. The Committee is of th e view that roads across the country require frequent 
trenching for the purpose of laying of fiber lines, gas pipelines, and other similar 
amenities. The patchwork done thereafter is often delayed and rarely meets the 
desired construction quality, thus thw arting the speed of vehicles on the road and 
acting as a safety hazard. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may 
consider the inclusion of a provision for dedicated underground utility corridors in 
its upcoming National Highways projects to prevent f requent trenching.  The 
provision for construction of dedicated underground utility corridor should be 
included at the DPR stage itself.  The extra cost incurred for building the 
underground utility corridors may be replenished by monetizing the constructed 
utility corridors by charging the Departments and Companies which will benefit 
from avoidance of frequent trenching of roads. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry may create a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for the purpose of 
monetization of the utility corridors.

pandemic

Atmanirbhar Bharat, for providing relief to Contractors/ Devel opers/ Concessionaires of

development of roads in the country. The Committee further recommends that the

concessionaires, as well as to help the banks and lending organizations recover thei r

EXTERNALLY AIDED PROJECTS 
The Committee notes that the expenditure under Externally Aided Projects head is ₹ 
2487.85 crores, upto 31 st January, 2021, which is about 54% of the amount allocated 
under the head at B.E. 2020 -21 s tage. This slow pace of expenditure resulted into a 
substantial reduction at R.E. 2020 -21. The slow pace of utilization of funds under the 
EAP head thus cannot be fully accounted for by the problems the Ministry must have 
faced because of the Coronavirus p andemic restrictions. The Committee calls upon the 
Ministry to review the actual reasons behind this slow pace of utilization of funds and 
ensure that the reduced al location of ₹ 3750 crore for EAPs is optimally utilized during 

75 
 
the FY 2021-22. 
(Para 97) 
The Committee is happy to note that the World Bank funded National Highways 
Interconnectivity Improvement Project (NHIIP) is likely to be completed by 30 th June, 
2021, albeit with a delay of 9 months. The Committee may be apprised of the steps 
being taken by the Ministry to resolve the land acquisition issues being faced in the 
project. 
(Para 99) 
The Committee notes that land acquisition is a major bottleneck in Externa lly Aided 
Projects as well as other NH road projects in the country. The Committee desires the 
Ministry to look into the issue from a holistic perspective and consider suitable 
legislative changes to discourage the stakeholders from initiating litigations which 
contribute to not only increasing their cost but also causing immense trouble to the 
people living in the nearby regions. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may 
analyze the possibility of periodically sharing a part of the revenue generated f rom road 
infrastructure projects with those, whose land was acquired, since one of the core 
reasons behind the reluctance of the land -owners to willingly let go of their land is that 
the land is the source of livelihood for landowners and a one -time paymen t does not 
promise a regular livelihood to them, post acquisition of their land. 
(Para 100) 
SCHEMES OF UTs FINANCED FROM CRIF 
The Committee is anguished over the slow pace of utilization of funds under the 
Schemes of UTs financed from CRIF, across all Unio n Territories except Pondicherry. 
Poor pace of utilization of funds particularly in UTs does not augur well for their being 
under the direct control of Central Government. The Committee is especially concerned 
to note that upto 31 st January, 2021, funds re leased to Jammu and Kashmir are a mere 
17.3% of the amount allocated for the year 2020 -21. Similarly, the funds released to 
Ladakh are also just 27% of the amount allocated for the year 2020 -21. The Committee 
would like to be apprised of the reasons for th e nominal amount of funds released to 
these crucial, newly formed Union Territories, along with the steps taken by the 
Ministry to encourage higher utilization of funds in future. 
(Para 102) 

76 
 
DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING, QUALITY ASSURANCE, RESEARCH AND TRAINING 
– FINANCED FROM CRIF 
Low utilization of funds under the head ‘Development, Planning, Quality Assurance, 
Research and Training’ upto 31 st December, 2020 is a matter of serious concern. The 
Committee is pained to point out the failure of the Ministry to utili ze even the small 
allocation of ₹ 79 crore under this critical head.  
(Para 105) 
The Committee would like the Ministry to initiate and fund researches to gain insights 
into innovative road construction techniques, road safety issues and measures for both 
pedestrians and vehicle passengers, increasing longevity of roads across the varied 
landscape of the country, standards for road construction of international standards, 
tackling issues such as water-logging, etc. The insights gained by the Ministry from such 
studies and researches would be of immense value to the entire road transport sector in 
the country. 
(Para 106) 
The Committee notes that the budgetary, allocation for ‘Development, Planning, 
Quality Assurance, Research and Traini ng’ has dropped to ₹ 48.96 crore at B.E. 2021 -
22 stage as compared to ₹ 79 crore at R.E. 2020 -21. The Committee is not convinced by 
the reasons furnished by the Ministry for this decrease in allocation. The Committee 
deplores that the projected fund requir ement as well as the utilization by the Ministry, 
under this vital head, is minuscule and instead it should have been several times more 
than the present allocation, to help push the road infrastructure sector in the country in 
the right direction.  
(Para 109) 
RESEARCH, TRAINING, STUDIES AND OTHER ROAD SAFETY SCHEMES 
The Committee is concerned to note the sizeable reduction in the allocation made for 
Research, Training, Studies and Other Road Safety Schemes at R.E. 2020 -21 stage. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry may look into the quantum of funds utilized 
by developed countries across the world, for the purpose of research, training and road 
safety, factor in the statistical input of road accidents and arrive upon the realistic 
budgetary requirement actually needed under this head against such worrisome road 
safety situation in the country.  
(Para 112) 

77 
 
The Committee is of the considered view that the North -Eastern Region is very 
important to the country from the point of view of strategic security a nd development 
perspective. Road infrastructure projects in the region pose unique challenges, owing to 
the ecologically delicate, mountainous terrain which receives very heavy rainfall. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry to allocate funds for carr ying out research in 
the field of construction techniques specific to the region, which can withstand the 
heavy rainfall in harmony with the environment.  
(Para 113) 
The Committee takes serious note of the budgetary shortfall being faced by the Indian 
Roads Congress and feels that the same reflects the apathy of the Ministry towards 
research and development in the road sector of the country. The Committee is of the 
view that the research programmes carried out by Indian Roads Congress are of critical 
importance to make it possible for the Ministry to execute high quality road projects 
and improve the state of Road Safety in the country. The Committee, would like the 
Ministry to provide budgetary support needed by the IRC to carry out research 
programmes in collaboration with the leading Universities/ Research Institutions in the 
country, as well as abroad. 
(Para 115) 
The Committee recommends the Ministry to make dedicated efforts to seek CSR funds 
for the development of driving training institutes across the country, for capacity 
building of the vehicle drivers who are often found lacking in proper driving training 
and are unaware of traffic laws. The Ministry should plan the development of a driving 
training institute in every district of the country. 
(Para 116) 
Road Safety 
The Committee takes note of the various initiatives taken/being taken by the Ministry to 
address the issue of road safety in the country. The statistics give a snapshot regarding 
road accidents in the country to suggest that although there is a consistent increase in 
the number of persons getting killed in road accidents, the number of road accidents 
taking place is witnessing a decrease. The Committee is apprehensive whether the trend 
indicates a decrease in the reporting of road accidents across the country or the severity 
of the road accidents occurring in the country has increased over time. The Committee 

78 
 
finds that a  significant percentage of these deaths belongs to working age individuals 
which might be pushing the livelihood of many fa milies at stake, causing serious 
financial trouble/ poverty. The Committee recommends the Ministry to target zero 
accidents on account of faults in road design and construction. The Ministry should 
take up identification and rectification of black spots on  a war footing, across the 
country. The Committee further recommends the Ministry to conduct research and 
analyze into why these black spots existed in the road projects in the first place and how 
the same can be avoided from the DPR preparation stage itself in the upcoming projects 
of the Ministry. 
(Para 121) 
The Committee takes note of the 2021 World Bank Report titled “Traffic Crash 
Injuries and Disabilities: The Burden on Indian Society”  which states that India tops 
the world in road crash deaths, contributing to 11% of all road accident deaths 
worldwide, despite accounting for only 1% of the world’s veh icles. The 2019 World 
Bank Report “Guide for Road Safety Opportunities and Challenges: Low - and Middle-
Income Countries Country Profiles” estimates the road crash and serious injury cost 
estimate at 7.5% of India’s GDP. The Committee is of the considered v iew that the 
observations made in World Bank Report should serve as a stark reminder of the 
gravity of the situation and a sense of urgency with which the Ministry should flag Road 
Safety as top priority, right from the DPR stage of a NH project. 
(Para 122) 
World Bank Report further highlights that as high as 44% of the households in rural 
areas reported at least one death after a road crash, compared to 11.6% of the 
households in urban areas. Similarly, Low Income Households reported twice the 
number of de aths post -crash vis-à-vis High Income Households. The Committee feels 
that this striking difference might be because of the difference in the quality of medical 
care available to the victims of road accidents. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry sho uld work in close coordination with the Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare, to ensure that free quality medical help is provided to road accident victims 
belonging to Low -Income Households. The Committee recommends that this may be 
partially funded by the penalties collected for the violation of traffic Rules. 
(Para 123) 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry may develop a Road Safety score to 

79 
 
quantify the safety of the National Highways across the country. The ongoing projects 
of the Ministry may be  granted approval only if they score excellent in terms of Road 
Safety. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may prescribe a standard 
format of data to be collected by the concerned local authorities. The data thus 
obtained, may be tapped int o in order to gain actionable insights into the factors 
causing road accidents. 
(Para 124) 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should promote the tollfree accident 
helpline number 1033 at toll booths and other suitable sites on the NHs, so as to spr ead 
awareness among road users as to how they can get help within the golden hour and 
potentially save the life of the accident victim.  
(Para 125) 
The Committee desires the Ministry to formulate an Action Plan with quantifiable goals 
regarding the number of black spots to be identified and rectified; reduction of response 
time in case of accidents; reduction in the number of accidents; and deaths caused 
thereby, etc. 
(Para 126) 
The Committee takes note of reduction of 54% in deaths occurring due to road 
accidents in the State of Tamil Nadu in the last four years. Even if the data for the year 
2020 is excluded from consideration on account of low vehicular traffic due to the 
COVID-19 pandemic, the Committee feels that the consistent decrease in the deaths 
caused due to road accidents, is commendable. The Committee lauds the efforts of the 
Government of Tamil Nadu and the concerned authorities in this regard. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry may conduct extensive research into the 
methodologies adopt ed in Tamil Nadu regarding Road Safety and replicate the same 
across the country on an urgent basis.  
(Para 127) 
The Committee desires the Ministry has to come up with solutions to minimize the large 
number of accidents that take place due to merging of tr affic from service lanes to the 
highway. Proper signage in three languages viz., English, Hindi and regional language, 
may be ensured to alert the drivers at the points where the road traffic gets merged with 
highways. The Ministry may look into the best i nternational practices in terms of 

80 
 
ensuring safety with regard to merging of traffic on the highways and incorporate the 
same in its road projects at the design stage itself. 
(Para 128) 
The Committee notes that the meetings of District Road Safety Committe es are barely 
held. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may keep track of the frequency of 
the meetings held by the District Road Safety Committees and as part of the monitoring 
mechanism. Further, the Committee recommends that it should be strictly  ensured that 
the Member of Parliament from the area is duly invited for the said meetings. The 
Committee further recommends that a Road Safety Committee should be constituted at 
the State level, comprising, inter alia , of representatives from the Ministry  of Road 
Transport and Highways and State Road Departments, Chief Secretary of the State and 
Members of Parliament belonging to the State, which may meet at least twice a year, to 
discuss the road safety issues in the State.   
(Para 131) 
The Committee is of the view that the funds generated through payment of penalties for 
traffic offences should be utilized for the purpose of enhancing Road Safety across the 
country. The Committee finds that the largest number of deaths due to road accidents, 
is on roads o ther than National Highways and State Highways. The Committee, would 
like the Ministry to urge the State Governments to follow certain Guidelines and Rules 
in the construction of roads and in the maintenance of roads, to ensure safety of road 
users, on roa ds other than National Highways and State Highways also. The State/UT 
Governments may be encouraged to utilize the funds collected from the general public 
as penalty for committing traffic offences towards a Road Safety Corpus to fund 
projects/activities that improve Road Safety in the respective State.   
(Para 133) 
The Committee takes note of the frequent road accidents that occur in mountainous 
areas and recommends that crash barriers, made of steel or bricks, should be made 
mandatory on all Highways in h illy areas. The Committee further recommends that the 
Ministry should ensure the installation of adequate signages and reflectors on roads in 
such areas. 
(Para 134) 
Core Group on Safety and Security 

81 
 
In this regard, the Committee would like to make the foll owing recommendations to be 
added to the mandate of Core Group on Safety and Security for better outcomes:  
 
i. The Core Group on Safety and Security should ensure necessary coordination 
between NHAI/Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and Ministry of 
Railways in order to identify sketches/pockets of land, along National 
Highways and Railway tracks to facilitate emergency landing of helicopter 
ambulance in the event of accidents/natural calamities and should be a part of 
the DPR in new road projects. 
ii. In orde r to further strengthen the Core Group, a Sub -Committee may be 
formed in the Ministry of (i) Railways; (ii) Road Transport & Highways; (iii) 
Ports, Shipping & Waterways; and (iv) Civil Aviation. 
iii. The Sub-Committees mentioned at point (ii) should be headed b y an officer 
not below the rank of Joint Secretary. 
iv. The Sub -Committees given at point (ii) should employ, within two months, 
the services of consultants who are experts in the respective fields and who 
have the requisite global exposure and good reputation  for the services 
rendered by them. 
v. The above stated Sub -Committees should mandatorily report to the Core 
Group on Safety and Security, on a monthly basis. The Core Group should 
review and monitor the activities of these Sub-Committees. 
vi. Another issue which  is of urgent importance in the context of safety is the 
identification of black spots in highways and roads and quick action for their 
rectification. It should be ensured that Chief Engineers of the respective road 
projects should be made Members of this Sub-Committee. The Ministry of 
Road Transport & Highways/NHAI should  accord top priority to such 
rectification and furnish monthly progress to the above cited Sub -Committee 
of Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.  
vii.  Ministry of Road Transport & Highways/ NHAI should furnish to the Sub -
Committee referred to at point (ii), the data regarding the number of 
accidents which took place in 2019 and 2020, category wise, along with the 
time gap between such accidents & reasons for the same; and the remedies 
undertaken/proposed to be undertaken. The updation of data should 
invariably be done periodically.  

82 
 
(Para 136) 
The Committee further takes note of the fact that the 'Supreme Court Committee on 
Road Safety' was constituted in April 2014. The Committee would like t he Core Group 
on Safety and Security to work in tandem with the Supreme Court Committee to 
address the issues related to Road Safety. 
(Para 137) 
Taking cognizance of the glacier burst at Uttarakhand that occurred on 7 th February, 
2021 which led to loss of precious lives, the Committee underlines the urgent need for 
providing for helicopter landing facilities at ecologically sensitive areas, in order to 
ensure effective disaster management operations. For such facilitation, the Core Group 
should actively eng age with NDRF also regularly. The Committee stresses upon the 
need for close monitoring of ecological changes using the latest technology available, in 
order to prevent such natural disasters. In brief, the Committee accentuates the 
necessity for a very cl ose and effective coordination among all the related 
Ministries/Departments/Organisations and entities. 
(Para 138) 
CHAR DHAM PARIYOJANA 
The Committee notes the delays being faced in the Char Dham Pariyojana on account 
of the litigations in the National Gre en Tribunal and Supreme Court. Keeping in view 
the fact that the regions covered under the Char Dham Pariyojana are ecologically 
sensitive in nature, the Committee recommends the Ministry to exercise due caution, 
diligence and care, while executing the rem aining stretches of the project and make 
sincere efforts to minimize its adverse impact, if any, on the environment and ecological 
balance. 
(Para 141) 
SCHEME ON WOMEN SAFETY ON PUBLIC ROAD TRANSPORT 
The Committee is distressed to note that substantial redu ction of funds under the 
Scheme on ‘Women Safety on Public Road Transport’ from B.E. 2020-21 allocation of ₹ 
174 crores to R.E. 2020 -21 allocation of ₹ 140 crores. For the Financial Year 2021 -22, 
the amount allocated under this head has been further decreased to ₹ 100 crores. The 
Committee feels that the decreasing  allocation under the head, alongwith the meagre 
utilization of ₹ 62.402 crores till 31 st January, 2021 reflects the lack of sense of urgency 

83 
 
towards the safety of women. The Committee is of the strong view that the issu e of 
women safety has to be addressed proactively, in order to increase the participation of 
women in the workforce. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry 
should ensure optimum utilization of the funds under the head and also encourage 
better participation of State Governments, to ensure the same. The Committee observes 
that this allocation needs to be substantially increased in future, in order to protect the 
dignity of women in the country.  
(Para 146) 
MISCELLANEOUS 
Motor Vehicle Aggregators Guidelines, 2020 
Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) 
The Committee welcomes and appreciates the above mentioned new initiatives of the 
Ministry. 
(Para 149) 
Strengthening the Public Transport System in the States/UTs 
The Committee observe s that the number of ‘Passenger/km Performed’ as per the 
combined physical performance of 56 State Road Transport Undertakings data has 
decreased from 55,91,694 crores in 2016 -17 to 55,84,156 crores in 2018 -19. This data, 
coupled with increasing population of the country every year, suggests that the share of 
public transport as a mode of transport, is witnessing a constant decrease. The 
Committee feels that the decrease in the share of public transport translates into traffic 
jams, higher environmental pol lution as well as increased fuel consumption per capita. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to encourage maximum utilization 
of funds under the “Strengthening ITS in Public Transport System” scheme and come 
up with more schemes for bolsterin g the public transport system across the country, so 
as to encourage more passengers to take up public transport. 
(Para 153) 
Promotion of usage of environment friendly vehicles 
The Committee takes note of the steps being taken by the Ministry to promote th e usage 
of environment friendly vehicles in India. However, the Committee strongly feels that 
the same may not be enough to achieve the pace of adoption of such vehicles needed in 
the country, to tackle the damaging effect of petroleum based vehicles. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry may pilot a legislation, in coordination with the 

84 
 
concerned Ministries, to facilitate faster manufacturing and adoption of electric vehicles 
across the country. While piloting such a legislation, the Ministry may look  into the 
feasibility of making it mandatory for the vehicle manufacturers, to manufacture a 
certain minimum percentage of their vehicles, as vehicles powered by electricity or 
other clean energy sources with low emission. The draft legislation may also co nsider 
mandating electric vehicle manufacturers to utilize a certain part of their profits in 
setting up electric vehicle charging infrastructure across the country.  
(Para 155) 
The Committee reiterates the recommendation that it made in para 34.2 of Chapt er III 
of its 285 th Report on “Action Taken by the Government on the 
Recommendations/Observations of the Committee contained in its 278 th Report of the 
Committee on Demands for Grants (2020 -21) of Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways”, underlining the need of a lucrative Electric Vehicle Policy.  
(Para 156) 
  Multi-Member Consultative Committee  
The Committee recommends that a  strong Research & Development wing may be 
formed with the collaborative efforts of the Ministries that are a part of the MMCC, to  
evolve new, cost-efficient ways in the country, for shifting to environment friendly fuels. 
The Research & Development wing should look into region -specific strategies, to 
identify the best possible alternatives for conventional fuel, depending upon the 
availability of natural resources in the region . A detailed study of the strategies adopted 
by the most carbon efficient countries for switching to environment friendly fuels in 
their country may be undertaken by the Ministry. The suitability of the same in  the 
Indian context may be looked into and global best practices may be incorporated, after 
suitable modifications. 
(Para 158) 
The Committee feels that Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and environmental 
clearances are often thought of as impediments, by the public, to the various 
infrastructure projects of the Ministries. The Committee recommends, in this regard, 
that the Ministry should explore ways and means to bring about a change in mindset of 
the public, by creating greater awareness on such issue s, and that the officials must be 
held accountable for the adverse environmental impact of the projects, if any, being 
proposed and undertaken by them. The MMCC may look into the existing mechanism 

85 
 
for coordination of the Ministries comprising the MMCC, wi th the Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change and suggest necessary changes in the same. 
(Para 159) 
The Committee further recommends that the MMCC may come up with budgetary 
requirements for the promotion of environment friendly fuel, carrying out the necessary 
R&D, providing subsidies to the common man as well as to the industries for such 
adoption, and submit the same to the Ministry of Finance. The MMCC may devise a 
quantifiable Action Plan to promote the manufacturing and purchase of electri c 
vehicles in the country, along with the creation of necessary infrastructure such as 
charging stations, battery manufacturing and disposal etc.  
(Para 160) 
The Committee takes cognizance of the fact that although norms regarding emissions 
for automobiles, railways, aircrafts, ships, power plants and industries exist on paper, 
they are not implemented in letter and spirit. The Committee recommends that a 
concrete plan to efficiently and regularly monitor such emissions across the different 
industries shoul d be chalked out. Checks may be put in place to ensure that large 
companies do not circumvent the testing methodologies of the concerned bodies, 
through the use of software and such, similar to the incidents that were widely reported 
in the media in the re cent past. The MMCC may also pursue the timely review of the 
emission norms specified by the various Ministries as well as the monitoring and 
enforcement strategies for the same, and take necessary remedial measures, promptly. 
(Para 161) 
 
Policy Framework for Electric Vehicles and Autonomous Vehicles 
In order to permit Indian vehicle manufacturers to keep pace with the vehicle 
manufacturers around the world and keeping in mind the positive effects of 
autonomous vehicles on Road Safety through features such as autonomous emergency 
braking, the Committee recommends that the Ministry should analyze the policy 
framework for autonomous vehicles which is already in effect in several countries 
around the world and develop a comprehensive policy framework of its own  to govern 
the testing and commercial operation of autonomous vehicles in the country.   
(Para 163) 

86 
 
Accountability of Road Contractors, Consultants and Approving Authorities 
The Committee takes note of the Policy Circular issued by NHAI on 8 th January, 2021 
to decide penal action on the contractor, in case of failure of structures/highways in 
NHAI projects. The Committee recommends that NHAI may reconsider the upper limit 
of penalty since a sanction of ₹ 10 crore might not have the desired detrimental effect on 
the road contractors, in case of large road projects to the tune of hundreds of crores of 
rupees. 
(Para 167) 
The Committee desires to be apprised of the accountability of the consultants who 
prepare the Detailed Project Report for any given project of  the Ministry. The 
Committee is of the view that many of the issues faced in the execution of road projects 
across the country are due to lack of due diligence at the time of preparation of DPR of 
the road project. The Committee, therefore, recommends that  the Ministry may come 
up with Rules, to fix the accountability of the personnel responsible for drafting the 
Detailed Project Report, till a stipulated period of time, after the completion of the 
project, for construction of poor quality roads and also to  devise a mechanism for 
broader consultation with public representatives and other stakeholders, prior to 
finalization and should be vetted in the District Development (DISHA) Committees 
headed by the respective Member of Parliament.  
(Para 168) 
Check barriers on National Highways  
The Committee feels that the Policy of the Ministry to not permit erection of check 
barriers on National Highways needs better implementation, since the presence of check 
barriers on NHs is almost ubiquitous across the country. T he Committee may be 
apprised of the steps taken by the Ministry to ensure the implementation of this Policy 
of the Ministry in its true spirit, so as to prevent frequent occurrence of traffic jams 
because of the check barriers.  
(Para 170) 
Exemption from earmarking funds for Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SCSP) Component 
The Committee endorses the views of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in 
this regard and recommends that the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Social Justice 
and Empowerment may grant special exemption to MoRTH from earmarking a part of 
the allocated funds for SC welfare. The Committee may be apprised about the response 

87 
 
received in this regard from MoSJ&E, DEA and NITI Aayog. 
(Para 178) 
Special Focus on Maintenance of National Highways in Jammu and Kashmir Region 
The Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry must place special focus on 
the maintenance of roads in the Jammu and Kashmir region, since the region needs 
good connectivity throughout the year, from both economic as well as strategic 
viewpoint. A well -connected, well maintained road network would spur economic 
activities and further the tourism prospects of the region. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends the Ministry to ensure sufficient budgetary provisions for this purpose and 
in case any shortage is felt in this regard, the same may be communicated to the 
Ministry of Finance at the Revised Estimates (2021-22) stage. 
(Para 180) 
Impact of vehicle overloading on National Highways 
The Committee recommends that the M inistry may look into the significant impact of 
vehicle overloa ding on the condition of National Highways across the country. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry may employ weigh -in-motion system at its 
toll booths across the country, to identify the extent of overloading by heavy vehicles, 
compared to the perm itted load which may be obtained through FASTag data of the 
vehicle and impose suitable penalty automatically, so as to have a strong detrimental 
effect on truck owners. The Committee feels that this will tackle the possible connivance 
of RTO officials wit h the truck owners for allowing such overloading, and will help in 
better maintenance of National Highways. There should be a special check on 
overloaded trucks, especially with reference to those transporting goods – stone chips 
and other minerals, causing damage to the roads.  
(Para 182) 
Setting up Dedicated Underground Utility Corridors 
The Committee is of the view that roads across the country require frequent trenching 
for the purpose of laying of fiber lines, gas pipelines, and other similar amenities . The 
patchwork done thereafter is often delayed and rarely meets the desired construction 
quality, thus thwarting the speed of vehicles on the road and acting as a safety hazard. 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry may consider the inclusion of a provision 
for dedicated underground utility corridors in its upcoming National Highways projects 

88 
 
to prevent frequent trenching. The provision for construction of dedicated underground 
utility corridor should be included at the DPR stage itself. The extra co st incurred for 
building the underground utility corridors may be replenished by monetizing the 
constructed utility corridors by charging the Departments and Companies which will 
benefit from avoidance of frequent trenching of roads. The Committee recommen ds 
that the Ministry may create a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for the purpose of 
monetization of the utility corridors. 
 (Para 184) 
 
Measures taken to provide relief to stakeholders from adverse impact of Coronavirus 
pandemic 
The Committee appreciates th e steps taken by the Ministry to provide relief to the 
contractors, concessionaires and developers of road sector from the adverse impacts of 
the Coronavirus pandemic restrictions during the Financial Year 2020 -21. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministr y may continue to work closely with various 
stakeholders in the road sector to ensure the desired pace of development of roads in the 
country. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may devise strategies to 
infuse liquidity into road contractor s and concessionaires, as well as to help the banks 
and lending organizations recover their loans by timely completion of delayed/stuck 
projects. 
(Para 186) 
Loss of toll revenue on account of construction of parallel roads  
The Committee recommends that the Ministry may work in coordination with the State 
Governments and ensure that roads are not constructed parallel to National Highways 
as far as possible, since the same have a damaging impact on the toll collection from the 
NHs, thereby affecting their viability.  
(Para 187) 
Preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for National Highway projects 
The Committee recommends that DPRs of National Highways road projects should 
have provisions for right of way and service roads. The DPRs should be prepared a fter 
public consultation and inputs from Members of Parliament of the area. The 
Committee further recommends that provisions for public amenities such as dhabas, 

89 
 
washroom facilities etc. should be included at the DPR stage of NH projects.  
(Para 189) 
Status of in-principle approved road projects in Rajasthan 
The Committee desires to be apprised of the status of those National Highway projects 
in the State of Rajasthan which have been stuck for years despite in-principle approval.  
(Para 191)

13. At the outset, the Chairman welcomed the Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways and other senior officials to the meeting. The Chairman, inter alia, requested the 
Secretary to make a presentation on the Demands for Grants (2021 -22) with respect to the 
performance of the Ministry in 2020-21 and the budgetary allocations made to the Ministry in 
Budget Estimates 2021-22. 
14. The Secretary made a detailed presentation on the salient features of the Demands for 
Grants (2021-22). He informed the Committee that the Ministry had projected a demand of ₹ 
1,40,234/- crores, whereas, the Ministry of Finance has allocated only ₹ 1,18,101/ - crores at 
the B.E. stage in 2021 -22. He further apprised the Committee that the Ministry has spent ₹ 
74,286/- crores (till 31 st January, 2021) against the allocated Revised Estimates of ₹ 
1,01,823/- crores for the year 2020-21. He also highlighted that National Highways Authority 
of India (NHAI) has raised a total of ₹ 41,435/- crores through Internal & External Budgetary 
(IEBR) sources in the Financial Year 2020 -21, till 31 st January, 2021 and that NHAI would 
be authorized to raise ₹ 65,000/- crores for 2021-22.  
15. Elaborating the physical achievements, the Secretary stated that the length of National 
Highways (NHs) has been increased from 91,287 km (as on April, 2014) to 1,36,521 km at 
present whereas a total length of 1,76,797 km and 59,02,539 km has been constructed on 
State Highways and Other Roads respectively, as on date. He informed the Committee that 
the fund allocation for development of NHs has increased by a rate of about 27% since F.Y. 
2014-15 and stands at ₹ 1,73,000 crores approximately (including IEBR), for FY 2021-22. 
16. The Secretary elucidated upon the fact that during 2020 -21 (as of January,  2021) 
under the ‘Bharatmala Pariyojna’, a length of 2,517 km highways has been awarded, out of 
which, 2,273 km highways have been constructed. He also narrated that for the National

Highway (Original) Scheme, an amount of ₹ 34,581/ - crores and ₹ 40,651/ - crores has been 
allocated in Revised Estimates 2020-21 and Budget Estimates 2021-22, respectively.  
17. The Secretary apprised the Committee about the private sector participation/ 
investments, wherein NHAI has revised the Model Concession Agreement (MCA) for Build-
Operate-Transfer (BOT) Toll; Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM); and Toll -Operate-Transfer 
(TOT) and has raised ₹9,755 crores from the private sector during 2020 -21 (upto January, 
2021) as against a target of ₹ 26,400/ - crores for the year FY21. He furth er established that 
NHAI is working towards Asset Monetization, through the implementation of Infrastructure 
Investment Trusts (InvIT) mechanism, for which, the board of the Investment Manager has 
been constituted and five operational roads have been identified to be transferred to InvIT. 
18. The Secretary briefed the Committee regarding the status of Expressways wherein, a 
stretch of 237 km has been completed before the Bharatmala Pariyojana; 1,344 km is under 
implementation; and 1,045 kms is at pre -construction stage. He underlined that to incentivize 
vehicle owners to scrap their old vehicles, the Ministry is formulating a voluntary vehicle 
scrapping policy under which 15 -year-old commercial vehicles and 20 -year-old personal 
vehicles will be covered & States will be encouraged to impose Green Tax. He also informed 
the Committee that the fitness testing Rules and scrapping centre Rules will be notified, and 
that the policy will boost investments to the tunes of ₹ 10,000 crores and will create 35,000 
job opportunities, once fully operationalized.  
19. The Secretary apprised the Committee regarding the significant achievements and 
reforms of the Ministry, wherein he informed that certain Flagship Projects viz., Agra-Etawah 
(6-laning) and Gwalior -Jhansi (North-South Corridor) have been completed whereas certain 
other Flagship Projects have been initiated in the ongoing Financial Year viz., Delhi -
Vadodara and Ambala -Kotputli; that in e -Tolling, around 2.31 crores FASTags have been 
issued and the Electronic Toll C ollection (ETC) penetration has reached 76%; and that the 
Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2020 were issued on 27 th November, 2020 under the 
Motor Vehicle Amendment Act, 2020.

REPORT 
 
 
I. BRIEF BACKGROUND 
 
 
1. Tourism plays a key role in socio-economic progress through employment 
generation, creation of infrastructure and revenue earnings. Not only does the tourism sector  
spearhead growth, it also  improves the quality of people’ s lives with its capacity to create  
large scale employment of diverse kind. It supports environmental protection, champions  
diverse cultural heritage and strengthens peace in the world. 
 
 
2. Ministry of Tourism  is the nodal agency to formulate  national policies and  
programmes for the development and promotion of tourism. In the process, the Ministry  
consults and collaborates with other stakeholders in the sector including various Central  
Ministries/ Agencies, State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations and the 
representatives of the private sector. 
 
 
3. Secretary (Tourism)  is the executive  chief of the Ministry.  The Directorate 
General of Tourism has 20 Domestic field offices and an Indian Institute of Skiing and  
Mountaineering within the country and 08 overseas offices. The overseas offices promote  
Indian tourism in the markets abroad. 
 
 
4. The domestic field offices also play a vital role for promotion of tourism sector  
in the country. They are also involved in monitoring th e progress of implementation of  
projects sanctioned by the Ministry to the State Governments/Union Territories. 
 
 
5. India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) is the only public sector 
undertaking under the charge of the Ministry of Tourism. 
 
 
6. The Ministry also has the following autonomous institutions: 
 
 
i. Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management (IITTM) 
ii. National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology (NCHMCT); and the 
Institutes of Hotel Management (IHMs). 
iii. Indian Culinary Institute (ICI). 

2  
Role and Functions of the Ministry of Tourism 
 
 
7. The Ministry has the following main functions: 
 
 
1) All policy matters including: 
a. Development Policies 
b. Incentives 
c. External Assistance 
d. Manpower Development 
e. Promotion & Marketing 
f. Investment Facilitation 
g. Growth Strategies 
2) Planning 
3) Co-ordination with other Ministries, Departments, States/Union Territory Administrations. 
4) Regulation: 
a. Standards 
b. Guidelines 
5) Infrastructure & Product Development: 
a. Central Assistance 
b. Distribution of Tourism Products 
6) Research, Analysis, Monitoring and Evaluation 
7) International Co-operation and External Assistance: 
a. International Bodies 
b. Bilateral Agreements 
c. External Assistance 
d. Foreign Technical Collaboration 
8) Legislation and Parliamentary Work 
9) Establishment Matters 
10) Overall Review of the Functioning of the Field Offices 
11) Vigilance Matters 
12) Official Language: Implementation of Official Language Policy 
13) VIP References 

3  
14) Budget Co-ordination and Related Matters 
15) Plan Co-ordination 
16) Overseas Marketing (OM) Work 
17) Welfare, Grievances and Protocol 
 
 
In addition to above, the Ministry has also the following functions: 
 
 
1) Assistance in the formulation of policies by providing feedback from the field offices 
2) Monitoring of plan projects and assisting in the plan formulation 
3) Coordinating the activities of the field offices and their supervision 
4) Regulation: 
a. Approval and classification of hotels, restaurants, Incredible India Bed & Breakfast (IIB&B) 
units 
b. Approval of Travel Agents, Tour Operators and Tourist Transport Operators, etc. 
5) Inspection & Quality Control: 
a. Guide service 
b. Complaints and redressal 
6) Infrastructure Development: 
a. Release of incentives 
b. Tourist facilitation and information 
c. Conventions & Conferences 
7) Human Resource Development: 
a. Developing HRD Institutions 
b. Setting standards and guidelines 
8) Publicity & Marketing: 
a. Policy 
b. Strategies 
c. Coordination 
d. Supervision 
e. Promotion & Marketing 
f. Hospitality programmes 
9) Parliamentary Work 

4  
10) Establishment Matters of Ministry of Tourism 
 
 
8. As per the information furnished in the Annual Report of the Ministry, the  
activities of this Ministry revolves around promoting internal tourism, i.e. both inbound and  
domestic tourism, in India. This is necessary in order to harness the dire ct and multiplier  
effect of tourism on employment and poverty eradication in the country. The other major  
objectives of the Ministry pertain to projec ting the country as a 365 days tourist destination, 
promoting tourism in a sustainable manner by active pa rticipation of all segments of the  
society, assuring quality standards amongst tourism service providers, etc. Apart from these,  
the focus is also on integrated development of tourism infrastructure and facilities through  
effective partnership with various stakeholders. 
 
 
9. Immense economic benefits flow into the economy of the country through growth  
of tourism. As per e stimation in accordance with 3 rd TSA for 2013 -14, 2014 -15, 2016 -17,

reduced drastically.  On the infrastructural Schemes also, construction activities could not
